### Expected behavior

With fill: 'stack', each dataset's area stays filled on every frame, including frames of an animated chart.update().

### Current behavior

Consider an animated update of a stacked area chart that moves points horizontally, for example because the
y-axis tick labels change width. Right when the transition looks finished, every band above the first dataset
disappears. The bands then reappear one by one in dataset order over the next few frames.

The same happens without animation: if a dataset's point `x` differs from the dataset below it by a tiny non-zero
amount (≤ 1e-6 px), that dataset's entire fill is not drawn.

### Reproducible sample

https://jsfiddle.net/pmswbfot/

### Optional extra steps/info to reproduce

Deterministic, no animation (Chart.js 4.5.1):

```js
const chart = new Chart(canvas, {
  type: 'line',
  data: {
    labels: ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e'],
    datasets: [
      { data: [1, 2, 1, 2, 1], fill: 'stack', backgroundColor: 'rgba(0, 0, 255, 0.5)', pointRadius: 0 },
      { data: [1, 1, 1, 1, 1], fill: 'stack', backgroundColor: 'rgba(255, 128, 0, 0.5)', pointRadius: 0 },
    ],
  },
  options: { animation: false, scales: { y: { stacked: true } } },
});

chart.getDatasetMeta(1).data[2].x += 1e-9;
chart.draw(); // the orange band (dataset 1) is gone completely
// nudging by 1e-3 instead of 1e-9 does not trigger it
```

Animated reproduction in the jsfiddle, which is the same as my real-world use case that found the bug. Switching in the jsfiddle between absolute and relative representation causes the animation to flicker.

### Possible solution

Minimal fix in `findPoint`. The matched points are the same point within the epsilon, so taking the first is
safe. The complete patch, with a regression test, is [chartjs-upstream-fix.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32850352/chartjs-upstream-fix.patch):

```diff
-import {_isBetween} from '../../helpers/index.js';
+import {_isBetween, isArray} from '../../helpers/index.js';
 ...
 function findPoint(line, sourcePoint, property) {
-  const point = line.interpolate(sourcePoint, property);
+  // interpolate() returns one point per matching segment (typed `undefined | Point | Point[]`).
+  // A value within the _isBetween epsilon of a vertex (but not equal to it) matches both
+  // adjacent segments, so it returns (practically) the same point twice.
+  let point = /** @type {PointElement|PointElement[]|undefined} */ (line.interpolate(sourcePoint, property));
+  if (isArray(point)) {
+    point = point[0];
+  }
   if (!point) {
     return {};
   }
```

The JSDoc cast is needed because `LineElement.interpolate`'s JSDoc says `@returns {PointElement|undefined}`,
while the public typing in `src/types/index.d.ts` already says `undefined | Point | Point[]`. Correcting the JSDoc
instead would also flag `interpolatedLineTo` in `filler.drawing.js`. That function has the same array blind spot,
and it is harmless today only because `ctx.lineTo(undefined, undefined)` is a no-op.

**Regression test** (added to `test/specs/plugin.filler.tests.js`). It uses the deterministic sample above for
`delta` = `1e-9` and `-1e-9`: render with `fill: 'stack'`, shift `getDatasetMeta(1).data[2].x` by `delta`, call
`chart.draw()`, and assert that the pixel in the middle of dataset 1's band is painted (`[255, 0, 0, 255]`).

| | v4.5.1 | master (6a86e23) |
|---|---|---|
| New test, without the fix | 2 FAILED (pixel is `[0, 0, 0, 0]`), 75 passed | 2 FAILED, 76 passed |
| New test + fix | 77/77 passed | 78/78 passed |
| Full suite + fix | 1686/1686 passed | not run |

Control: with `delta` = `0` or `1e-3` the same assertion passes without the fix, so the test detects exactly the
sub-epsilon case. Also clean with the patch applied: `eslint` on the changed files and `tsc -p tsconfig.json`
(checkJs). Run with Karma in headless Chromium 141 (`--browsers ChromeHeadless`).

With the fix applied to the 4.5.1 build, the animated repro also shows 0 frames with a missing band.

A more thorough fix would make `_boundSegment` use the same tolerance for its start/stop decisions as for
`inside`, so that a single-value bound never yields two overlapping sub-segments. That touches shared segment
code, though.

### Context

Seen in production with vue-chartjs 5.3.4. Its setDatasets update keeps dataset object identity (Object.assign onto the existing dataset), so the update is animated from the current state. The workaround we use is fill: 'origin' on dataset 0 and fill: '-1' on the rest, with scales.y.stacked: true. At rest it renders pixel-identical to 'stack' for a single stack group without null gaps.

### chart.js version

4.5.1

### Browser name and version

Chrome, Firefox, Headless Chromium via Playwright

body_text:
With a horizontal legend and `align: 'end'`, the last item is sometimes not drawn,
depending on chart width and font metrics. Its hit box is still there, so clicking the
empty spot toggles the dataset.

Repro (label widths stubbed so it doesn't depend on fonts):
https://gistpreview.github.io/?51eab27b3af93f9a67b12b85f39cce7e
(code: https://gist.github.com/xpuu/51eab27b3af93f9a67b12b85f39cce7e)
Only "Alpha" is drawn, "Beta" gets fillText with x = NaN.

We only saw it on Windows machines, not on Linux. Display scaling snaps the canvas to
device pixels and the fonts measure differently there, so which widths fail differs
per machine.

Cause: `_draw` starts the row at `right - lineWidths[0]`, then checks each item with
`x + width + padding > this.right`. For the last item both sides are equal, so float
rounding decides it. When it rounds up, the item moves to `cursor.line + 1`,
`lineWidths[1]` is undefined, x becomes NaN and nothing is painted.

Possible fix: a small tolerance in that check, e.g.
`x + width + padding > this.right + 1e-6`.

Other

### 🐛 Bug Description

Hi,

I'm currently trying to integrate Claude/Anthropic into Nextchat (setup via Docker on Almalinux). I thought it's a trivial exercise of just entering some configuration data, but after two days, I'm about to give up.

After overcoming several obstacles, I'm stuck at a "model not found" error with models that clearly exist. 

{
  "error": {
    "message": "The model `claude-sonnet-5-5` does not exist or you do not have access to it.",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "param": null,
    "code": "model_not_found"
  }
}

Troubleshooting with the Anthropic chatbot:

	 curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages \
	 -H "x-api-key: YOUR_KEY" \
	 -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
	 -H "content-type: application/json" \
	 -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","max_tokens":10,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hi"}]}' 
	 If that works but Nextchat doesn't, the problem is in Nextchat's configuration or how it constructs requests. (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors)

The result:

{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg6kV95af4UdPzjpqhjXp","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Hi there! How can I help you"}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"max_tokens","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":11,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":0,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":10,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null}

So since the model ID works perfectly with the Anthropic API directly, it seems like the issue is on Nextchat's side: how it's formatting requests, which headers it's sending, or possibly an outdated API version string. 

### 📷 Recurrence Steps

Launch Docker (in this case, via Wireguard):

docker run -d \
  --name nextchat \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  -p 10.8.0.1:3000:3000 \
  -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="<VALID_KEY>" \
  -e CUSTOM_MODELS="-all,+claude-sonnet-5-5" \
  yidadaa/chatgpt-next-web:latest
  
Configure Custom API via Nexchat Client configuration
- Anthropic
- https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages [or leave blank or just https://api.anthropic.com - doesn't matter]
- Insert key
- Model name: -all,+claude-sonnet-5-5 [also tried tons of different ones here, this one was tested and confirmed via CURL]

Try to chat. See error.

### 🚦 Expected Behavior

Since the model is valid, Claude should respond.

### 📝 Additional Information

Went for this several times, for hours and hours, with and without the help of AI, but couldn't find the needle in the haystack (and I don't think it exists). Filing this as a bug now.

body_text:
## Summary

`requestOpenai()` in `app/api/common.ts` enforces `CUSTOM_MODELS` / `DISABLE_GPT4` with `isModelNotavailableInServer(customModels, jsonBody.model, [OpenAI, Azure, ...])` — the server-side check added in #5883. For Azure the upstream URL is built from the request path, `/api/azure/deployments/<dep>/...`, and Azure bills `<dep>`; it ignores the body `model`. A request whose body names an allowed model and whose path names another deployment passes the check, and is then forwarded with `AZURE_API_KEY`, which `auth()` injects for any path containing `azure/deployments`. Verified on v2.16.1 (tag commit 557a2cce), built from source; `app/api/common.ts`, `app/api/auth.ts` and `app/utils/model.ts` are byte-identical on `main` 839a24d.

## Impact

- Entry point: `POST /api/azure/deployments/{deployment}/chat/completions`.
- Requires only the shared access code (`CODE`), the normal user role. With `HIDE_USER_API_KEY=1` users cannot bring their own key, so the operator's key is used.
- Usage is billed on any deployment in the same Azure resource that the operator excluded (GPT-4, o1, …). The attacker has to know or guess the deployment name; default model names are the obvious guesses.

## Reproduction

Azure was replaced by a local mock that routes and bills by path deployment and logs every request to `/data/hits.jsonl`.

Config: `CODE=cage-access-code-2026`, `HIDE_USER_API_KEY=1`, `CUSTOM_MODELS=-all,+gpt-4o-mini@Azure=gpt4o-mini-dep`, `DISABLE_GPT4=1`.

1. Honest request for gpt-4 (`/deployments/gpt-4/...`, body `model: gpt-4`): `403 you are not allowed to use gpt-4 model`.
2. Bypass (`/deployments/gpt-4/...`, body `model: gpt-4o-mini`): 3 of 3 return `200`.
3. Mock ledger: gpt-4 billed lines go from 0 to 3, $0 to $0.27, each with `api-key` = `AZURE_API_KEY` and `body_model` = `gpt-4o-mini`.
4. With the fix: 3 of 3 return `403`, the ledger stays 0 → 0, and the allowed deployment still returns 200.

The same result was reproduced from the chat UI by modifying a captured request: gpt-4 billed lines went from 3 to 4 unpatched and stayed 0 → 0 patched (HTTP 403).

The check and the mismatch (`app/api/common.ts`):

```ts
isModelNotavailableInServer(customModels, jsonBody.model, [OpenAI, Azure, ...])
// Azure bills the deployment in the URL path, not jsonBody.model
```

## Suggested fix

On the Azure branch with `customModels` set, check the deployment from the path (`path.split("/")[1]`) against the model table and return 403 when it is not available, before the `{deploy-id}` forward-compatibility rewrite. Happy to re-test a candidate fix.

- Entry point: `POST /api/azure/deployments/{deployment}/chat/completions`.
- Requires only the shared access code (`CODE`), the normal user role. With `HIDE_USER_API_KEY=1` users cannot bring their own key, so the operator's key is used.
- Usage is billed on any deployment in the same Azure resource that the operator excluded (GPT-4, o1, …). The attacker has to know or guess the deployment name; default model names are the obvious guesses.

On the Azure branch with `customModels` set, check the deployment from the path (`path.split("/")[1]`) against the model table and return 403 when it is not available, before the `{deploy-id}` forward-compatibility rewrite. body_text:
### Summary
Spotless formatting tool fails locally but CI doesn't detect the issues. Similar to the PMD problem (#18479), there's inconsistency between local and CI environments.

### Details
After recent CI configuration changes, Spotless is not properly failing the build in CI when formatting issues are found locally. This suggests either:
1. Spotless is not running in CI
2. Spotless configuration differs between local and CI
3. CI is configured to ignore Spotless failures

### Expected Behavior
- Spotless should run successfully both locally and in CI
- CI should fail when Spotless detects formatting violations
- Local and CI behavior should be consistent
- Developers should get immediate feedback about formatting issues

### Current Behavior
- Spotless fails when running locally (`./mvnw spotless:check`)
- CI pipeline continues without detecting the Spotless failures
- Inconsistent behavior between local development and CI environments

### Impact
- Code formatting inconsistencies may reach the repository
- Developers waste time debugging formatting issues that CI should catch
- Inconsistent code style across the codebase
- Reduced effectiveness of automated formatting tools

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Run locally: `./mvnw spotless:check`
2. Observe formatting violations (if any)
3. Push changes to CI
4. CI passes even though local check failed

### Configuration Check Needed
Verify:
- Spotless is included in CI pipeline
- Spotless configuration is identical in local and CI
- CI properly fails on Spotless violations
- No `-DskipSpotless` or similar flags in CI configuration

### Related Issues
- #18479 - PMD Tool Fails Locally but CI Doesn't Detect It
- Recent CI configuration changes may have affected both tools

### Notes
Similar to the PMD issue, this suggests a configuration discrepancy. Need to ensure:
1. Spotless runs in CI with same parameters as local
2. CI correctly interprets Spotless exit codes
3. No silent skipping of Spotless in CI workflow

body_text:
This issue is the main tracker for integrating support for **Compact Source Files and Instance Main Methods** (Java 25, JEP 512) into Checkstyle. 

**Status of grammar support:** implemented in #17810. Adds the `COMPACT_COMPILATION_UNIT` token and the `compactMemberDeclaration` rule. When a file declares any top-level method or field, the grammar emits `COMPACT_COMPILATION_UNIT` as the AST root in place of `COMPILATION_UNIT`

---

## 1.1 Review of Java Enhancement Proposals (JEPs)

**JEP timeline:** [JEP 445](https://openjdk.org/jeps/445) preview (Java 21), [JEP 463](https://openjdk.org/jeps/463) second preview (Java 22), [JEP 477](https://openjdk.org/jeps/477) third preview (Java 23), [JEP 495](https://openjdk.org/jeps/495) fourth preview (Java 24), [JEP 512](https://openjdk.org/jeps/512) final (Java 25).

**What the JEP introduces.** A Java source file may consist of top-level methods and fields with no enclosing class declaration. The compiler wraps the file's members in an implicit class that is always `final` and resides in the unnamed package; the file cannot declare a package. The feature also makes an instance `void main()` (no `public`, no `static`, no parameters) a valid program entry point.

```java
String greeting = "Hello";

void main() {
    System.out.println(greeting);
}
```

**AST structure under the implemented grammar:**

```
COMPACT_COMPILATION_UNIT          (root, replaces COMPILATION_UNIT for compact files)
|--IMPORT
|--VARIABLE_DEF
|--CLASS_DEF                      (nested types are siblings of methods and fields)
`--METHOD_DEF
```

**Problems the JEP creates for existing checks:**

1. Top-level members have no enclosing `CLASS_DEF` or `OBJBLOCK`. Every check that walks `getParent()` to find a class, or guards on `parent == OBJBLOCK`, must be reviewed. This drives §1.2.
2. Instance `void main()` is now a valid entry point. `UncommentedMainCheck` currently insists on `public static` and silently misses the new form. This drives a child issue in §1.2.
3. The unnamed package is mandatory. `PackageDeclarationCheck` will fire "Missing package declaration" on every compact file with no way to fix it.
4. The implicit class is always `final`. `RedundantModifierCheck` should flag `final` on its top-level methods.

---

## 1.2 Similar and Related Tokens

### Method

Candidate impacted checks were identified by:

```bash
checks=src/main/java/com/puppycrawl/tools/checkstyle/checks
{
  grep -rl "OBJBLOCK"  $checks
  grep -rl "CLASS_DEF" $checks
  grep -rl "COMPILATION_UNIT"   $checks
} | sed "s|^$checks/||" | sort -u

```

Each candidate was then run via the Checkstyle CLI against a minimal compact source file mirroring the scenarios in the audit (top-level field plus `void main()`, with the specific construct each check needs to trigger) and against a sanity-check file with the same members inside a normal class. 

### 2a. NPE Crashes (11, verified still crashing)

| Check | Verified behaviour | Child Issue |
|---|---|---|
| `RequireThisCheck` | Throws `NullPointerException` (`frame is null`); no `CLASS_FRAME` is pushed for the implicit class | #19972 |
| `FinalLocalVariableCheck` | Throws `NullPointerException` (`Deque.peek()` null); scope-stack underflow with no `OBJBLOCK` pushed | #19973 |
| `MethodNameCheck` | Throws `NullPointerException` (`classDefOrNew is null`) on any top-level method | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20210 |
| `MissingOverrideCheck` (`javaFiveCompatibility=true`) | Throws `NullPointerException` (`defOrNew is null`) on a top-level method whose Javadoc contains `@inheritDoc` | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20212 |
| `UnusedLocalVariableCheck` | Throws `NullPointerException` (`grandParent is null`) when a top-level field is present | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20213 |
| `MissingOverrideOnRecordAccessorCheck` | Throws `NullPointerException` (`grandParent is null`) on a top-level record accessor | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20214 |
| `EmptyLineSeparatorCheck` | Throws `NullPointerException` (`getParent() is null`) in `isTypeField` on a compact file with adjacent top-level members | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20215 |
| `MagicNumberCheck` (`ignoreFieldDeclaration=true`) | Throws `NullPointerException` (`getParent() is null`) in `isFieldDeclaration` on a top-level numeric literal | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20216 |
| `ModifiedControlVariableCheck` | Throws `NullPointerException` (`Deque.contains` on null `currentVariables`); scope-stack underflow with no `OBJBLOCK` pushed when a `for` loop appears in a top-level method | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20267 |
| `FinalClassCheck` | Throws `NullPointerException` (`Deque.peek()` null in `typeDeclarations`) on a top-level anonymous class declaration in a compact file; no `CLASS_DEF` ancestor pushes onto the stack when the anonymous class's outer type is the implicit class | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20523 |
| `AbbreviationAsWordInNameCheck` | Throws `NullPointerException` (`astParent2` null in `isInterfaceDeclaration`) on a top-level field whose name contains an abbreviation; `variableDefAst.getParent().getParent()` overshoots `COMPACT_COMPILATION_UNIT` to null | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20524 |


### 2b. False Positives (5, all verified)

| Check | Verified behaviour | Child Issue |
|---|---|---|
| `PackageDeclarationCheck` | Fires "Missing package declaration" on every compact file. Compact files must be in the unnamed package, so the violation is unfixable | #19908 |
| `OuterTypeFilenameCheck` | Fires "type.file.mismatch" on a named nested class. That class is a member of the implicit class, not the outer type | #19909 |
| `InvalidJavadocPositionCheck` | Fires "Javadoc comment is placed in the wrong location" on correctly-placed Javadoc before top-level fields and methods. Field and method detection requires `OBJBLOCK` ancestry, which does not exist in compact files | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20217 |
| `OuterTypeNumberCheck` | Counts every `CLASS_DEF` child of `COMPACT_COMPILATION_UNIT` as an outer type, so a compact file with two top-level classes is flagged "Outer types defined is 2". Identical classes inside an ordinary outer class produce zero violations | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20268 |
| `UnnecessarySemicolonAfterOuterTypeDeclarationCheck` | Fires on `} ;` after a nested class in a compact file. The class is a member of the implicit class, not an outer type | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20269 |

### 2c. False Negatives (17, all verified)

Each input that should fire produces zero violations. 

| Check | Symptom on compact file | Child Issue |
|---|---|---|
| `MissingJavadocMethodCheck` | Top-level public method without Javadoc not flagged | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20218 |
| `AnnotationLocationCheck` | Annotation on a top-level variable not flagged | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20219 |
| `UncommentedMainCheck` | Instance `void main()` not flagged | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20220 |
| `JavadocMethodCheck` | Wrong `@param` on a top-level method not flagged | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20221 |
| `HiddenFieldCheck` | Parameter shadowing a top-level field not flagged | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20222 |
| `DeclarationOrderCheck` | Field after method not flagged | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20223 |
| `JavadocStyleCheck` | Missing first-sentence period on a top-level member not flagged | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20224 |
| `MethodCountCheck` | Top-level methods not counted toward `maxTotal`, `maxPublic`, etc. | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20225 |
| `RedundantModifierCheck` | `final` on a top-level method not flagged, though the implicit class is always final | #20226 |
| `RedundantModifierCheck` | `public` on a top-level method not flagged, though the implicit class is final and in the unnamed package, so `public` cannot widen access to anything | #20266 |
| `ClassMemberImpliedModifierCheck` | Nested enum or interface missing implied `static` not flagged | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20227 |
| `OverloadMethodsDeclarationOrderCheck` | Split top-level overloads not flagged | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20228 |
| `VisibilityModifierCheck` | Non-private top-level fields not flagged. `isAnonymousClassVariable` uses `parent != OBJBLOCK` as a proxy for "anonymous-class field" and excludes every top-level field in a compact file | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20270 |
| `UnnecessarySemicolonAfterTypeMemberDeclarationCheck` | Trailing `;` after a nested-type declaration that is a child of `COMPACT_COMPILATION_UNIT` not flagged; the check guards on `parent == OBJBLOCK` | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20271 |
| `ClassFanOutComplexityCheck` | Fan-out of the implicit class is not measured; the check registers for `CLASS_DEF`/`INTERFACE_DEF`/etc. and never starts because there is no top-level `CLASS_DEF` for the implicit class | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20553 |
| `CovariantEqualsCheck` | Covariant `equals` method declared at the top level of a compact source file is not flagged; the check walks bodies of `CLASS_DEF`/`ENUM_DEF`/`RECORD_DEF`/`LITERAL_NEW` and the implicit class has none of those tokens | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20552 |
| `WriteTagCheck` | The first top-level method's `@tag` values are not reported; any leading block comment at the top of the file (copyright header, xdocs inline-config header, etc.) attaches to that method's `TYPE` node in compact form and is misread as its Javadoc | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20555 |

### Verified clean, no change required

The implemented grammar gives top-level members a non-null parent (`COMPACT_COMPILATION_UNIT`), which fixes one of the originally audited NPEs:

---

## 1.3 Frequently Impacted Checks

| Check | Verified behaviour on compact source files | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `IllegalToken` | Accepts all token types via `TokenUtil.getAllTokenIds()`; default tokens (`LABELED_STAT` only) are unaffected. Users can opt into `COMPACT_COMPILATION_UNIT` if desired. | No change required |
| `IllegalTokenText` | Operates only on literals, identifiers, and comments. JEP 512 introduces no new text-bearing tokens. | No change required |
| `IndentationCheck` | Correctly tracks indent context for top-level methods (verified: an over-indented body inside `void main()` is flagged with the expected level). No crash, correct violation. | No change required |
| Whitespace family: `EmptyLineSeparatorCheck` | See §2a (NPE) | NPE, child issue listed above |
| Whitespace family: `NoLineWrapCheck` | Operates on `PACKAGE_DEF` and `IMPORT` only. Compact files cannot declare a package and imports remain unchanged structurally. No crash on tested inputs. | No change required |
| Whitespace family: `NoWhitespaceAfter`, `MethodParamPad`, `ParenPad`, `GenericWhitespace` | Not structurally relevant: compact source files contain no new operator or punctuation patterns these checks target. | No change required |

---

## 1.5 Review of Other Static Analysis Tools

| Tool | What it ships for JEP 512 |
|---|---|
| **IntelliJ IDEA** | Recognises instance `void main()` as a valid entry point and supports running compact source files directly. No inspection that forbids the compact source file form. |
| **PMD** | PMD 7.16.0 (2025-07-25) added Java 25 language support, including JEP 512 parser support. No built-in PMD rule that targets compact source files. |

---

## 1.7 Good Source of Best Practices

- [JEP 512](https://openjdk.org/jeps/512): normative spec. Defines compact source files, the implicit class semantics (always `final`, unnamed package, single implicit class per file), and the instance `main()` entry point.
- [Inside Java articles on compact source files](https://inside.java/tag/compact-source-files): explanatory material from the OpenJDK team on intended use cases (scripting, learning, single-file programs).

**Enforceable by Checkstyle:**

1. Detect a compact source file (drives `CompactSourceFileCheck`, §3).
2. All NPE, FP, and FN fixes in §1.2 (token-level and parent-walk fixes; purely syntactic).

---

## 3. Proposed New Checks

- **CompactSourceFileCheck**: detects compact source files. With the implemented grammar this is simply the presence of a `COMPACT_COMPILATION_UNIT` node at the AST root; the check registers for `COMPACT_COMPILATION_UNIT` and fires when it is visited. Allows teams that require explicit class declarations to prohibit compact source files in their codebases. Child issue: https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20229

---

## Identified Work Items

- **NPE crashes (9):** `RequireThis` #19972, `FinalLocalVariable` #19973, `MethodName`, `MissingOverride`, `UnusedLocalVariable`, `MissingOverrideOnRecordAccessor`, `EmptyLineSeparator`, `MagicNumber`, `ModifiedControlVariable` #20267, `FinalClass` #20523, `AbbreviationAsWordInName` #20524.
- **False positives (5):** `PackageDeclaration` #19908, `OuterTypeFilename` #19909, `InvalidJavadocPosition`, `OuterTypeNumber` #20268, `UnnecessarySemicolonAfterOuterTypeDeclaration` #20269.
- **False negatives (17):** `MissingJavadocMethod`, `AnnotationLocation`, `UncommentedMain`, `JavadocMethod`, `HiddenField`, `DeclarationOrder`, `JavadocStyle`, `MethodCount`, `RedundantModifier` (`final` #20226, `public` #20266), `ClassMemberImpliedModifier`, `OverloadMethodsDeclarationOrder`, `VisibilityModifier` #20270, `UnnecessarySemicolonAfterTypeMemberDeclaration` #20271, CovariantEqualsCheck #20552, ClassFanOutComplexityCheck #20553,  WriteTagCheck #20555
- **Verified clean (no action needed):** `AbbreviationAsWordInName`, `IllegalToken`, `IllegalTokenText`, `Indentation`, `NoLineWrap`, `NoWhitespaceAfter`, `MethodParamPad`, `ParenPad`, `GenericWhitespace`.
- **Proposed new check (1):** `CompactSourceFileCheck`.

**Status of grammar support:** implemented in #17810. Adds the `COMPACT_COMPILATION_UNIT` token and the `compactMemberDeclaration` rule. When a file declares any top-level method or field, the grammar emits `COMPACT_COMPILATION_UNIT` as the AST root in place of `COMPILATION_UNIT`

---

## 1.1 Review of Java Enhancement Proposals (JEPs)

**JEP timeline:** [JEP 445](https://openjdk.org/jeps/445) preview (Java 21), [JEP 463](https://openjdk.org/jeps/463) second preview (Java 22), [JEP 477](https://openjdk.org/jeps/477) third preview (Java 23), [JEP 495](https://openjdk.org/jeps/495) fourth preview (Java 24), [JEP 512](https://openjdk.org/jeps/512) final (Java 25).

**What the JEP introduces.** A Java source file may consist of top-level methods and fields with no enclosing class declaration. The compiler wraps the file's members in an implicit class that is always `final` and resides in the unnamed package; the file cannot declare a package. The feature also makes an instance `void main()` (no `public`, no `static`, no parameters) a valid program entry point.

```java
String greeting = "Hello";

void main() {
    System.out.println(greeting);
}
```

**AST structure under the implemented grammar:**

```
COMPACT_COMPILATION_UNIT          (root, replaces COMPILATION_UNIT for compact files)
|--IMPORT
|--VARIABLE_DEF
|--CLASS_DEF                      (nested types are siblings of methods and fields)
`--METHOD_DEF
```

**Problems the JEP creates for existing checks:**

1. Top-level members have no enclosing `CLASS_DEF` or `OBJBLOCK`. Every check that walks `getParent()` to find a class, or guards on `parent == OBJBLOCK`, must be reviewed. This drives §1.2.
2. Instance `void main()` is now a valid entry point. `UncommentedMainCheck` currently insists on `public static` and silently misses the new form. This drives a child issue in §1.2.
3. The unnamed package is mandatory. `PackageDeclarationCheck` will fire "Missing package declaration" on every compact file with no way to fix it.
4. The implicit class is always `final`. `RedundantModifierCheck` should flag `final` on its top-level methods.

---

## 1.2 Similar and Related Tokens

### Method

Candidate impacted checks were identified by:

```bash
checks=src/main/java/com/puppycrawl/tools/checkstyle/checks
{
  grep -rl "OBJBLOCK"  $checks
  grep -rl "CLASS_DEF" $checks
  grep -rl "COMPILATION_UNIT"   $checks
} | sed "s|^$checks/||" | sort -u

```

Each candidate was then run via the Checkstyle CLI against a minimal compact source file mirroring the scenarios in the audit (top-level field plus `void main()`, with the specific construct each check needs to trigger) and against a sanity-check file with the same members inside a normal class. 

### 2a. NPE Crashes (11, verified still crashing)

| Check | Verified behaviour | Child Issue |
|---|---|---|
| `RequireThisCheck` | Throws `NullPointerException` (`frame is null`); no `CLASS_FRAME` is pushed for the implicit class | #19972 |
| `FinalLocalVariableCheck` | Throws `NullPointerException` (`Deque.peek()` null); scope-stack underflow with no `OBJBLOCK` pushed | #19973 |
| `MethodNameCheck` | Throws `NullPointerException` (`classDefOrNew is null`) on any top-level method | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20210 |
| `MissingOverrideCheck` (`javaFiveCompatibility=true`) | Throws `NullPointerException` (`defOrNew is null`) on a top-level method whose Javadoc contains `@inheritDoc` | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20212 |
| `UnusedLocalVariableCheck` | Throws `NullPointerException` (`grandParent is null`) when a top-level field is present | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20213 |
| `MissingOverrideOnRecordAccessorCheck` | Throws `NullPointerException` (`grandParent is null`) on a top-level record accessor | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20214 |
| `EmptyLineSeparatorCheck` | Throws `NullPointerException` (`getParent() is null`) in `isTypeField` on a compact file with adjacent top-level members | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20215 |
| `MagicNumberCheck` (`ignoreFieldDeclaration=true`) | Throws `NullPointerException` (`getParent() is null`) in `isFieldDeclaration` on a top-level numeric literal | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20216 |
| `ModifiedControlVariableCheck` | Throws `NullPointerException` (`Deque.contains` on null `currentVariables`); scope-stack underflow with no `OBJBLOCK` pushed when a `for` loop appears in a top-level method | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20267 |
| `FinalClassCheck` | Throws `NullPointerException` (`Deque.peek()` null in `typeDeclarations`) on a top-level anonymous class declaration in a compact file; no `CLASS_DEF` ancestor pushes onto the stack when the anonymous class's outer type is the implicit class | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20523 |
| `AbbreviationAsWordInNameCheck` | Throws `NullPointerException` (`astParent2` null in `isInterfaceDeclaration`) on a top-level field whose name contains an abbreviation; `variableDefAst.getParent().getParent()` overshoots `COMPACT_COMPILATION_UNIT` to null | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20524 |


### 2b. False Positives (5, all verified)

| Check | Verified behaviour | Child Issue |
|---|---|---|
| `PackageDeclarationCheck` | Fires "Missing package declaration" on every compact file. Compact files must be in the unnamed package, so the violation is unfixable | #19908 |
| `OuterTypeFilenameCheck` | Fires "type.file.mismatch" on a named nested class. That class is a member of the implicit class, not the outer type | #19909 |
| `InvalidJavadocPositionCheck` | Fires "Javadoc comment is placed in the wrong location" on correctly-placed Javadoc before top-level fields and methods. Field and method detection requires `OBJBLOCK` ancestry, which does not exist in compact files | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20217 |
| `OuterTypeNumberCheck` | Counts every `CLASS_DEF` child of `COMPACT_COMPILATION_UNIT` as an outer type, so a compact file with two top-level classes is flagged "Outer types defined is 2". Identical classes inside an ordinary outer class produce zero violations | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20268 |
| `UnnecessarySemicolonAfterOuterTypeDeclarationCheck` | Fires on `} ;` after a nested class in a compact file. The class is a member of the implicit class, not an outer type | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20269 |

### 2c. False Negatives (17, all verified)

Each input that should fire produces zero violations. 

| Check | Symptom on compact file | Child Issue |
|---|---|---|
| `MissingJavadocMethodCheck` | Top-level public method without Javadoc not flagged | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20218 |
| `AnnotationLocationCheck` | Annotation on a top-level variable not flagged | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20219 |
| `UncommentedMainCheck` | Instance `void main()` not flagged | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20220 |
| `JavadocMethodCheck` | Wrong `@param` on a top-level method not flagged | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20221 |
| `HiddenFieldCheck` | Parameter shadowing a top-level field not flagged | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20222 |
| `DeclarationOrderCheck` | Field after method not flagged | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20223 |
| `JavadocStyleCheck` | Missing first-sentence period on a top-level member not flagged | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20224 |
| `MethodCountCheck` | Top-level methods not counted toward `maxTotal`, `maxPublic`, etc. | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20225 |
| `RedundantModifierCheck` | `final` on a top-level method not flagged, though the implicit class is always final | #20226 |
| `RedundantModifierCheck` | `public` on a top-level method not flagged, though the implicit class is final and in the unnamed package, so `public` cannot widen access to anything | #20266 |
| `ClassMemberImpliedModifierCheck` | Nested enum or interface missing implied `static` not flagged | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20227 |
| `OverloadMethodsDeclarationOrderCheck` | Split top-level overloads not flagged | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20228 |
| `VisibilityModifierCheck` | Non-private top-level fields not flagged. `isAnonymousClassVariable` uses `parent != OBJBLOCK` as a proxy for "anonymous-class field" and excludes every top-level field in a compact file | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20270 |
| `UnnecessarySemicolonAfterTypeMemberDeclarationCheck` | Trailing `;` after a nested-type declaration that is a child of `COMPACT_COMPILATION_UNIT` not flagged; the check guards on `parent == OBJBLOCK` | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20271 |
| `ClassFanOutComplexityCheck` | Fan-out of the implicit class is not measured; the check registers for `CLASS_DEF`/`INTERFACE_DEF`/etc. and never starts because there is no top-level `CLASS_DEF` for the implicit class | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20553 |
| `CovariantEqualsCheck` | Covariant `equals` method declared at the top level of a compact source file is not flagged; the check walks bodies of `CLASS_DEF`/`ENUM_DEF`/`RECORD_DEF`/`LITERAL_NEW` and the implicit class has none of those tokens | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20552 |
| `WriteTagCheck` | The first top-level method's `@tag` values are not reported; any leading block comment at the top of the file (copyright header, xdocs inline-config header, etc.) attaches to that method's `TYPE` node in compact form and is misread as its Javadoc | https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20555 |

### Verified clean, no change required

The implemented grammar gives top-level members a non-null parent (`COMPACT_COMPILATION_UNIT`), which fixes one of the originally audited NPEs:

---

## 1.3 Frequently Impacted Checks

| Check | Verified behaviour on compact source files | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `IllegalToken` | Accepts all token types via `TokenUtil.getAllTokenIds()`; default tokens (`LABELED_STAT` only) are unaffected. Users can opt into `COMPACT_COMPILATION_UNIT` if desired. | No change required |
| `IllegalTokenText` | Operates only on literals, identifiers, and comments. JEP 512 introduces no new text-bearing tokens. | No change required |
| `IndentationCheck` | Correctly tracks indent context for top-level methods (verified: an over-indented body inside `void main()` is flagged with the expected level). No crash, correct violation. | No change required |
| Whitespace family: `EmptyLineSeparatorCheck` | See §2a (NPE) | NPE, child issue listed above |
| Whitespace family: `NoLineWrapCheck` | Operates on `PACKAGE_DEF` and `IMPORT` only. Compact files cannot declare a package and imports remain unchanged structurally. No crash on tested inputs. | No change required |
| Whitespace family: `NoWhitespaceAfter`, `MethodParamPad`, `ParenPad`, `GenericWhitespace` | Not structurally relevant: compact source files contain no new operator or punctuation patterns these checks target. | No change required |

---

## 1.5 Review of Other Static Analysis Tools

| Tool | What it ships for JEP 512 |
|---|---|
| **IntelliJ IDEA** | Recognises instance `void main()` as a valid entry point and supports running compact source files directly. No inspection that forbids the compact source file form. |
| **PMD** | PMD 7.16.0 (2025-07-25) added Java 25 language support, including JEP 512 parser support. No built-in PMD rule that targets compact source files. |

---

## 1.7 Good Source of Best Practices

- [JEP 512](https://openjdk.org/jeps/512): normative spec. Defines compact source files, the implicit class semantics (always `final`, unnamed package, single implicit class per file), and the instance `main()` entry point.
- [Inside Java articles on compact source files](https://inside.java/tag/compact-source-files): explanatory material from the OpenJDK team on intended use cases (scripting, learning, single-file programs).

**Enforceable by Checkstyle:**

1. Detect a compact source file (drives `CompactSourceFileCheck`, §3).
2. All NPE, FP, and FN fixes in §1.2 (token-level and parent-walk fixes; purely syntactic).

---

## 3. Proposed New Checks

- **CompactSourceFileCheck**: detects compact source files. With the implemented grammar this is simply the presence of a `COMPACT_COMPILATION_UNIT` node at the AST root; the check registers for `COMPACT_COMPILATION_UNIT` and fires when it is visited. Allows teams that require explicit class declarations to prohibit compact source files in their codebases. Child issue: https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/20229

---

## Identified Work Items

- **NPE crashes (9):** `RequireThis` #19972, `FinalLocalVariable` #19973, `MethodName`, `MissingOverride`, `UnusedLocalVariable`, `MissingOverrideOnRecordAccessor`, `EmptyLineSeparator`, `MagicNumber`, `ModifiedControlVariable` #20267, `FinalClass` #20523, `AbbreviationAsWordInName` #20524.
- **False positives (5):** `PackageDeclaration` #19908, `OuterTypeFilename` #19909, `InvalidJavadocPosition`, `OuterTypeNumber` #20268, `UnnecessarySemicolonAfterOuterTypeDeclaration` #20269.
- **False negatives (17):** `MissingJavadocMethod`, `AnnotationLocation`, `UncommentedMain`, `JavadocMethod`, `HiddenField`, `DeclarationOrder`, `JavadocStyle`, `MethodCount`, `RedundantModifier` (`final` #20226, `public` #20266), `ClassMemberImpliedModifier`, `OverloadMethodsDeclarationOrder`, `VisibilityModifier` #20270, `UnnecessarySemicolonAfterTypeMemberDeclaration` #20271, CovariantEqualsCheck #20552, ClassFanOutComplexityCheck #20553,  WriteTagCheck #20555
- **Verified clean (no action needed):** `AbbreviationAsWordInName`, `IllegalToken`, `IllegalTokenText`, `Indentation`, `NoLineWrap`, `NoWhitespaceAfter`, `MethodParamPad`, `ParenPad`, `GenericWhitespace`.
- **Proposed new check (1):** `CompactSourceFileCheck`.

**Total: 33 child issues + 1 new check.**

I have read check documentation: https://checkstyle.org/checks/coding/expressionoverblocklambda.html
I have downloaded the latest checkstyle from: https://checkstyle.org/cmdline.html#Download_and_Run
I have executed the cli and showed it below, as cli describes the problem better than 1,000 words

```bash
/var/tmp $ javac ControlLambda.java
/var/tmp $ cat config.xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE module PUBLIC
          "-//Checkstyle//DTD Checkstyle Configuration 1.3//EN"
          "https://checkstyle.org/dtds/configuration_1_3.dtd">
<module name="Checker">
  <module name="TreeWalker">
    <module name="ExpressionOverBlockLambda"/>
  </module>
</module>
/var/tmp $ cat ControlLambda.java
import java.util.function.Supplier;
public class ControlLambda {
    Supplier<String> c1 = () -> { return "ctrl"; };  // flagged

    Supplier<String> rule(int x) {
        return switch (x) {
            case 1 -> () -> { return "one"; };  // should be flagged too
            default -> () -> "other";
        };
    }
}
/var/tmp $ RUN_LOCALE="-Duser.language=en -Duser.country=US"
/var/tmp $ java $RUN_LOCALE -jar checkstyle-14.1.0-all.jar -c config.xml ControlLambda.java
Starting audit...
[ERROR] /var/tmp/ControlLambda.java:4:30: Expression lambdas are preferred over single-line block lambdas. [ExpressionOverBlockLambda]
Audit done.
Checkstyle ends with 1 errors.
```

---

**Describe what you expect in detail.**

Both `c1` and the `case 1` rule value are single-line block lambdas whose only statement is `return <expr>;` and are convertible to expression lambdas (`() -> "ctrl"` / `() -> "one"`). The check should report **both**. Only line 4 is reported; the switch-rule value lambda on line 9 is silently skipped.

body_text:
Most of our workflows don't declare a top-level `permissions:` block, so their `GITHUB_TOKEN` inherits whatever the repository-level default happens to be. That default can be widened by an admin without any diff or PR — the workflow itself gives no indication of what scope its token actually has at runtime.

**Where we are today**

24 of 39 workflows have no top-level `permissions:` in `upstream/master`:

- `.github/workflows/actionlint.yml`
- `.github/workflows/check-performance-regression.yml`
- `.github/workflows/check-pr-description.yml`
- `.github/workflows/checker-framework.yml`
- `.github/workflows/error-prone.yml`
- `.github/workflows/google-java-format.yml`
- `.github/workflows/no-error-workflow.yml`
- `.github/workflows/no-exception-workflow.yml`
- `.github/workflows/no-old-refs.yml`
- `.github/workflows/pitest.yml`
- `.github/workflows/qodana.yml`
- `.github/workflows/release-copy-github-io-to-sourceforge.yml`
- `.github/workflows/release-maven-perform.yml`
- `.github/workflows/release-publish-releasenotes-twitter.yml`
- `.github/workflows/release-update-github-io.yml`
- `.github/workflows/release-update-github-page.yml`
- `.github/workflows/release-update-xdoc-with-releasenotes.yml`
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- `.github/workflows/releasenotes-gen.yml`
- `.github/workflows/run-checkstyle-ast-print.yml`
- `.github/workflows/run-checkstyle.yml`
- `.github/workflows/run-link-check.yml`
- `.github/workflows/shellcheck.yml`
- `.github/workflows/verify-no-exception-configs.yml`

**Why it matters**

Two concrete failure modes:

1. **Blast radius on a compromised action or step.** Any code that runs inside a workflow (a third-party action, a shell step, an inline script) can use `GITHUB_TOKEN` at whatever scope the workflow was granted. If the token has `contents: write` because nothing declares otherwise, a compromised step can push commits, delete branches, or create releases. If the workflow declares `permissions: { contents: read }` at the root, the same compromised step can only read.

2. **Silent widening.** Settings → Actions → General → "Workflow permissions" controls the repo-level default. Flipping it from read-only to write is a single-click admin action with no diff, no PR, no audit trail visible to reviewers. Explicit `permissions:` at the workflow level makes the intended scope readable in the workflow file itself.

body_text:
From [#18811](https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/pull/18811#discussion_r3252149340)

`EmptyLineSeparator` reports violations at different locations for fields and methods depending on the type of comment associated with the definition.

The current behavior is inconsistent:

```
default field        -> 'VARIABLE_DEF'
default method       -> 'METHOD_DEF'
public/private field -> '/*'
public/private method -> '/*'
class definitions    -> always '/*'
```
The same variation can also be observed with different comment types, including single-line comments, multi-line comments, and javadoc comments.

## Example
### config_check.xml

```
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE module PUBLIC "-//Puppy Crawl//DTD Check Configuration 1.3//EN" 
"http://www.puppycrawl.com/dtds/configuration_1_3.dtd">

<module name="Checker">
  <module name="TreeWalker">
    <module name="EmptyLineSeparator">
      <property name="allowMultipleEmptyLines" value="false"/>
    </module>
  </module>
</module>
```
### Test.java
```


/** Field docs. */
class Test {



    /** Field docs. */
    int value;


    /** Field docs. */
    public int value;

    
    /** Field docs. */
    private int value;

    
    /** Method docs. */
    void method() {}


    /** Method docs. */
    public void method1() {}


    /** Method docs. */
    private void method2() {}
    
}
```

### logs
```
$ java -jar checkstyle-13.4.2-all.jar -c config_check.xml Test.java
Starting audit...
[ERROR] F:\GitHub\headhtmltagname\Test.java:3:1: '/*' has more than 1 empty lines before. [EmptyLineSeparator]
[ERROR] F:\GitHub\headhtmltagname\Test.java:9:5: 'VARIABLE_DEF' has more than 1 empty lines before. [EmptyLineSeparator]
[ERROR] F:\GitHub\headhtmltagname\Test.java:12:5: '/*' has more than 1 empty lines before. [EmptyLineSeparator]
[ERROR] F:\GitHub\headhtmltagname\Test.java:16:5: '/*' has more than 1 empty lines before. [EmptyLineSeparator]
[ERROR] F:\GitHub\headhtmltagname\Test.java:21:5: 'METHOD_DEF' has more than 1 empty lines before. [EmptyLineSeparator]
[ERROR] F:\GitHub\headhtmltagname\Test.java:24:5: '/*' has more than 1 empty lines before. [EmptyLineSeparator]
[ERROR] F:\GitHub\headhtmltagname\Test.java:28:5: '/*' has more than 1 empty lines before. [EmptyLineSeparator]
Audit done.
Checkstyle ends with 7 errors.
```

## Expected behavior

The violation location should be consistent for fields and methods regardless of their modifiers or the type of comment preceding them.

Reporting the violation on the comment token (`/*`) would also make the locaiton consistent with the existing behvaior for other definitions and provide a more suitable location for automatic fixes.

This issue is intended to address the inconsistent violation location for fields and mehtods.

{"repository": "checkstyle/checkstyle", "task_candidate_id": 2763, "repository_id": 57, "issue_number": 21726, "github_issue_id": 5591278188, "html_url": "https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/21726", "created_at": "2026-09-26T04:15:25+00:00", "author_association": "CONTRIBUTOR", "title": "EmptyLineSeparator: Inconsistent violation location for fields and methods with comments and Javadoc", "body_text": "From [#18811](https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/pull/18811#discussion_r3252149340)

`EmptyLineSeparator` reports violations at different locations for fields and methods depending on the type of comment associated with the definition.

The current behavior is inconsistent:

```
default field        -> 'VARIABLE_DEF'
default method       -> 'METHOD_DEF'
public/private field -> '/*'
public/private method -> '/*'
class definitions    -> always '/*'
```
The same variation can also be observed with different comment types, including single-line comments, multi-line comments, and javadoc comments.

## Example
### config_check.xml

```
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE module PUBLIC "-//Puppy Crawl//DTD Check Configuration 1.3//EN" 
"http://www.puppycrawl.com/dtds/configuration_1_3.dtd">

<module name="Checker">
  <module name="TreeWalker">
    <module name="EmptyLineSeparator">
      <property name="allowMultipleEmptyLines" value="false"/>
    </module>
  </module>
</module>
```
### Test.java
```


/** Field docs. */
class Test {



    /** Field docs. */
    int value;


    /** Field docs. */
    public int value;

    
    /** Field docs. */
    private int value;

    
    /** Method docs. */
    void method() {}


    /** Method docs. */
    public void method1() {}


    /** Method docs. */
    private void method2() {}
    
}
```

### logs
```

[ERROR] F:\GitHub\headhtmltagname\Test.java:3:1: '/*' has more than 1 empty lines before. [EmptyLineSeparator]
[ERROR] F:\GitHub\headhtmltagname\Test.java:9:5: 'VARIABLE_DEF' has more than 1 empty lines before. [EmptyLineSeparator]
[ERROR] F:\GitHub\headhtmltagname\Test.java:12:5: '/*' has more than 1 empty lines before. [EmptyLineSeparator]

[ERROR] F:\GitHub\headhtmltagname\Test.java:21:5: 'METHOD_DEF' has more than 1 empty lines before. [EmptyLineSeparator]
[ERROR] F:\GitHub\headhtmltagname\Test.java:24:5: '/*' has more than 1 empty lines before. [EmptyLineSeparator]
[ERROR] F:\GitHub\headhtmltagname\Test.java:28:5: '/*' has more than 1 empty lines before. [EmptyLineSeparator]
Audit done.
Checkstyle ends with 7 errors.
```

## Expected behavior

The violation location should be consistent for fields and methods regardless of their modifiers or the type of comment preceding them.

Reporting the violation on the comment token (`/*`) would also make the locaiton consistent with the existing behvaior for other definitions and provide a more suitable location for automatic fixes.

This issue is intended to address the inconsistent violation location for fields and mehtods.

https://checkstyle.sourceforge.io/styleguides/sun-code-conventions-19990420/CodeConventions.doc6.html#a460

#### Description
Add Checkstyle checks for all rules under 7.6 - while Statements of the Code Conventions for the Java™ Programming Language.

#### Rules covered

From 7.6 - while Statements (`CodeConventions.doc6.html#a460`):

> A while statement should have the following form:
>
> ```java
> while (condition) {
>     statements;
> }
> ```
>
> An empty while statement should have the following form:
>
> ```java
> while (condition);
> ```

#### Checks to add to sun_checks.xml

None for the braced form: `NeedBraces` and `LeftCurly` are already present and check `LITERAL_WHILE` by default. Only the coverage row and test suite are missing.

#### Open Points

1. **Empty `while` statement**

   Sun allows `while (condition);`, but `sun_checks.xml` reports it through `NeedBraces` (`allowEmptyLoopBody` is `false`) and `EmptyStatement` (which is not configurable). The braced alternative `while (condition) {}` is reported as well, by `EmptyBlock`.

   This is the same question as the empty `for` statement in rule 7.5, so I suggest following whatever is decided there:

   - **Option A:** Set `allowEmptyLoopBody=true` on `NeedBraces` and extend `EmptyStatement` with a property to skip empty loop bodies. This requires a check change, not only a configuration change.
   - **Option B:** Set `allowEmptyLoopBody=true` and remove `EmptyStatement` from `sun_checks.xml`.
   - **Option C:** Keep `sun_checks.xml` stricter than Sun and document the deviation on the coverage page.

2. **Closing brace.** `RightCurly` doesn't include `LITERAL_WHILE` by default, so the `}` of a while body is unchecked. Should we add it to the tokens, together with `LITERAL_FOR` from 7.5?

#### Progress tracker

| Check | Rule | PR |
|---|---|---|
| NeedBraces | while body uses braces | |
| LeftCurly | `{` at end of the while line | |
| RightCurly | `}` closing the while body | point 2 |
| ? | empty while statement | point 1 |

I have read check documentation: https://checkstyle.org/checks/coding/unnecessarynullcheckwithinstanceof.html
I have downloaded the latest checkstyle from: https://checkstyle.org/cmdline.html#Download_and_Run
I have executed the cli and showed it below, as cli describes the problem better than 1,000 words

```bash
/var/tmp $ javac Test.java
# (no errors - compilation successful)

/var/tmp $ cat config.xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE module PUBLIC
          "-//Puppy Crawl//DTD Check Configuration 1.3//EN"
          "https://checkstyle.org/dtds/configuration_1_3.dtd">
<module name="Checker">
  <module name="TreeWalker">
    <module name="UnnecessaryNullCheckWithInstanceOf"/>
  </module>
</module>

/var/tmp $ cat Test.java
public class Test {
    public void testArithmeticWrap(Object obj) {
        // obj.hashCode() is a real dereference - null check IS necessary
        if (obj != null && (obj.hashCode() + 1 > 0) && obj instanceof String) {
            System.out.println("ok");
        }
    }
}

/var/tmp $ RUN_LOCALE="-Duser.language=en -Duser.country=US"
/var/tmp $ java $RUN_LOCALE -jar checkstyle-14.3.0-all.jar -c config.xml Test.java
Starting audit...
[ERROR] Test.java:4:13: Unnecessary nullity check before instanceof. [UnnecessaryNullCheckWithInstanceOf]
Audit done.
Checkstyle ends with 1 errors.
```

---

**Describe what you expect in detail.**

No violation should be reported on line 4. The expression
`obj != null && (obj.hashCode() + 1 > 0) && obj instanceof String`
dereferences `obj` via `obj.hashCode()` inside an arithmetic sub-expression
(`obj.hashCode() + 1`). Removing the `obj != null` guard would cause a
`NullPointerException` when `obj` is `null`. The null check is **necessary**
and must **not** be flagged.

The false positive is caused by `containsVariableDereference()` in
`UnnecessaryNullCheckWithInstanceOfCheck.java` (lines 244-266). The method
only recurses into four token types (`DOT`, `METHOD_CALL`, `LAND`, `LOR`).
When a real dereference like `obj.hashCode()` is wrapped inside an arithmetic
(`PLUS`), comparison (`GT`, `LT`), or bitwise (`BAND`, `BOR`, `BXOR`) operator
node, the recursion stops at that parent node without ever visiting the
`DOT`/`METHOD_CALL` inside it. The method therefore returns `false` (no
dereference found) and the null check is incorrectly flagged as redundant.

**AST of the false-positive expression**
(`obj != null && (obj.hashCode() + 1 > 0) && obj instanceof String`):

```
LAND
+-- LAND
|   +-- NOT_EQUAL            <- flagged as redundant (incorrect)
|   |   +-- IDENT (obj)
|   |   +-- LITERAL_NULL
|   +-- GT                   <- NOT in the dispatch list; recursion stops here
|       +-- PLUS
|       |   +-- METHOD_CALL
|       |   |   +-- DOT (obj . hashCode)  <- dereference is MISSED
|       |   +-- NUM_INT (1)
|       +-- NUM_INT (0)
+-- LITERAL_INSTANCEOF
    +-- IDENT (obj)
    +-- TYPE (String)
```

Additional cases that trigger the same false positive:

```java
// GT wrapping a method call dereference
if (obj != null && obj.hashCode() > 0 && obj instanceof String) { }

// BAND wrapping a DOT dereference
if (obj != null && (obj.hashCode() & 0xFF) == 0 && obj instanceof String) { }

// EQUAL wrapping a method call
if (obj != null && obj.toString().equals("x") == false && obj instanceof String) { }
```

**Expected fix:** Extend `containsVariableDereference()` to perform a full
depth-first traversal of all node types, not just the four currently listed
(`DOT`, `METHOD_CALL`, `LAND`, `LOR`). A regression test input file
`InputUnnecessaryNullCheckWithInstanceOfArithmeticDereference.java` should be
added under:
`src/test/resources/com/puppycrawl/tools/checkstyle/checks/coding/unnecessarynullcheckwithinstanceof/`
covering `PLUS`, `MINUS`, `GT`, `LT`, `EQUAL`, `BAND`, `BOR`, and `BXOR`
wrapper scenarios with both violation and no-violation cases.

Note: Issue #17137 (fixed Jan 2026) addressed false positives for `LOR`/nested
cases. It did **not** address non-logical binary operator wrappers (`PLUS`,
`GT`, `BAND`, etc.), which is the distinct root cause described here.

In Test.java:

java
if (this.str != null && this.str instanceof String)

The null check this.str != null is redundant because this.str instanceof String inherently evaluates to false when this.str is null.

Currently, UnnecessaryNullCheckWithInstanceOf only inspects direct IDENT tokens under LITERAL_INSTANCEOF and NOT_EQUAL. When a class field is referenced with this. I have read check documentation: https://checkstyle.org/checks/coding/redundantthis.html
I have downloaded the latest checkstyle from: https://checkstyle.org/cmdline.html#Download_and_Run
I have executed the cli and showed it below, as cli describes the problem better than 1,000 words

`RedundantThis` is not released yet (it is `@since 14.4.0`), so this was reproduced on current master (`e60c0cb348`) by running `com.puppycrawl.tools.checkstyle.Main` from `target/classes`.

```bash
/var/tmp $ javac Test.java

/var/tmp $ cat config.xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE module PUBLIC
  "-//Checkstyle//DTD Checkstyle Configuration 1.3//EN"
  "https://checkstyle.org/dtds/configuration_1_3.dtd">
<module name="Checker">
  <module name="TreeWalker">
    <module name="RedundantThis"/>
  </module>
</module>

/var/tmp $ cat Test.java
public class Test {
    private int x;

    public void update(int k) {
        switch (k) {
            case 1:
                int x = 1;
                System.out.println(x);
                break;
            case 2:
                x = 5; // local 'x' declared in case 1 is still in scope
                this.x = x; // 'this' is required here
                break;
            default:
                break;
        }
    }
}

/var/tmp $ RUN_LOCALE="-Duser.language=en -Duser.country=US"
/var/tmp $ java $RUN_LOCALE -cp target/classes:<dependencies> \
    com.puppycrawl.tools.checkstyle.Main -c config.xml Test.java
Starting audit...
[ERROR] Test.java:12:17: Redundant "this", field 'x' can be accessed directly. [RedundantThis]
Audit done.
Checkstyle ends with 1 errors.
```

---

**Describe what you expect in detail.**

No violation on line 12.

In an old-style (`case ...:`) switch, the scope of a local variable declared in a switch block statement group is the rest of the whole switch block (JLS 6.3), not only its own case group. So the local `x` from `case 1` is still in scope in `case 2`, and `this.x` is required there to refer to the field.

Following the violation and removing `this.` turns line 12 into `x = x;`, which assigns the local to itself and silently stops updating the field.

The check pushes a new scope for every `SLIST`, and every case group gets its own `SLIST`, so the local is dropped from the scope when `case 1` ends.

Related, but different cases of scope tracking: #21974 (lambda parameters), #21995 (for loop variables).

body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

AI coding agents (Claude Code, Copilot, Codex, ...) are used more and more for contributions. Without
project-specific guidance they repeat the same mistakes that CI then rejects:

- running `-Pno-validations` tests without `-DskipTests=false` (the profile silently skips all tests)
- missing the UTF-8 locale requirement of `antrun:run@ant-phase-verify`
- writing multi-line commit messages or trailers that `CommitValidationTest` rejects
- ignoring the inline config / `// violation` conventions of test inputs and the strict jacoco/pitest
  requirements

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Add an `AGENTS.md` (the common convention read by AI coding agents) in the repository root. It would
cover:

- build and test commands
- the CI tasks in `.ci/validation.sh`
- repository layout
- test, code and commit conventions
- OpenRewrite pitfalls

It only contains facts already enforced by the build or CI, and it is checked by the existing
markdownlint and spelling jobs.

**Additional context**

Requested to be split out of #21902 in review. Implementation: #22043.

---

**Describe what you expect in detail.**

No crash. Checkstyle should report the violation, as it does for smaller expressions:

```
[ERROR] /var/tmp/Test.java:2:5: Count of 9999 for 'VARIABLE_DEF' descendant 'PLUS' exceeds maximum count 100. [DescendantToken]
```

`DescendantTokenCheck#countTokens` recurses once per AST level, so a deep tree such as a long
string concatenation overflows the stack. The parser already handles such trees without recursion
(see `JavaAstVisitorTest#testNoStackOverflowOnDeepStringConcat`). The traversal in the check
should be iterative too.

```
[ERROR] /var/tmp/Test.java:2:5: Count of 9999 for 'VARIABLE_DEF' descendant 'PLUS' exceeds maximum count 100. [DescendantToken]
```

`DescendantTokenCheck#countTokens` recurses once per AST level, so a deep tree such as a long
string concatenation overflows the stack. The parser already handles such trees without recursion
(see `JavaAstVisitorTest#testNoStackOverflowOnDeepStringConcat`). The traversal in the check
should be iterative too.

Related tracker: #12191. This issue asks for a design decision on its remaining `AbstractFileSetCheck.process` to `CommonUtil.matchesFileExtension` dependency.

**How it works Now:**

This concerns internal architecture, rather than a new check or property. Check-specific documentation, a downloaded release CLI, and a `javac`/CLI failure reproduction are not applicable: no user-visible failure is being reported.

In the current upstream implementation, `setFileExtensions` copies the supplied array and normalizes extensions with a leading dot. `process` then calls:

```java
if (CommonUtil.matchesFileExtension(file, fileExtensions)) {
    processFiltered(file, fileText);
}
```

`CommonUtil.matchesFileExtension` normalizes extensions again before comparing them to `file.getName()`. This call is covered by a temporary API-to-util suppression in `ArchUnitTest`.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The approved tracker asks contributors to resolve these architecture suppressions or explain why they should be permanent. PR #22012 resolved the FileText/FileContents slice and left this matcher as shared logic needing a separate decision. I would like to confirm that decision before submitting a change for this slice.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Use a private matcher in `AbstractFileSetCheck` over the extension state that its setter already copies and normalizes, then remove only the corresponding architecture suppression. Retain acceptance of unconfigured/empty filters, case-sensitive basename suffix matching, compound suffixes, and the public API.

`Checker`, the general-purpose `CommonUtil` method, and the logging/tab-expansion suppressions would remain unchanged. Expected CLI diagnostics would be unchanged for valid configurations; no performance improvement is claimed.

Is this normalized-state approach acceptable, or should this particular API-to-util dependency be retained as a permanent suppression?

**Additional context**

- Approved parent task: #12191.
- Related merged work: #22012, merged October 18, 2026. Its body identifies this matcher as a remaining design decision.
- The same scope was noted on the parent tracker: https://github.com/checkstyle/checkstyle/issues/12191#issuecomment-6314425058.
- A local three-file prototype and PR description are prepared. Targeted API/architecture tests and scoped style/static/coverage checks pass; scoped PIT kills 86/86 mutations. These results are not full-project validation.
- Updating the prototype to the latest master, successful `mvn clean verify`, and an external-project diff report are still pending. No PR is open, and the new issue is not being treated as approval of the proposed implementation.

### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem-solving, not venting, and I have provided as much detail as possible.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched existing open/closed issues, discussions, and PRs for tab-bar status indicators and found nothing.
- [x] The title is short and descriptive.
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include this feature: `AppShellTabBar` renders no session status today.

### Platform

macOS (the implementation itself is platform-agnostic)

### Version

v2.1.3 (dev checkout). The feature is implemented on a local `main` working tree, not yet committed.

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

The topic / agent-session list already shows per-conversation status through `ConversationRowStatus` — green dot = completed and not yet seen, amber "Pending" pill = awaiting tool approval, red alert icon = error, grey spinner = running. The top tab bar (`AppShellTabBar`) shows none of it, so that state is only discoverable conversation by conversation.

The workflow this costs us: many tabs open with several agents running at once. Whenever an agent needs a response, the only place that says so is the conversation list — so we read the conversation's name there, then hunt for that name among the top tabs, and only then open it. Every hand-off costs a lookup through two separate surfaces.

### Desired Solution

**Implemented locally, pending design review** (no PR yet): a status dot inside the tab on the right, using the same vocabulary as the list — green = completed & unseen, amber = awaiting approval, red = error, grey spinner = running. The tab that needs you is then marked where you are already looking.

No second status source is introduced. Tab URLs already carry the conversation key (`/app/chat?topicId=…`, `/app/agents?sessionId=…`), so a tab resolves the stream-scoped topic id (agent sessions use the synthetic `agent-session:<id>` topic) and reuses the existing `useTopicStreamStatus` over the exact shared-cache keys the list reads (`topic.stream.statuses.<topicId>` and the read receipt `topic.stream.last_seen_completion.<topicId>`). Files:

- new `src/renderer/components/layout/TabConversationStatus.tsx`
- `src/renderer/utils/conversationNavigation.ts`: new `getConversationTopicIdFromTabUrl()`
- `src/renderer/components/layout/AppShellTabBar.tsx`: wiring for normal and pinned tabs

**Questions for the core team, most important first.**

**Q0 — Is this feature wanted at all?** Everything below assumes yes. Value: with many tabs and several agents running in parallel, the tab bar becomes the single surface that answers "which conversation needs me right now" — no more reading a name in the sidebar and then hunting for it among the tabs. If the direction is no, the rest of this issue is moot.

**Q1 — At rest, the dot overlaps the trailing title text.** On a tab that is neither active nor hovered the title runs essentially to the end of the tab (the 80%→100% fade mask is barely perceptible in practice, at most a few percent), so a truncated title ends underneath the dot. Options:

- A. Give the title a right yield while a status dot is present, so it truncates earlier — the same mechanism the close button already uses when it expands. Cost: 12–16px of title on any tab that carries a status.
- B. Start the title's fade mask earlier while a dot is present (e.g. fade from 60%). No layout cost, but less text remains readable.
- C. Accept the overlap.

**Q2 — On the active tab the dot and the close button coexist permanently.** The active tab always shows its close button, so the dot is placed to its left (`right-[26px]`) and both stay visible for as long as the tab is active and the status lasts — this is a steady state, not a transition, and the title's fade is even less adequate there. Options:

- A. Show no dot on the active tab (the state is already visible in the conversation itself).
- B. Keep it and fix the clearance via Q1.
- C. Move the ongoing states (running / approval / error) into the leading icon slot, replacing `TabIcon` (Chrome favicon-spinner style) — zero geometry conflict at any width, at the cost of a second visual language.

**Q3 — Pinned (circular icon) tabs.** The indicator is currently a corner badge on the 28px circle; the 12px spinner reads as oversized there and spills past the circle's edge.

- A. Smaller, inset badge (e.g. an 8px dot at `top-0.5 right-0.5`, with a smaller spinner or none).
- B. A small dot or short underline centred below the icon, leaving the icon area untouched.
- C. Highlight the circle itself (ring / border) instead of adding a badge.
- D. Widen the circular button horizontally into a pill while a status exists, so it can host the indicator.
- E. No indicator on pinned tabs.

**Q4 — Is the overall approach right?** A dot inside the tab at its right edge — is that the Cherry way, or is something else better (dot only on non-active tabs, a colour strip along the tab's bottom edge, a single surfacing point elsewhere in the chrome, …)?

### Alternative Solutions

Implementation paths considered and rejected:

- **Write the status into the `Tab` model / `metadata`**: normal tabs are persisted, so every status transition would write localStorage; more decisively, a background tab's page runs no effects under `<Activity mode="hidden">`, so it could never write its own status. Dead end.
- **One batch subscription in the tab bar, passed down as props**: workable, but it re-renders the whole strip on every status change and enlarges the prop surface; the current per-tab subscription re-renders only the affected tab (2 subscriptions per tab, N≤30, negligible).
- **Reuse the list's `ConversationRowStatus` component directly**: its styles are built for a resource row (absolute overlay, amber text pill, `mr-7` yield). The text pill does not fit a 56–160px tab, so only the semantics and colours were carried over.

### Additional Information

Decisions taken along the way that should be confirmed together with the above:

1. **Semantics identical to the list**: green = completed and unseen; amber = awaiting tool approval (including `awaitingApprovalAnchors`, i.e. an MCP `needsApproval` stream that ends as `done` while still awaiting); red = error; spinner = running; `aborted` shows nothing, as in the list.

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem-solving, not venting, and I have provided as much detail as possible.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched existing open/closed issues, discussions, and PRs for tab-bar status indicators and found nothing.
- [x] The title is short and descriptive.
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include this feature: `AppShellTabBar` renders no session status today.

### Platform

macOS (the implementation itself is platform-agnostic)

### Version

v2.1.3 (dev checkout). The feature is implemented on a local `main` working tree, not yet committed.

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

The topic / agent-session list already shows per-conversation status through `ConversationRowStatus` — green dot = completed and not yet seen, amber "Pending" pill = awaiting tool approval, red alert icon = error, grey spinner = running. The top tab bar (`AppShellTabBar`) shows none of it, so that state is only discoverable conversation by conversation.

The workflow this costs us: many tabs open with several agents running at once. Whenever an agent needs a response, the only place that says so is the conversation list — so we read the conversation's name there, then hunt for that name among the top tabs, and only then open it. Every hand-off costs a lookup through two separate surfaces.

### Desired Solution

**Implemented locally, pending design review** (no PR yet): a status dot inside the tab on the right, using the same vocabulary as the list — green = completed & unseen, amber = awaiting approval, red = error, grey spinner = running. The tab that needs you is then marked where you are already looking.

No second status source is introduced. Tab URLs already carry the conversation key (`/app/chat?topicId=…`, `/app/agents?sessionId=…`), so a tab resolves the stream-scoped topic id (agent sessions use the synthetic `agent-session:<id>` topic) and reuses the existing `useTopicStreamStatus` over the exact shared-cache keys the list reads (`topic.stream.statuses.<topicId>` and the read receipt `topic.stream.last_seen_completion.<topicId>`). Files:

- new `src/renderer/components/layout/TabConversationStatus.tsx`
- `src/renderer/utils/conversationNavigation.ts`: new `getConversationTopicIdFromTabUrl()`
- `src/renderer/components/layout/AppShellTabBar.tsx`: wiring for normal and pinned tabs

**Questions for the core team, most important first.**

**Q0 — Is this feature wanted at all?** Everything below assumes yes. Value: with many tabs and several agents running in parallel, the tab bar becomes the single surface that answers "which conversation needs me right now" — no more reading a name in the sidebar and then hunting for it among the tabs. If the direction is no, the rest of this issue is moot.

**Q1 — At rest, the dot overlaps the trailing title text.** On a tab that is neither active nor hovered the title runs essentially to the end of the tab (the 80%→100% fade mask is barely perceptible in practice, at most a few percent), so a truncated title ends underneath the dot. Options:

- A. Give the title a right yield while a status dot is present, so it truncates earlier — the same mechanism the close button already uses when it expands. Cost: 12–16px of title on any tab that carries a status.
- B. Start the title's fade mask earlier while a dot is present (e.g. fade from 60%). No layout cost, but less text remains readable.
- C. Accept the overlap.

**Q2 — On the active tab the dot and the close button coexist permanently.** The active tab always shows its close button, so the dot is placed to its left (`right-[26px]`) and both stay visible for as long as the tab is active and the status lasts — this is a steady state, not a transition, and the title's fade is even less adequate there. Options:

- A. Show no dot on the active tab (the state is already visible in the conversation itself).
- B. Keep it and fix the clearance via Q1.
- C. Move the ongoing states (running / approval / error) into the leading icon slot, replacing `TabIcon` (Chrome favicon-spinner style) — zero geometry conflict at any width, at the cost of a second visual language.

**Q3 — Pinned (circular icon) tabs.** The indicator is currently a corner badge on the 28px circle; the 12px spinner reads as oversized there and spills past the circle's edge.

- A. Smaller, inset badge (e.g. an 8px dot at `top-0.5 right-0.5`, with a smaller spinner or none).
- B. A small dot or short underline centred below the icon, leaving the icon area untouched.
- C. Highlight the circle itself (ring / border) instead of adding a badge.
- D. Widen the circular button horizontally into a pill while a status exists, so it can host the indicator.
- E. No indicator on pinned tabs.

**Q4 — Is the overall approach right?** A dot inside the tab at its right edge — is that the Cherry way, or is something else better (dot only on non-active tabs, a colour strip along the tab's bottom edge, a single surfacing point elsewhere in the chrome, …)?

### Alternative Solutions

Implementation paths considered and rejected:

- **Write the status into the `Tab` model / `metadata`**: normal tabs are persisted, so every status transition would write localStorage; more decisively, a background tab's page runs no effects under `<Activity mode="hidden">`, so it could never write its own status. Dead end.
- **One batch subscription in the tab bar, passed down as props**: workable, but it re-renders the whole strip on every status change and enlarges the prop surface; the current per-tab subscription re-renders only the affected tab (2 subscriptions per tab, N≤30, negligible).
- **Reuse the list's `ConversationRowStatus` component directly**: its styles are built for a resource row (absolute overlay, amber text pill, `mr-7` yield). The text pill does not fit a 56–160px tab, so only the semantics and colours were carried over.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

2.1.4

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Currently, Cherry Studio does not support RTL (Right-to-Left) direction for languages such as Persian (Farsi) and Arabic. 

When typing in the chat input or reading responses in Persian/Arabic, the text is aligned to the left (LTR). This breaks sentence structures, punctuation marks are placed in the wrong positions, and mixed Persian/English sentences become very difficult to read.


### Desired Solution

Cherry Studio should automatically detect text direction (e.g., using `dir="auto"` or `unicode-bidi: plaintext`) for:
1. The chat input textarea / input fields.
2. The rendered Markdown message bubbles (paragraphs and lists).

Applying the following CSS style can solve the bidirectional layout issues:
```css
.chat-message, .markdown-body p, textarea {
  direction: auto;
  unicode-bidi: plaintext;
  text-align: start;
}
```


### Alternative Solutions

Manually injecting CSS via Developer Tools (Ctrl+Shift+I) or forcing the model to output HTML with `dir="rtl"` in every response.

_No response_
