- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the issue list.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio available to me (2.1.6).

### Platform

Windows

### Version

2.1.6 (Electron 44.4.0 / Chrome 152.0.7977.78, Windows 11 Pro)

### Bug Description

Opening a regular Chat topic that carries many attachments puts the whole window into an OS "not responding" state for several seconds; it recovers by itself. Agent sessions opened in the same app do not show this.

The reporter's condition is deterministic on attachment count: one conversation with 12 attachments blocks every time, conversations with few attachments are not noticeably affected. Their local attachment library holds 754 files / 1.43 GB, of which 519 are PNG (1.17 GB) and 71 are single files above 5 MB.

Diagnostic logs captured at the time show two concurrent main-process problems in the same window:

1. Text-decoding of attachment buffers on the main thread: 120 `Utils:File` warning/error lines inside roughly two seconds, three per attachment ("Auto-detected windows-1252 but content has invalid characters", "Auto-detected UTF-8 but content has invalid characters", "Failed to decode buffer with all candidate encodings; falling back to UTF-8"). Files that are not text are evidently being run through encoding detection and failing all candidate encodings.
2. Cascading data-API timeouts: 24 `DataApiService` requests hit the 3000 ms ceiling within one and the same second — one `GET /topics` and 23 `GET /files/entries/<id>` — which is the point where the window is reported as unresponsive.

The reporter's own hypothesis is that entering a chat loads metadata for every attachment of the topic, and that the main-process read path performs text-encoding detection on binary files, saturating the main thread and starving IPC. The exact call site is not confirmed by this report; two candidate paths were inspected during triage (see Evidence) and both decode buffers in the main process.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Build up an attachment library of a few hundred files (screenshots, videos, archives) so that one conversation can hold a dozen attachments.
2. Open a regular Chat conversation that has around 12 attachments attached to its messages.
3. Observe the window title / task manager: the window is marked as not responding for a few seconds, then recovers.
4. Compare with a conversation that has one or two attachments, and with an Agent session: neither shows the freeze.

### Expected Behavior

Entering a conversation must not block the main process. Specifically:

- Attachment metadata loading must not run text-encoding detection over binary payloads (images, video, archives).
- Attachment reads should not be issued in a way that lets a dozen of them race into the 3000 ms per-request ceiling at once; a slow or large attachment library must degrade gracefully instead of freezing the UI.
- The window should stay responsive while attachments of a conversation are being resolved.

### Relevant Log Output

Names, paths and identifiers are removed; only levels, modules, timings and endpoint shapes are kept.

```shell
# main-process text decoding of attachment buffers (module Utils:File), 120 lines in ~2s
main warn  Auto-detected windows-1252 but content has invalid characters; trying other encodings
main warn  Auto-detected UTF-8 but content has invalid characters; trying other encodings
main error Failed to decode buffer with all candidate encodings; falling back to UTF-8

# data-API timeouts, 24 requests inside the same second, each at the 3000ms ceiling
DataApiService error Request failed: GET /topics Request timeout: /topics (3000ms)
DataApiService error Request failed: GET /files/entries/<id> Request timeout: /files/entries/<id> (3000ms)
```

### Additional Context

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for commenting in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.

- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [ ] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

Collector note: this report is built from diagnostic packages sent by the affected installations. The latest-version checkbox is left unchecked because a newer build may exist. The FAQ entry was not reviewed. Open and closed issues and pull requests were searched for `session already exists`, `JsonRpcResponseError`, DSH session lifecycle and the Agent session resume path; the closest items are listed under Additional Context. GitHub Discussions were not indexed by the available tooling.

## Platform

Windows 11 Pro x64 and Windows 10 Pro x64 (win32-x64). Two separate installations.

## Version

2.1.6 (also recorded on 2.1.4 in the same package)

## Bug Description

An Agent conversation turn ends with the raw JSON-RPC message surfaced to the user:

```text
session "<sessionId>" already exists
```

The main process records the same text as an `JsonRpcResponseError` (JSON-RPC code `-32603`) raised inside the DSH JSON-RPC line transport while the turn is starting, and the renderer then reports it as an AI stream error for that conversation. Nothing else about the turn is shown: no classified cause, no hint whether the session was adopted or abandoned.

The runtime rejects the request because a session with that id is already registered in the DSH process, while the app is still performing the create/resume step for the same stored conversation. The id is the one the conversation already had, so the app is not generating a new one; the two sides disagree about whether the session is "new" or "existing".

## Steps To Reproduce

The exact trigger is not established from the packages; the observed sequence is:

1. Have an Agent conversation that already ran at least one turn on the DSH runtime.
2. Send the next message in that conversation (in both packages this is a plain send, right after the app has been running or has been restarted).
3. The turn fails immediately with `session "<sessionId>" already exists` instead of continuing the conversation.

## Expected Behavior

- Creating or attaching to a session should be idempotent: if the runtime already holds the id, the app adopts the existing session instead of failing the turn.
- If the runtime state really cannot be reused, the failure should be a named, recoverable condition: close or re-create the runtime session, retry once, and tell the user what happened.
- A raw JSON-RPC error string should not be the only thing a user sees for a turn.

## Relevant Log Output

```text
{"appver":"2.1.6","error":{"message":"session \"<sessionId>\" already exists","name":"JsonRpcResponseError",
 "stack":"JsonRpcResponseError: session \"<sessionId>\" already exists\n    at JsonRpcLineTransport.handleIncomingResponse (app.asar/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-sdk-protocol/lib/index.js)\n    at JsonRpcLineTransport.handleLine (...)\n    at JsonRpcLineTransport.drainLines (...)"},
 "level":"error","message":"AI stream error","module":"useChatWithHistory","process":"renderer"}
```

Session ids, absolute paths, account names and conversation content are removed.

## Additional Context

### Impact

- Two packages from two Windows machines: Windows 11 Pro x64 (2.1.6) and Windows 10 Pro x64 (2.1.4 and 2.1.6), 2026-10-15 to 2026-10-17.
- In each package the error repeats for more than one turn of the affected conversation; the conversation does not recover on its own.
- Independent reporters: two different installations and hardware profiles; the packages do not expose a stable installation id, so this is inferred, not confirmed.

### Evidence

- The raised error is `JsonRpcResponseError` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sdk-protocol` (`JsonRpcLineTransport.handleIncomingResponse`), i.e. the DSH runtime answered the create/resume request with an error, it is not a client-side validation failure.
- Repository `main` at `ab3a0459` contains no producer of the string `already exists` in the Agent session path: `src/main/ai/agentSession/AgentSessionRuntimeService.ts` manages connection lifecycle but the session registry itself lives in the bundled `dsh-sdk-protocol` package, so the conflicting state cannot be read from this tree.

Open and closed issues and pull requests were searched for `unsupported native Responses stream event`, `native_response_conversion_failed`, gateway stream failures and the native Responses adapter family; no matching item was found. GitHub Discussions were not indexed by the available tooling.

## Platform

Windows 11 Home China x64 and Windows 10 Home China x64 (win32-x64). Two separate installations.

## Version

2.1.6 and 2.1.4

## Bug Description

An Agent turn on a model served over the native OpenAI Responses wire fails as soon as the provider stream reaches an event the conversion layer does not know:

```text
发生未知错误 (unsupported native Responses stream event)
```

The same turn is recorded in the main process as a classified error, not as a provider outage:

```text
{"code":"native_response_conversion_failed","errorMessage":"unsupported native Responses stream event",
 "message":"agentLoop error unsupported native Responses stream event","module":"agentLoop","process":"main"}
```

followed by `Execution loop error` in `AiStreamManager`, `Gateway stream failed` in `ProxyStreamService` and an
`API gateway request error` with `code: "UNKNOWN"` in `ApiGatewayErrors`. The renderer then reports the AI stream
error to the user. The turn produces no answer at all, so every event the converter does not model discards the
whole response instead of the single event.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Configure a provider/model that is served through the native OpenAI Responses API (in these packages: two
   different custom provider entries pointing at Responses-capable relays).
2. Start an Agent conversation on that model and send a request that produces a long streamed answer.
3. The turn ends with `unsupported native Responses stream event`; the log shows `native_response_conversion_failed`
   from `agentLoop`, not an upstream HTTP error.

## Expected Behavior

- A stream event that has no mapping should be ignored or passed through, not turned into a terminal error for the
  whole turn; partial text already received should be kept.
- If an event genuinely cannot be represented, the failure should name the event type and be classified as a
  conversion problem the user can act on (change wire API, report the event), not as an unknown error.
- The converter should cover the standard Responses event set, including events that carry no text.

## Relevant Log Output

```text
{"appver":"2.1.6","code":"native_response_conversion_failed","errorMessage":"unsupported native Responses stream event",
 "level":"error","message":"agentLoop error unsupported native Responses stream event","module":"agentLoop","process":"main"}
{"appver":"2.1.6","err":{"code":"native_response_conversion_failed","errorMessage":"unsupported native Responses stream event"},
 "level":"error","message":"Execution loop error","module":"AiStreamManager","process":"main"}
{"appver":"2.1.6","agentSessionId":"<sessionId>","error":{"message":"unsupported native Responses stream event"},
 "level":"warn","message":"Gateway stream failed","module":"ProxyStreamService","process":"main"}
{"appver":"2.1.6","level":"error","message":"AI stream error","module":"useChatWithHistory","process":"renderer",
 "streamError":{"message":"unsupported native Responses stream event"}}
```

Session ids, model/provider ids, absolute paths and conversation content are removed.

## Additional Context

### Impact

- Two packages from two Windows machines on 2.1.6 and 2.1.4, 2026-10-15 to 2026-10-16, covering two different
  Responses-served models through two different custom provider entries. The error repeats many times per package.
- In one package the same conversation also records `Message with id ... not found` (`NOT_FOUND`) errors; that is a
  separate persistence defect and is not what this issue reports.

### Evidence

- The failure is classified by the app itself (`native_response_conversion_failed`), so it happens in Cherry's
  conversion layer between the provider stream and the agent loop, not at the provider.
- Checked against the current `main` (`ab3a0459`, 2026-10-19): a repository-wide search for
  `unsupported native Responses stream event` and `native_response_conversion_failed` returns no hit, so the
  producer is a bundled layer whose source is not in this tree. The closest tracked code is the Responses adapter
  family `src/main/features/apiGateway/adapters/stream/AiSdkToOpenAiResponsesSse.ts` (unknown chunk types are
  silently skipped in the `default` branch) and `src/main/features/apiGateway/adapters/converters/OpenAiResponsesMessageConverter.ts`.
- Searched open and closed issues and pull requests for the error string, the error code and the "Responses stream"
  conversion area: no item covers this failure. #20586 (open) is an auto-aborted Agent stream with a different cause.
- Not confirmed: which specific Responses event type is rejected (the packages do not log the event name), and
  whether it depends on the relay's Responses implementation being newer or older than the one Cherry models.

### Acceptance criteria

- An Agent turn on a native Responses model does not fail because of a single unmapped stream event.
- The skipped or failed event type is logged, and the turn either continues or fails with a named conversion error.
- A regression test feeds the Responses event set, including text-less/metadata events, through the conversion
  layer and asserts the turn still completes.

### Collector note

This issue records an observed failure. It does not mean a fix is approved, implemented or released.

The FAQ entry was not reviewed. Open and closed issues and pull requests were searched for `Input tag 'function'`, `AI_APICallError` tool validation and Anthropic tool `input_schema` conversion; the closest items are listed under Additional Context. GitHub Discussions were not indexed by the available tooling.

## Platform

Windows 11 Home China x64 (win32-x64).

## Version

2.1.6

## Bug Description

A plain chat turn fails before anything is generated:

```text
发生未知错误 (tools.0: Input tag 'function' found using 'type' does not match any of the expected tags:
'bash_20250124', 'browser_toolset_20260801', 'code_execution_20250522', ..., 'web_search_...')
```

The app classifies it as `AI_APICallError` with `invalid_request_error`, and its own request-shape capture shows why:
the outgoing request carries OpenAI chat-completions tool definitions

```text
"tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":...,"description":...,"parameters":{...}}}, ...]
```

while the target is an Anthropic Messages endpoint, whose tool schema accepts only native forms (`custom`,
`web_search_*`, `bash_*`, `text_editor_*`, ...) and expects `name` plus `input_schema` at the top level of a tool.
The request is rejected while it is being validated, so the turn produces no answer and the user sees an English
tag list instead of an actionable message.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Add a provider that serves Anthropic models and select a Claude model from it (in this package: a user-created
   provider entry, model `claude-opus-5-5`, messages enabled with tools).
2. Open a normal chat (not Agent) and send a trivial message.
3. The turn fails with `tools.0: Input tag 'function' found using 'type' does not match any of the expected tags`.

## Expected Behavior

- For an Anthropic endpoint, tool definitions are converted to the native shape (`name`, `description`,
  `input_schema`) before the request is built, whatever internal IR produced them.
- If a provider genuinely cannot take the active tools, the request should be sent without tools or fail with a
  named configuration error that says which provider/model/tool is incompatible.
- The user should never receive a raw schema-tag validation dump as the chat error.

## Relevant Log Output

```text
{"appver":"2.1.6","err":{"data":{"error":{"code":null,"message":"<tool tag validation>","type":"invalid_request_error"}},
 "errorMessage":"tools.0: Input tag 'function' found using 'type' does not match any of the expected tags: ...",
 "errorName":"AI_APICallError","isRetryable":false,
 "requestShape":{"max_tokens":"<redacted>","messages":[{"content":"<string>","role":"system"},{"content":"<string>","role":"user"}],
 "model":"claude-opus-5-5","stream":true,
 "tools":[{"function":"[Truncated]","type":"function"},{"function":"[Truncated]","type":"function"}]}}
{"appver":"2.1.6","level":"error","message":"AI stream error","module":"useChatWithHistory","process":"renderer",
 "streamError":{"message":"tools.0: Input tag 'function' found using 'type' ..."}}
{"appver":"2.1.6","level":"error","message":"Missing key <providerId>","module":"i18n:label","process":"renderer"}
```

Provider ids, session ids, absolute paths and message content are removed.

## Additional Context

### Impact

- One package (Windows 11 Home China x64, 2.1.6, 2026-10-15 to 2026-10-16) fails on the very first message of a
  plain chat, so the affected provider/model is unusable in chat while it stays selectable.
- The same tool-tag error appears in other packages of the same period; only this one carries the app's own
  `requestShape` capture, which is why it is used as the representative record.

### Evidence

- The app itself captured the outgoing body: `tools[0]` is `{"type":"function","function":{...}}`, i.e. the
  OpenAI-compatible shape, on a request whose validation error comes from the Anthropic tool union.
- In `main` at `ab3a0459`, the internal message adapter materialises tool calls in that same OpenAI shape
  (`packages/aiCore/src/core/context/adapter.ts`, `modelMessageAdapter.ts`), and the Anthropic path is expected to
  carry `input_schema` (`src/main/ai/provider/custom/__tests__/boundary/aihubmix.anthropicTools.test.ts`
  asserts `tools[0].input_schema`). No guard in the current tree converts a `{type:"function"}` tool list before an
  Anthropic request is validated.
- Searched open and closed issues and pull requests for the tag names, `Input tag`, and the Anthropic tool-shape
  conversion: #9592 (closed) is the same class of tag error but for a `developer` role message, not for tools;
  #18643 and #18765 are OpenAI-format fields leaking into other dialects. No open issue covers tools reaching an
  Anthropic endpoint in the OpenAI shape.
- Not confirmed: whether the provider was created with the Anthropic API type or with an OpenAI-compatible type
  pointed at an Anthropic relay. The provider label is missing from the app's i18n (`Missing key <providerId>`), so
  the configured type cannot be read from the package, and the second possibility would make this a
  misconfiguration that should still be rejected with a named error.

### Acceptance criteria

- A chat request to an Anthropic endpoint never carries `{"type":"function"}` tool entries.
- A provider/model whose tools cannot be expressed in the target dialect fails with a named, localized error, or
  is sent without tools when the user has not enabled any tool.
- A regression test covers "tool definitions in OpenAI shape + Anthropic target" for a user-created provider.

### Collector note

This issue records an observed failure. It does not mean a fix is approved, implemented or released.

### Issue Checklist

- [x] This is a feature request for `@cherrystudio/file-preview` selection.
- [x] A focused search found no matching request.

_Disclosure: written by an AI agent (Claude Code) for the Cherry Studio Mobile maintainer._

### Feature Description

PPTX selection currently returns only a slide anchor: `slideToPptxAnchor` is documented as "v1 is slide-only". `PptxAnchorSchema` already defines `nodeId`, `paragraph` and `tableCell`, but the renderer never emits them. Tapping any text box therefore selects the whole slide, and the excerpt is the concatenated text of every shape on it.

Please emit shape-level anchors when the tap lands inside a text shape or table cell. That means `nodeId` (`p:cNvPr` id), plus `paragraph` or `tableCell` when they can be resolved, with the excerpt limited to that shape or paragraph.

### Why

Cherry Studio Mobile passes the selection to the Agent as a `selection-ref` for targeted edits. With a slide-only anchor, the Agent has to inspect the slide again and guess which shape the user meant. A device test changed one sentence on a 6-card KPI slide correctly, but the request had to quote the sentence explicitly. A shape-level anchor would remove both the extra inspection and the ambiguity, matching DOCX paragraphs and XLSX ranges, which are already precise.

### Additional context

Mobile edit tools already accept `{ format: "pptx", slide, nodeId, paragraph | tableCell }`, so no consumer change is needed.

### Platform

Windows 11 (as reported).

### Version

2.1.6 (as reported).

### Bug Description

In an Agent conversation that already contains messages, the working-directory control at the top of the conversation (under the composer when the window is narrow) shows the folder icon and the current directory name, but clicking it opens the current directory in File Explorer instead of showing the directory picker. Because the picker never appears, "Add a new working directory" is also unreachable, so the session cannot be moved to another directory.

The same control still opens the picker in a new, empty Agent conversation, and the reported directory exists and is writable, so this does not look like a broken path or a permissions problem. The reporter also notes that earlier builds appeared to allow choosing a new location inside an existing conversation, so the current behaviour may be a regression.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open an Agent conversation that already has at least one message.
2. Click the working-directory control in the conversation header (or under the composer in a narrow window).
3. The app opens File Explorer at the current directory; no directory picker appears.
4. Repeat in a new, empty Agent conversation: the same control opens the picker.

### Expected Behavior

For a conversation that already has messages, the working-directory control should open the directory picker as it does for an empty conversation, and "Add a new working directory" should let the session move there. If moving an existing session is intentionally unsupported, an explicit migration entry for that session's directory would still be needed.

### Relevant Log Output

Not attached: the report describes UI behaviour and no renderer or main-process log was captured with it, so no raw log is included here.

### Additional Context

**Impact** — Desktop, Windows 11, Cherry Studio 2.1.6. One report so far. Reproducible in every Agent conversation that already has messages (the empty-conversation control case works). Effect: an existing conversation cannot be moved to another directory, so the work has to be restarted in a new task.

**Evidence** — Reported behaviour with reproduction steps, plus the empty-conversation control case that points at the UI gating rather than at the directory itself. Checked and not the same item: #20457 (a persisted DSH session rejects a changed working directory at runtime), #21711 (support multiple directories in one Agent workspace, a feature request), #17796 (a project directory address does not refresh in time). No diagnostic package content, personal path or account detail is included here.

**Acceptance criteria** — On Windows 11 with 2.1.6 or a later build: clicking the working-directory control in an Agent conversation that already has messages opens the picker; choosing another directory (including via "Add a new working directory") moves the session; subsequent tool calls resolve paths against the new directory; a new empty conversation keeps its current behaviour.

body_text:
## Problem

With long contexts (50k–250k tokens), the time-to-first-token on self-hosted OpenAI-compatible backends is dominated by **prompt prefill**, which can take minutes. During that time Cherry Studio shows a generic "preparing response" state with no feedback, and users assume the app is stuck.

## What the servers already send

llama.cpp's server (llama-server) and other OpenAI-compatible backends support a streaming prefill progress signal:

- Request: `"return_progress": true` in the `/v1/chat/completions` body (streaming)
- During prefill, the SSE stream contains chunks with:

```json
"prompt_progress": {
  "total": 152340,
  "cache": 0,
  "processed": 9216,
  "time_ms": 12450
}
```

ETA is trivially derivable: `(total - processed) * time_ms / (processed - cache)`.

We verified that gateways such as LiteLLM forward the parameter and pass these chunks through untouched, so the only missing piece is client-side rendering.

## Request

While waiting for the first token, render the prefill progress in the message placeholder — e.g. a progress bar or "Reading the conversation… 62 % (~1 min left)" — when `prompt_progress` chunks are present in the stream. Fallback to the current UI when they are absent (all cloud providers).

This makes long-context local models usable for non-technical users, who currently cannot tell a 3-minute prefill from a hang.

## Environment

- Cherry Studio 2.1.7 (Windows)
- Backend: llama.cpp llama-server behind LiteLLM (OpenAI-compatible)

Thanks for the great app!

## Problem
When a time is converted using chronos [`Local.from_local_datetime(&naive)`](https://docs.rs/chrono/latest/chrono/struct.Local.html#method.from_local_datetime) Function,
a problem occurs at the exact instant of a time-zone change.

Given the IANA Timezone Europe/Berlin, approaching the last hour of daylight saving time,
converting the timestamp:
"25.10.2026 03:00:00" yields `Ambigious("25.10.2026 03:00:00 CEST", "25.10.2026 03:00:00 CET")` 

On the one hand, this is true, since the clock returns from daylight savings at exactly 25.10.2026 03:00:00 CEST.
But practically, digital systems NEVER display a time of "25.10.2026 03:00:00 CEST".
In practice, the clock advances to 02:59:59 CEST, and then jumps directly to 02:00:00 CET.

So, working backwards from a pure "wall-clock time" the current behaviour seems wrong to me.
If a human reads 03:00:00 of a clock and converts it back to a timezone aware date - it would have been in CET.

## Current behaviour
"25.10.2026 02:59:59" -> Ambigous("25.10.2026 02:59:59 CEST", "25.10.2026 02:59:59 CET")
"25.10.2026 03:00:00" -> Ambigous("25.10.2026 03:00:00 CEST", "25.10.2026 03:00:00 CET")
"25.10.2026 03:00:01" -> Single("25.10.2026 03:00:01 CET")

## Expected Behaviour
"25.10.2026 02:59:59" -> Ambigous("25.10.2026 02:59:59 CEST", "25.10.2026 02:59:59 CET")
"25.10.2026 03:00:00" -> **Single**( "25.10.2026 03:00:00 CET")
"25.10.2026 03:00:01" -> Single("25.10.2026 03:00:01 CET")

In our opinion, the 03:00:00 Timestamp no longer belongs to the "double-hour", as we like to call it.

### Please complete the following tasks

- [x] I have searched the [discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [x] I have searched the [open](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/issues) and [rejected](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AS-wont-fix+is%3Aclosed) issues

### Rust Version

rustc 1.97.1 (8bab26f4f 2026-07-14)

### Clap Version

4.6.6 (`main`, af30442)

### Minimal reproducible code

```rust
use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, ArgGroup, Command};

fn main() {
    // A required ARG next to an exclusive flag: the exclusive flag works.
    let arg_case = Command::new("prog")
        .arg(Arg::new("excl").long("excl").exclusive(true).action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("a").long("a").required(true).action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .try_get_matches_from(vec!["prog", "--excl"]);
    println!("ARG-CASE   -> {:?}", arg_case.map(|_| "Ok").map_err(|e| e.kind()));

    // A required GROUP instead of a required arg: the exclusive flag stops working.
    let group_case = Command::new("prog")
        .arg(Arg::new("excl").long("excl").exclusive(true).action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("a").long("a").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("b").long("b").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .group(ArgGroup::new("ab").args(["a", "b"]).required(true))
        .try_get_matches_from(vec!["prog", "--excl"]);
    println!("GROUP-CASE -> {:?}", group_case.map(|_| "Ok").map_err(|e| e.kind()));

    // Following the usage line clap prints for the group case.
    let obey = Command::new("prog")
        .arg(Arg::new("excl").long("excl").exclusive(true).action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("a").long("a").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("b").long("b").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .group(ArgGroup::new("ab").args(["a", "b"]).required(true))
        .try_get_matches_from(vec!["prog", "--excl", "--a"]);
    println!("OBEY-USAGE -> {:?}", obey.map(|_| "Ok").map_err(|e| e.kind()));
}
```

### Steps to reproduce the bug with the above code

`cargo run`

### Actual Behaviour

```
ARG-CASE   -> Ok("Ok")
GROUP-CASE -> Err(MissingRequiredArgument)
OBEY-USAGE -> Err(ArgumentConflict)
```

The error printed for the group case is:

```
error: the following required arguments were not provided:
Usage: prog --excl <--a|--b>
```

That usage line tells the user to pass `--excl` together with one of the group's members, which is exactly what `exclusive(true)` forbids. So no invocation using `--excl` succeeds: alone it is `MissingRequiredArgument`, and with `--a` it is `ArgumentConflict`. The exclusive flag cannot be used at all.

### Expected Behaviour

`GROUP-CASE -> Ok`, matching `ARG-CASE`. An exclusive argument that is present should waive a required group the same way it waives a required arg.

### Additional Context

`Validator::validate_required` computes `is_exclusive_present` once and then consults it in two of the three places that can report something missing:

- `clap_builder/src/parser/validator.rs:247` — the arg branch: `if !is_exclusive_present && !self.is_missing_required_ok(arg, conflicts)`
- `clap_builder/src/parser/validator.rs:313` — the conditionally-required branch: `if !is_exclusive_present && required`
- the group branch in between (roughly `:255`-`:270`) does not consult it at all

`grep -rn is_exclusive_present clap_builder/src/` returns only the definition and those two uses, so the group branch is the odd one out rather than a deliberate exception.

On whether waiving is the intended behaviour at all: #5957 raised the arg case and the conclusion there was that the parser is working correctly and the confusion belonged to the derive layer — so waiving a required arg is intended, which is what makes the group branch look like an oversight.

I do not think this overlaps #6050 (draft, for #4707): that one is about `requires` being bypassed by mutually exclusive groups, a different direction, though it does touch the same function.

Happy to open a PR adding `!is_exclusive_present &&` to the group branch with tests, if that is the fix you would want. I held off because #5957 carries `M-breaking-change` / `S-waiting-on-decision` and this changes when an error is reported, so it seemed worth agreeing on first.

### Debug Output

Not attached — the reproduction above is a plain `try_get_matches_from` on `main`, no debug feature needed. Happy to add `--features debug` output if useful.

That usage line tells the user to pass `--excl` together with one of the group's members, which is exactly what `exclusive(true)` forbids. So no invocation using `--excl` succeeds: alone it is `MissingRequiredArgument`, and with `--a` it is `ArgumentConflict`. The exclusive flag cannot be used at all.

### Expected Behaviour

`GROUP-CASE -> Ok`, matching `ARG-CASE`. An exclusive argument that is present should waive a required group the same way it waives a required arg.

### Additional Context

`Validator::validate_required` computes `is_exclusive_present` once and then consults it in two of the three places that can report something missing:

- `clap_builder/src/parser/validator.rs:247` — the arg branch: `if !is_exclusive_present && !self.is_missing_required_ok(arg, conflicts)`
- `clap_builder/src/parser/validator.rs:313` — the conditionally-required branch: `if !is_exclusive_present && required`
- the group branch in between (roughly `:255`-`:270`) does not consult it at all

`grep -rn is_exclusive_present clap_builder/src/` returns only the definition and those two uses, so the group branch is the odd one out rather than a deliberate exception.

On whether waiving is the intended behaviour at all: #5957 raised the arg case and the conclusion there was that the parser is working correctly and the confusion belonged to the derive layer — so waiving a required arg is intended, which is what makes the group branch look like an oversight.

I do not think this overlaps #6050 (draft, for #4707): that one is about `requires` being bypassed by mutually exclusive groups, a different direction, though it does touch the same function.

Happy to open a PR adding `!is_exclusive_present &&` to the group branch with tests, if that is the fix you would want. I held off because #5957 carries `M-breaking-change` / `S-waiting-on-decision` and this changes when an error is reported, so it seemed worth agreeing on first.

### Debug Output

Not attached — the reproduction above is a plain `try_get_matches_from` on `main`, no debug feature needed. Happy to add `--features debug` output if useful.

### Describe the bug

After a GraphQL rate limit is exhausted and then resets, `gh issue list` (and other subcommands using GraphQL) continues to fail with "API rate limit exceeded" for up to 24 hours. Meanwhile, `gh api graphql` works fine with the same token.

The root cause: `gh` caches a `SearchType` introspection query with `X-Gh-Cache-Ttl: 24h`. When this query is made during rate limit exhaustion, the cached **response** carries `X-Ratelimit-Remaining: 0` in its headers. After the actual rate limit resets (~1 hour), `gh` serves this response from cache and reads the stale rate-limit headers, refusing to make new requests.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Exhaust the GraphQL rate limit (e.g. via automated tooling making many `gh issue list` calls)
2. Wait for the rate limit to reset (~1 hour)
3. Verify the rate limit has reset:
   ```
   $ gh api rate_limit --jq '.resources.graphql'
   {"limit":5000,"remaining":4148,"reset":1772334629,"resource":"graphql","used":852}
   ```
4. Try `gh issue list`:
   ```
   $ gh issue list --repo owner/repo --limit 1 --json number
   GraphQL: API rate limit already exceeded for user ID 477956.
   ```
5. Meanwhile, direct GraphQL works fine:
   ```
   $ gh api graphql -f query='{ viewer { login } rateLimit { remaining } }'
   {"data":{"viewer":{"login":"kim-em"},"rateLimit":{"remaining":4136}}}
   ```

### Evidence from `GH_DEBUG=api`

```
* Request at 2026-03-01 12:15:24 +0000 UTC
* Request to https://api.github.com/graphql
> X-Gh-Cache-Ttl: 24h0m0s          <-- request asks for 24h cache

< HTTP/2.0 200 OK
< Date: Sun, 01 Mar 2026 01:42:54 GMT   <-- response is ~10h old (from cache)
< X-Ratelimit-Remaining: 0              <-- stale! actual remaining is 4148
< X-Ratelimit-Reset: 1772331384
< X-Ratelimit-Used: 5001
```

The response `Date` header (`01:42:54`) is from when the rate limit was exhausted. The request timestamp (`12:15:24`) is current. `gh` is serving the cached response and honoring its stale rate-limit headers.

### Root cause

The `SearchType` introspection query (used internally by `gh issue list` and similar subcommands) is cached with a 24-hour TTL. The rate-limit headers are properties of the request moment, not the response content. When gh serves a cached response, it should not use the cached rate-limit headers to gate new requests.

### Workaround

Delete the cached introspection response:

```sh
# Find and remove cached responses with exhausted rate limits
grep -rl "X-Ratelimit-Remaining: 0" ~/.cache/gh/ 2>/dev/null | xargs rm -f
```

### Expected vs actual behavior

**Expected:** After the rate limit resets, `gh issue list` should work again.
**Actual:** `gh issue list` fails for up to 24 hours after rate limit recovery due to stale cached headers.

### Suggested fix

Either:
1. Strip rate-limit headers when storing responses in cache, or
2. Don't check rate-limit headers when serving from cache, or
3. Include rate-limit state in cache invalidation (evict entries whose `X-Ratelimit-Reset` timestamp has passed)

### gh version

```
gh version 2.83.2 (nixpkgs)
```

### Note

This is likely the root cause of many reports in #8321, where users see "rate limit exceeded" while `gh api /rate_limit` shows plenty of remaining quota. That issue was closed without identifying the caching mechanism.

## Describe the bug

`gh skill search` and `gh skill install` from remote repos rely on the GitHub API (Code Search API for search, and repo content API for install). The standard authenticated API rate limit for personal accounts is 5,000 requests per hour. However, in practice, the rate limit is hit almost immediately when using `gh skill`, making the entire feature unusable for skill discovery and management.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run `gh skill search agent-browser --limit 5`
2. Run a second search for a different skill name
3. Already hit the rate limit:

```
GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please wait a minute and try again.
```

## Expected behavior

`gh skill` should be able to perform multiple searches and installs without immediately exhausting the rate limit. Possible improvements:

1. **Client-side caching**: Cache search results and repository tree traversals locally with a reasonable TTL
2. **Reduced API calls**: Each `gh skill install` from a remote repo does a full tree traversal — this could be optimized
3. **Batching**: Allow installing multiple skills from the same repo in a single API call
4. **Rate limit awareness**: Display remaining rate limit before operations and warn the user, or automatically wait/retry with backoff
5. **Offline-first metadata**: Ship or support a community-maintained skill registry/index to reduce search API dependency

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- gh version: latest
- Account type: personal (5,000 requests/hr limit)

## Additional context

This is particularly problematic because the `gh skill` feature was announced as a major workflow improvement (https://github.blog/changelog/2026-04-16-manage-agent-skills-with-github-cli/), but in practice users can barely do 1-2 operations before getting rate-limited, making it effectively a non-functional feature for managing multiple skills.

<details>
<summary>What is a No-Op?</summary>

A no-op (no operation) occurs when an agentic workflow runs successfully but determines that no action is required. For example:
- A security scanner that finds no issues
- An update checker that finds nothing to update
- A monitoring workflow that finds everything is healthy

These are successful outcomes, not failures, and help provide transparency into workflow behavior.

</details>

<details>
<summary>How This Helps</summary>

This issue helps you:
- Track workflows that ran but determined no action was needed
- Distinguish between failures and intentional no-ops
- Monitor workflow health by seeing when workflows decide not to act

## 🐛 Bug Report

When running `gh issue create ... --assignee <USER>` and the assignee fails (e.g., due to permissions), the command returns an error BUT the issue is already created.

## 📋 Scenario

```bash
gh issue create --title 'Test' --body 'Body' --assignee hugom97
# Output: Error: isramontoro doesn't have the correct permissions...
```

**What happens:**
- Issue IS created (e.g., #5501)
- User sees only the error about assignment
- If user retries, creates duplicate issue (#5502)

## 🎯 Expected behavior

When creating an issue with a failed assignment, the CLI should either:
1. **Option A:** Show clear success message + assignment error separately
   - ✅ Issue created: https://github.com/...#5501
   - ❌ Assignment failed: Permission denied

2. **Option B:** Rollback issue creation if assignment fails (atomic operation)

3. **Option C:** Separate the operations so assignment doesn't block creation output

## 🔧 Current behavior

Error output hides the fact that issue was created, causing users to retry and create duplicates.

body_text:
### Describe the bug

`gh pr checks` reports a re-queued check run with the conclusion of the run it replaced, and exits 0, while the new run is still queued.

`eliminateDuplicates` in `pkg/cmd/pr/checks/aggregate.go` keeps the newest entry per check by sorting on `StartedAt` descending. A check run that has not started yet has no `startedAt`, so its `StartedAt` is the zero time, which sorts as the *oldest* entry. The completed run it supersedes wins the deduplication and its conclusion is reported.

### Affected version

Built from trunk at 0d121e8c (2026-09-05); the logic is unchanged in the current release.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. On a PR with a completed check run, re-run that check so a new run is queued but has not started.
2. Run `gh pr checks <pr>` while the new run is queued.
3. The old run's conclusion is shown and the command exits 0.

A driver that feeds `eliminateDuplicates` a completed run and a queued re-run of the same check (queued run: `startedAt` unset) returns the completed run:

```

error: <nil>
```

With the queued entry ranked first (a stable sort that puts zero `StartedAt` values ahead, then newest first) the same input returns:

```
build pending
error: PendingError
```

A fix with that ordering and a table case in `TestEliminateDuplicates` is ready; happy to open the PR if this is labelled help wanted.

body_text:
### Describe the bug

After migrating from GitHub.com to GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency (`<tenant>.ghe.com`), an existing GitHub Actions release workflow fails because `gh` does not recognise the repository's remote as a known GitHub host.

The workflow supplies `GH_TOKEN` using `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`:

```yaml
- name: Create GitHub Release
  env:
    GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
  run: gh release create "${TAG}" --generate-notes
```

 The checkout's remote points to `https://<tenant>.ghe.com/<owner>/<repo>`, but `gh release create` asks me to run `gh auth login`.

Explicitly setting the repository fixes the problem:

```yaml
env:
  GH_REPO: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}
```

### Affected version

`gh version 2.98.0 (2026-08-20)`

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Use a repository on GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency (`<tenant>.ghe.com`).
2. Run the following workflow by pushing a version tag.
3. Observe that the `gh release create` step fails.

```yaml
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+"

permissions: {}

jobs:
  gh-release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    permissions:
      contents: write

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Create GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: gh release create "${TAG}" --generate-notes
```

### Expected vs actual behavior

Expected: `gh` recognises the `*.ghe.com` remote as a GitHub host, infers the repository from the checkout, and creates the release using `GH_TOKEN`, without requiring `GH_HOST`, `GH_REPO`, or an interactive login.

Actual: remote resolution fails with the error below. The same workflow worked on GitHub.com, and explicitly setting `GH_REPO` makes it work on the data-residency instance.

### Logs

```text
none of the git remotes configured for this repository point to a known GitHub host. To tell gh about a new GitHub host, please use `gh auth login`
```

### Describe the bug

`gh pr merge <PR-URL> --delete-branch` runs its local cleanup in the repository of the **current working directory**, even when that repository is not the one the PR belongs to. It matches the head branch by **name only**. If a linked worktree there has a branch with the same name checked out, gh removes that worktree and force-deletes the branch. The branch and worktree belong to an unrelated repository.

`git worktree remove` (without `--force`) only refuses uncommitted changes, so a clean worktree whose branch holds **unpushed commits** is removed. `git branch -D` then leaves those commits reachable only from the reflog, so the work is effectively lost.

Version: `gh version 2.100.0 (2026-09-03)`, macOS.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Repo A (`owner-a/repo-a`) has an open PR whose head branch is `feature-x`.
2. An unrelated local repo B, whose remote is a different GitHub repository, has a linked worktree with its own branch also named `feature-x`. That branch holds a commit that has not been pushed.
3. With the cwd anywhere inside repo B, run:
   `gh pr merge https://github.com/owner-a/repo-a/pull/N --merge --delete-branch`
4. The PR in repo A merges and its remote branch is deleted, as expected. **In addition**, gh removes repo B's worktree and deletes repo B's local `feature-x`. The unpushed commit is no longer reachable from any ref. A process running in that worktree (a build, in our case) was also broken.

### Where it comes from (v2.100.0 source)

- `pkg/cmd/pr/merge/merge.go:124`: `opts.CanDeleteLocalBranch = !cmd.Flags().Changed("repo")`. A URL selector does not set `--repo`, so local cleanup stays enabled.
- `merge.go:594`: `localBranchExists: opts.CanDeleteLocalBranch && opts.GitClient.HasLocalBranch(ctx, pr.HeadRefName)`. This is evaluated in the cwd's repo, by name, and nothing checks that the cwd's repo is the PR's repository.
- `merge.go:494-504`: if the branch is checked out in another linked worktree, gh calls `WorktreeRemove` and then `DeleteLocalBranch` (`git branch -D`). This worktree handling appears to have come in with #13380.

Passing `--repo` avoids it, because `CanDeleteLocalBranch` becomes false, and the remote branch is still deleted.

### Expected behavior

Local cleanup should only touch a repository whose remote actually is the PR's base (or head) repository. For example, skip local cleanup unless one of the cwd repo's remotes resolves to the PR's repo, and/or unless the local branch's upstream tracks the PR's head repo and branch.

Independently, gh should not remove a worktree, or force-delete a branch, whose tip has commits that are not on the PR head (the merged commit). A safe check is that the local tip is equal to, or an ancestor of, `headRefOid`; otherwise, skip and warn. `git branch -D` bypasses git's own merged check, so this is the only guard.

### Additional context

This mostly bites people who work across several repos with a shared branch-naming convention (e.g. tooling that names branches `claude/<topic>`), or who merge a PR by URL from whichever repo their shell happens to be in. Nothing in the output hints that a different repository was touched: gh prints `Removed worktree <path>` and `Deleted local branch <name>`, and the path belongs to the other repo.

### Describe the bug

`gh release list -R https://github.com/cli/cli/` gives back:

```
non-200 OK status code: 401 Unauthorized body: "{\r\n  \"message\": \"Requires authentication\",\r\n  \"documentation_url\": \"https://docs.github.com/rest\",\r\n  \"status\": \"401\"\r\n}"
```
Instead of listing available releases.

### Affected version

```
gh version 2.102.0 (2026-09-30)
https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v2.102.0
```

Running on
```
DISTRIB_ID=Ubuntu
DISTRIB_RELEASE=26.04
DISTRIB_CODENAME=resolute
DISTRIB_DESCRIPTION="Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS"
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Download `gh` using any browser from "https://github.com/cli/cli/release"
2. Install `gh` using `dpkg -i gh_2.102.0_linux_amd64.deb`
3. Try `gh release list -R https://github.com/cli/cli/`

### Expected vs actual behavior

Show list of available releases.

### Logs

```
$ GH_DEBUG=api gh release list -R https://github.com/cli/cli/
* Request at 2026-10-06 11:11:31.899403718 +0200 CEST m=+0.078085442
* Request to https://api.github.com/graphql
> POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.github.com
> Accept: application/vnd.github.merge-info-preview+json, application/vnd.github.nebula-preview
> Authorization: 
> Content-Length: 83
> Content-Type: application/json
> Graphql-Features: merge_queue
> Time-Zone: Europe/Berlin
> User-Agent: GitHub CLI 2.102.0
> X-Gh-Cache-Ttl: 24h0m0s
> X-Github-Api-Version: 2022-11-28

{

body_text:
### Describe the bug

`gh skill update --help` says that `--force` refreshes locally modified skill files but “does not remove extra files added locally.” On 2.102.0, applying an update replaces all contents of the installed skill directory, deleting locally added files. This also happens during a version update without `--force`.

A user relying on that sentence can lose notes or scripts they added to a skill directory. The documented `--force --all` example describes restoring modified files without explaining that additional files are discarded.

### Affected version

```text
gh version 2.102.0 (2026-09-30)
https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v2.102.0
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

```sh
dir=$(mktemp -d)
gh skill install cli/cli gh --dir "$dir"
echo notes > "$dir/gh/LOCAL-NOTES.md"
gh skill update gh --dir "$dir" --force --all
ls "$dir/gh"
```

A version update reproduces this without `--force`: install `gh` with `--pin v2.100.0`, add `LOCAL-NOTES.md`, then run `gh skill update gh --dir "$dir" --unpin --all`.

### Expected vs actual behavior

Expected from the help: `LOCAL-NOTES.md` remains alongside the refreshed `SKILL.md`.

Actual: `LOCAL-NOTES.md` is deleted; only `SKILL.md` remains in this reproduction.

#13449 explicitly made stale-file removal part of an in-place update, and [the update test requires a locally planted file to disappear](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/fc4b137cdef0a6bd28fd461b7cf9c84a5812a8cd/pkg/cmd/skills/update/update_test.go#L730-L780). However, [the help still promises to keep extra local files](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/fc4b137cdef0a6bd28fd461b7cf9c84a5812a8cd/pkg/cmd/skills/update/update.go#L98-L100).

Please correct the help to explain that applying any update replaces the installed directory's contents with the upstream skill, discarding local modifications and additional files. The `--force` description should separately explain that it also applies this replacement when the upstream version has not changed.

### Logs

```text
$ gh skill update gh --dir "$dir" --force --all
1 update(s) available:
  • gh (cli/cli) a4791f98 (reinstall) [v2.102.0]

Updated gh
$ ls "$dir/gh"
SKILL.md
```

body_text:
### Describe the bug

`gh issue create --type <name>` creates the issue **first** and resolves the type name **afterwards**. When the type does not exist — which is always the case on user-owned repositories, because issue types are an organization feature (`repository.issueTypes` is `null`) — the command exits with status 1 and `type "Bug" not found; available types: ` **after the issue was already created, and without printing its URL**.

Scripts (and AI agents) reasonably read exit code 1 as "nothing was created" and retry, which creates **duplicate issues**. This is what happened in our automation: https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3326 (duplicates https://github.com/konard/medical-neural-network-ml/issues/3 and #4).

Source at `819f972` (`pkg/cmd/issue/create/create.go`):

https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/819f972eff771d5ec433c8d03c369cc43f1eab49/pkg/cmd/issue/create/create.go#L481-L496

`deferredUpdateIssueOptions` → `issueShared.ResolveIssueTypeName` (https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/819f972eff771d5ec433c8d03c369cc43f1eab49/pkg/cmd/issue/shared/lookup.go#L233-L248) runs only after `api.IssueCreate`. The existing unit test "create with type not found" (`create_test.go` L908) even stubs `mutation IssueCreate` before `query RepositoryIssueTypes`, i.e. it pins this behaviour.

This is a sibling of #13804 (permission error on the deferred `UpdateIssueIssueType`) and #14367 (`--assignee`). Note that #13899 keeps `type "X" not found` fatal on the premise that it "runs before any mutation" — per the code above it runs after `createIssue`, so #13899 would not fix this case.

### Affected version

gh version 2.102.0 (also present on `trunk` at 819f972).

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

On any repository owned by a **user** (not an organization):

```bash
gh issue create --repo <user>/<repo> --title "type repro" --body "type repro" --type Bug
echo "exit code: $?"
# type "Bug" not found; available types:
# exit code: 1
gh issue list --repo <user>/<repo> --search "type repro in:title"
# -> the issue exists
```

The same happens on an organization repository with a misspelled type (`--type Bugz`).

### Expected vs actual behavior

Expected (either):
1. Resolve `--type` **before** `api.IssueCreate` (the name → ID lookup needs no issue), so an unknown type fails without side effects; or
2. If the issue was already created, print its URL to stdout and report the type problem as a warning on stderr (like #13899 does for the deferred mutation), or at least include the URL in the error.

Actual: issue created, URL not printed, exit status 1.

### Workaround

Before calling `gh issue create --type`, query
`gh api graphql -f query='query($o:String!,$n:String!){repository(owner:$o,name:$n){issueTypes(first:100){nodes{name}}}}' -F o=OWNER -F n=REPO`
and drop `--type` when the name is not listed (`issueTypes` is `null` for user-owned repositories). After any failure, look up a just-created issue with the same title/body before retrying.

### Suggested fix

In `createRun`, call `deferredUpdateIssueOptions` (or at least `ResolveIssueTypeName`) before `api.IssueCreate` and pass the resolved ID afterwards; and/or print `newIssue.URL` before running deferred updates. Happy to help with a PR.

{"repository": "cli/cli", "task_candidate_id": 3173, "repository_id": 61, "issue_number": 14703, "github_issue_id": 5867107090, "html_url": "https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/14703", "created_at": "2026-10-15T13:31:49+00:00", "author_association": null, "title": "`gh issue create --type` creates the issue, then exits 1 with `type "X" not found` without printing its URL (causes duplicates on retry)", "body_text": "### Describe the bug

`gh issue create --type <name>` creates the issue **first** and resolves the type name **afterwards**. When the type does not exist — which is always the case on user-owned repositories, because issue types are an organization feature (`repository.issueTypes` is `null`) — the command exits with status 1 and `type "Bug" not found; available types: ` **after the issue was already created, and without printing its URL**.

Scripts (and AI agents) reasonably read exit code 1 as "nothing was created" and retry, which creates **duplicate issues**. This is what happened in our automation: https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3326 (duplicates https://github.com/konard/medical-neural-network-ml/issues/3 and #4).

Source at `819f972` (`pkg/cmd/issue/create/create.go`):

https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/819f972eff771d5ec433c8d03c369cc43f1eab49/pkg/cmd/issue/create/create.go#L481-L496

`deferredUpdateIssueOptions` → `issueShared.ResolveIssueTypeName` (https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/819f972eff771d5ec433c8d03c369cc43f1eab49/pkg/cmd/issue/shared/lookup.go#L233-L248) runs only after `api.IssueCreate`. The existing unit test "create with type not found" (`create_test.go` L908) even stubs `mutation IssueCreate` before `query RepositoryIssueTypes`, i.e. it pins this behaviour.

This is a sibling of #13804 (permission error on the deferred `UpdateIssueIssueType`) and #14367 (`--assignee`). Note that #13899 keeps `type "X" not found` fatal on the premise that it "runs before any mutation" — per the code above it runs after `createIssue`, so #13899 would not fix this case.

### Affected version

gh version 2.102.0 (also present on `trunk` at 819f972).

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

On any repository owned by a **user** (not an organization):

```bash
gh issue create --repo <user>/<repo> --title "type repro" --body "type repro" --type Bug
echo "exit code: $?"
# type "Bug" not found; available types:
# exit code: 1
gh issue list --repo <user>/<repo> --search "type repro in:title"
# -> the issue exists
```

The same happens on an organization repository with a misspelled type (`--type Bugz`).

### Expected vs actual behavior

Expected (either):
1. Resolve `--type` **before** `api.IssueCreate` (the name → ID lookup needs no issue), so an unknown type fails without side effects; or
2. If the issue was already created, print its URL to stdout and report the type problem as a warning on stderr (like #13899 does for the deferred mutation), or at least include the URL in the error.

Actual: issue created, URL not printed, exit status 1.

### Workaround

Before calling `gh issue create --type`, query
`gh api graphql -f query='query($o:String!,$n:String!){repository(owner:$o,name:$n){issueTypes(first:100){nodes{name}}}}' -F o=OWNER -F n=REPO`
and drop `--type` when the name is not listed (`issueTypes` is `null` for user-owned repositories). After any failure, look up a just-created issue with the same title/body before retrying.

### Suggested fix

In `createRun`, call `deferredUpdateIssueOptions` (or at least `ResolveIssueTypeName`) before `api.IssueCreate` and pass the resolved ID afterwards; and/or print `newIssue.URL` before running deferred updates. Happy to help with a PR.

### Describe the bug

Two help texts tell users to use flags that the commands do not define:

1. `gh ruleset view --help` has this example:

   ```
   # Interactively choose a ruleset to view from only rulesets configured in the current repository
   $ gh ruleset view --no-parents
   ```

   The command has only a boolean `-p, --parents` flag (default `true`). Cobra does not generate `--no-<flag>` forms, so the example fails with `unknown flag: --no-parents`. The way to turn the flag off is `--parents=false`.

2. `gh search issues --help` and `gh search prs --help` say:

   > On supported GitHub hosts, advanced issue search syntax can be used in the `--search` query.

   These commands take the query as positional arguments and have no `--search` flag. The sentence appears to come from `gh issue list` and `gh pr list`, which do have `--search`. The rest of the paragraph (pass `OR`/`AND` and parentheses as separate arguments) describes positional arguments and is correct.

### Affected version

```
gh version 2.102.0 (2026-09-30)
https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v2.102.0
```

The same text is on `trunk` (`pkg/cmd/ruleset/view/view.go`, `pkg/cmd/search/issues/issues.go`, `pkg/cmd/search/prs/prs.go`).

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

```console
$ gh ruleset view --no-parents -R cli/cli
unknown flag: --no-parents
(usage follows, exit status 1)

$ gh ruleset view 4898070 -R cli/cli --parents=false
Copilot Code Review
ID: 4898070
Source: cli/cli (Repository)
...

$ gh search issues --search 'label:bug OR label:enhancement' --repo cli/cli
unknown flag: --search

$ gh search issues --repo cli/cli --state open '(' label:gh-ruleset OR label:gh-attestation ')'
(returns results)

$ gh search issues --repo cli/cli --state open '(label:gh-ruleset OR label:gh-attestation)'
Invalid search query "( (label:\"gh-ruleset OR label:gh-attestation)\" ) repo:cli/cli state:open type:issue".
The search query contains invalid syntax.
```

The last two commands show that the "separate arguments" advice is right. Only the reference to a `--search` flag is wrong.

### Expected vs actual behavior

Expected: the examples and descriptions in `--help` use flags that the command accepts.
Actual: copying `gh ruleset view --no-parents` gives an error. `gh search issues/prs --help` points to a `--search` flag that does not exist.

### Suggested fix

- `gh ruleset view`: change the example to `gh ruleset view --parents=false`.
- `gh search issues` / `gh search prs`: change "can be used in the `--search` query" to "can be used in the search query".

I have this three-line change ready and can open a pull request if this gets the `help wanted` label.

### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

Skills under the supported `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` convention can be previewed and installed with `--allow-hidden-dirs`, but `gh skill search` has no equivalent opt-in. This leaves a publisher using a normal project-local agent layout dependent on users already knowing the repository and exact path.

With `gh version 2.97.0 (2026-07-31)`, I ran this scoped search and got `[]`:

```sh
gh skill search gooo --owner kimjooyoon --limit 5 \
  --json repo,skillName,path,description,namespace
```

An exact pinned preview succeeded, and a project-scope installation subsequently listed the same commit with `pinned: true`:

```sh
gh skill preview kimjooyoon/gooo-go-ports \
  .agents/skills/gooo-first-program@9ac1f5786999be9affec14bd4dc73ce3fc3e97f0 \
  --allow-hidden-dirs
```

The empty search result alone does not establish GitHub indexing status. Separately, the current released [v2.102.0 search parser](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/v2.102.0/pkg/cmd/skills/search/search.go#L873) calls `discovery.MatchSkillPath`. That [matcher](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/v2.102.0/internal/skills/discovery/discovery.go#L407) uses `matchSkillConventions`, which excludes dot-prefixed segments; hidden conventions are handled by a separate matcher. Thus this client path cannot retain such a hit even if Code Search returns it. I inspected the v2.102.0 source but did not run that binary.

### Proposed solution

Would an explicit `gh skill search --allow-hidden-dirs`, matching preview/install, fit the intended trust policy? Keeping the default unchanged would preserve the existing opt-in boundary. If exclusion from search is intentional, documenting that limitation would also help publishers avoid duplicating skill directories unnecessarily.

### Additional context

#13876 and draft #13894 concern arbitrary **non-hidden** nested layouts; I believe this request is separate from that expansion. I searched existing issues for the search command and flag but may have missed a related discussion.

This is a request for policy/acceptance clarification, not an implementation PR or a claim that installing a skill verifies its safety. Prepared with AI assistance; the reported preview, search and project installation were actually run.

## Summary

`gh auth login --with-token` advertises a minimum scope set that it does not
enforce: the flow prints "The minimum required scopes are 'repo', 'read:org',
'workflow'", but the login completes successfully with a token that carries no
`workflow` scope.

## Environment

- `gh` 2.102.0 (2026-09-30)
- Linux x86_64
- Classic PAT (not fine-grained)

## Reproduction

1. Create a classic personal access token with the scopes `repo`, `read:org`
   and `read:project`. Do **not** grant `workflow`.
2. Run `gh auth login --hostname github.com --with-token` and paste the token
   at the prompt.
3. The login completes without an error.
4. Run `gh auth status`. It reports:
   `- Token scopes: 'read:org', 'read:project', 'repo'`

## Expected

Either the pasted token is rejected because it lacks the advertised
`workflow` scope, or the hint lists only the scopes that are actually
required.

## Actual

The token is accepted, and the advertised `workflow` scope is never checked.
The stored credential works for API calls while lacking a scope the flow
claimed to require.

## Additional Context

- The hint is printed by the paste-token flow. The browser (OAuth) flow
  requests a different scope set, so the two flows do not agree on what
  "minimum" means.
- Not verified whether the missing check is intentional, or whether the hint
  is simply a copy of the OAuth scope set.
- Relevant to any setup that treats the printed scopes as an enforced
  contract rather than a suggestion.

body_text:
This was drafted by AI from my prompts and corrections. I've kept some details I'm not personally qualified to vouch for — several of the use cases especially — on the chance they're on point and useful; feel free to discount them. I do vouch for the overall thrust and most of the specifics. (Disclosure: I maintain the zodexy fork and json-schema-to-zodexy.)

----

## TL;DR

Zod has no standard, lossless, language-neutral way to represent a schema as data. The community keeps rebuilding one, most notably [`zodex`](https://github.com/commonbaseapp/zodex) (and its Zod 4 fork [`zodexy`](https://github.com/brettz9/zodexy)). These projects are good, but each lives outside Zod, tracks Zod's internals by hand, and risks silent breakage on every release.

I'd like to ask the maintainers to consider giving Zod a *formal* serialization format: either a small spec maintained under the Zod org, an official companion package, or at minimum a documented pointer to a recommended implementation and a commitment to keep the introspection surface it depends on stable.

## What exists today

- **`z.toJSONSchema()`** (Zod 4) converts a schema to JSON Schema. It is
  one-directional and deliberately lossy.
- **`z.core.$ZodType["_zod"].def`** and the global registry expose a schema's
  structure at runtime. This is powerful but is not a stable, documented
  contract, so tools that read it break on minor versions.
- **`zodex` / `zodexy`** serialize a schema to compact JSON and deserialize it
  back to a working Zod schema, with the TypeScript types round-tripping too.

## The gap

There is no supported answer to: *"Take this schema, turn it into JSON, store or
send it, and reconstruct the same schema (and the same static type) elsewhere."*

Concrete cases that need this:

- **Server-defined, client-consumed schemas** without shipping the server's code
  to the client (form rendering, client-side validation, API discovery).
- **Schemas stored in a database** — user-defined forms, CMS field configs,
  low-code builders, rule engines.
- **Schemas sent over the wire** — RPC contracts, config services, plugin
  manifests.
- **Cross-language consumers** — a Python, Go, or Rust service validating
  against a schema authored in Zod.
- **Structured-clone data** — values crossing `postMessage` (workers, iframes,
  `MessageChannel`) or stored in IndexedDB, where the payload can carry `Date`,
  `Map`, `Set`, `ArrayBuffer`, `File` / `Blob`, and `BigInt` that a JSON-only
  schema language cannot describe. These *can* be
  forced into JSON, but there is no standard encoding for them and nothing in
  the result signals that the original values were of those types. A schema format
  that can describe them serves double duty: it validates the payload and tells
  consumers how to rehydrate it."
- **Tooling** — visual editors, schema diffing, documentation generators, a
  shareable schema registry.
- **Build-time snapshots and caching** of generated schemas.
- **AI / codegen** — a canonical, compact target format for a model to read or
  emit, instead of ad-hoc prompt encodings.

Today each of these is solved privately, incompatibly, and fragilely.

## Why JSON Schema doesn't close the gap

`z.toJSONSchema()` is valuable and should stay. But JSON Schema solves a
different problem — *validating a JSON document* — and using it as the
serialization of *a Zod schema* fails in specific, unavoidable ways.

### It is one-directional, by design

- **No official inverse.** There is no `z.fromJSONSchema()`, and a faithful
  general one is not possible.
- **`z.toJSONSchema()` is explicitly lossy.** For anything it cannot express it
  either throws or emits a placeholder (`{}` / an override). That is documented
  behavior, not a bug — but it means the output is not a complete record of the
  schema.
- **The mapping is many-to-many.** Different Zod schemas produce the same JSON
  Schema, and most JSON Schemas correspond to no Zod schema at all, so there is
  nothing to invert unambiguously.

### It cannot represent much of Zod's surface

*Pipeline / effect constructs — no JSON Schema equivalent at all:*

- `.transform()`, `.pipe()`, `.preprocess()`, and `z.codec()` — JSON Schema has
  no notion of transforming a value.
- `.catch()` — a fallback value on validation failure — has no equivalent.
- `.default()` — JSON Schema's `default` is a non-normative annotation that
  validators do not apply; Zod actually substitutes the value.
- Coercion (`z.coerce.*`, `z.stringbool()`) — JSON Schema validates, it does not
  coerce.

*Input vs. output types:* transforms, pipes, codecs, defaults, and coercion make
a Zod schema's input type differ from its output type. JSON Schema describes one
document shape and cannot carry both.

*Non-JSON runtime values:* `z.date()` (an actual `Date`), `z.bigint()`,
`z.map()`, `z.set()`, `z.symbol()`, `z.file()`, `z.instanceof()`, `z.function()`,
`z.promise()`, `z.nan()`, `z.undefined()`, `z.void()` — JSON Schema only
describes JSON, so these have no home.

*Arbitrary logic:* `.refine()`, `.check()`, `.superRefine()` are predicates.
JSON Schema cannot express general logic, and `format` is advisory only.

*TypeScript-level information:* `.brand()` (nominal typing) and `.readonly()`
exist only in the type system and vanish.

*Diagnostics:* custom error messages, error maps, and localization keys have
nowhere to live in JSON Schema.

*Structural details that degrade:* discriminated unions collapse to `anyOf`
(`discriminator` is an OpenAPI extension and non-normative); object modes
(`strict` / `strip` / `passthrough` / `catchall`) partially map to
`additionalProperties`; tuple rest elements, `z.record()` key schemas, enums vs.
`const`, and template-literal types all lose information.

### It adds its own ambiguity

- **Dialect drift.** JSON Schema has many draft versions (Draft-07,
  2019-09, 2020-12, …). `z.toJSONSchema()` targets a subset of one, and every
  consumer must agree on the dialect.
- **Wrong problem shape.** A serialized Zod schema must reconstruct a *schema
  object* — methods, static types, effects, registry links — not just describe
  data. JSON Schema was never meant to round-trip into a program.

### They are complementary, not competing

JSON Schema remains the right tool for interop with non-Zod consumers. A
serialized-Zod format is the right tool for exact round-trips. A blessed format
does not replace `z.toJSONSchema()`; it covers the case `z.toJSONSchema()`
explicitly does not.

## Prior art: `zodex` / `zodexy`

`zodex` already demonstrates that the hard parts are solvable:

- A compact, human-readable JSON encoding whose `type` names mirror Zod's.
- **Type-level round-tripping**: `zerialize` / `dezerialize` are type-safe, so
  the reconstructed schema has the original static type.
- **Inlined modifiers and checks** (`isOptional`, `isNullable`, `defaultValue`,
  `min`, `max`, …) for readability instead of deep wrapper nesting.
- **Local and recursive references** via JSON Reference (`$ref`).
- **Named registries** for the parts that genuinely cannot be serialized —
  errors, checks, transforms, codecs, `instanceof` constructors — turning silent
  data loss into an explicit, opt-in extension point.
- A **self-describing document** with a schema-URI mechanism
  (`$zodexySchema`) for versioned dialects and constrained profiles. `zodexy`
  ships a machine-readable schema-for-schemas
  ([`schema.zodexy.json`](https://github.com/brettz9/zodexy/blob/main/lib/schema.zodexy.json)).
- **Documented, bounded caveats** (`brand` omitted; `refine`/`custom` treated as
  `check`; `catch` with a function not restorable).

`zodexy` is a fork that exists only because `zodex` had not yet been updated for
Zod 4 — which is exactly the maintenance risk a blessed format would remove.
There are already downstream projects (e.g.
[`json-schema-to-zodexy`](https://github.com/brettz9/json-schema-to-zodexy))
that would benefit from a stable target.

## What "blessing" could look like

From lowest to highest commitment — any one of these would help:

1. **Documentation pointer.** Name a recommended serialization approach in the
   Zod docs, the way other ecosystem tools are referenced.
2. **A versioned spec under the Zod org.** A short specification document plus a
   schema-for-schemas and a conformance test suite. Implementations in any
   language can then claim conformance. Stays out of core.
3. **An official companion package.** Ship `zerialize` / `dezerialize` (or
   `z.toSerialized()` / `z.fromSerialized()`) as `@zod/serialize`, released in
   lockstep with Zod so it never lags a release.
4. **A stable introspection contract.** Whatever option is chosen, commit to a
   documented, versioned surface (building on `_zod.def` and the registry) that
   a serializer can depend on without breaking on patch releases.

## Benefits to Zod itself

- One well-tested implementation instead of many partial ones.
- Fewer bug reports and less pressure to keep undocumented internals frozen.
- A foundation for an official schema-sharing / registry story.
- A better AI and codegen story: a single canonical format to target.
- Makes Zod-compatible validators in other languages realistic.

## Anticipated objections

- **"Just use JSON Schema."** Covered above — it is lossy and one-directional,
  and the two formats serve different purposes.
- **"Maintenance burden."** A community-maintained package or spec with an
  official blessing and a conformance suite spreads the load; the format only
  has to track Zod's *public surface*, which changes far less than its
  internals.
- **"The format will churn as Zod evolves."** Versioned dialects and a
  `$schema`-style identifier (already in `zodexy`) exist precisely for
  this; changes can be additive.
- **"This belongs in userland."** It can stay in userland — the ask is an
  official pointer and a stable target, not core integration.

## Precedent

Mature schema ecosystems converge on a serialized, language-neutral form:
GraphQL SDL plus introspection, Protobuf's `FileDescriptorProto`, OpenAPI, and
JSON Schema itself. Zod is now large enough to warrant one.

## The ask

1. Is the Zod team open to an officially recognized serialization format?
2. If so, which shape is preferable — docs pointer, org-hosted spec, companion
   package, or a documented stable introspection contract?
3. Would you accept `zodex` / `zodexy` as the starting point, or is there a
   different direction you'd want?

Happy to help with a spec draft, a conformance suite, or migrating an
implementation under the org.
