https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/security#17-validate-the-sender-of-all-ipc-messages

> ## 17. Validate the sender of all IPC messages
> You should always validate incoming IPC messages sender property to ensure you aren't performing actions or sending information to untrusted renderers.
>
> ### Why?
> All Web Frames can in theory send IPC messages to the main process, including iframes and child windows in some scenarios. If you have an IPC message that returns user data to the sender via event.reply or performs privileged actions that the renderer can't natively, you should ensure you aren't listening to third party web frames.
> 
> You should be validating the sender of all IPC messages by default.

*Written by AI (Claude Fable 5.1), reviewed by Gideon Wald before filing. Everything below was run on the
official 2.9.6 release binary and on the official canary build of `main` (2.9.6+057a3da), on
macOS 26.6 (aarch64) and on Linux aarch64 (the `denoland/deno:2.9.6` Docker image); the output
is copied from those runs.*

Version: Deno 2.9.6 (release) and `main` at 057a3da (canary). First seen on 2.9.4.

## What happens

A native `WebSocket` client sends one 4 MiB binary message over `wss:` to a server that reads
slowly. `bufferedAmount` drops to 0, which per the spec means every byte has been handed to the
network. The server, still reading, stops receiving about 56 or 72 KB short of the end of the
message and never gets the rest: the connection stays open and nothing more arrives. As soon as
the client sends *any* further message, the missing bytes arrive, followed by that message.

We hit this in production with ~160 KB messages: the client waits forever for a reply to a
message the server never fully received.

## Reproduction

`server.ts`: a raw TLS listener that does the WebSocket handshake by hand, then reads 16 KiB at
a time with a 1 ms pause and prints how many bytes it has received so far:

```ts
// Raw TLS server that accepts one WebSocket connection by hand and reads it slowly.
const listener = Deno.listenTls({ port: 8443, cert: Deno.readTextFileSync("cert.pem"), key: Deno.readTextFileSync("key.pem") });
const conn = await listener.accept();
const buf = new Uint8Array(1 << 16);
const request = new TextDecoder().decode(buf.subarray(0, (await conn.read(buf))!));
const key = request.match(/Sec-WebSocket-Key: (\S+)/i)![1] + "258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11";
const accept = btoa(String.fromCharCode(...new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-1", new TextEncoder().encode(key)))));
await conn.write(new TextEncoder().encode(`HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nSec-WebSocket-Accept: ${accept}\r\n\r\n`));
let received = 0;
setInterval(() => console.log(`server: received ${received} bytes`), 500);
for (let n; (n = await conn.read(buf.subarray(0, 16384)).catch(() => null)) !== null;) {
  received += n;
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1)); // read slowly so the client's socket backs up
}
Deno.exit(0);
```

`client.ts`: sends one 4 MiB message, reports `bufferedAmount` until it reaches 0, and 3 s
later sends one more message:

```ts
const ws = new WebSocket("wss://localhost:8443");
ws.onopen = () => {
  ws.send(new Uint8Array(4 * 1024 * 1024)); // one 4 MiB binary message (4194318 bytes on the wire)
  const timer = setInterval(() => {
    console.log(`client: bufferedAmount=${ws.bufferedAmount}`);
    if (ws.bufferedAmount > 0) return;
    clearInterval(timer);
    setTimeout(() => { console.log("client: sending one more message"); ws.send("x"); }, 3000);
    setTimeout(() => Deno.exit(0), 5000);
  }, 500);
};
```

```sh
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem -days 30 -subj /CN=localhost \
  -addext subjectAltName=DNS:localhost -addext basicConstraints=critical,CA:FALSE
deno run --allow-net --allow-read server.ts &
sleep 1
deno run --allow-net --cert cert.pem client.ts
```

## Expected

Once `bufferedAmount` is 0, the server receives the rest of the message on its own: 4 MiB of
payload plus a 14-byte frame header, 4194318 bytes in total.

## Actual

The last lines of a failing run (2.9.6 release):

```
server: received 3502318 bytes
client: bufferedAmount=0
server: received 4122542 bytes
server: received 4122542 bytes
server: received 4122542 bytes
server: received 4122542 bytes
server: received 4122542 bytes
client: sending one more message
server: received 4155310 bytes
server: received 4194325 bytes
server: received 4194325 bytes
```

After the client reports `bufferedAmount=0`, the server is stuck at 4122542 bytes, 71776 short
of the end, and stays there. The one-byte text message the client sends 3 s later (7 bytes on
the wire) releases everything: 4194318 + 7 = 4194325. In the runs below the stuck tail was
between 20 KB and 73 KB, most often about 56 KB or 72 KB.

Whether a run stalls depends on the socket being full at the moment the last bytes of the
message are handed to TLS, so not every run does. On this machine, running the two files above
ten times each:

| Deno | stalled | runs |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| macOS, 2.9.6 release (official binary) | 4 | 10 |
| macOS, `main` at 057a3da (official canary binary) | 6 | 10 |
| macOS, `main` at 685eb3b (local debug build) | 4 | 10 |
| Linux, 2.9.6 (`denoland/deno:2.9.6`), server and client in two containers on a Docker bridge network | 1 | 6 |
| Linux, `main` at 057a3da (official Linux canary binary in the same image), same setup | 1 | 6 |

Every stalled run released the whole tail on the follow-up message. On Linux the two files in
one container over loopback did not stall in 12 runs: Linux loopback has a 64 KiB MTU and
autotunes the socket buffers into the megabytes, so the whole 4 MiB was accepted before the
client's send could block. Across a bridge network (veth, MTU 1500) it stalls like a real
network path does. Two controls with the same
server: the same client over plain `ws:` (`Deno.listen` instead of `Deno.listenTls`) completed
3 of 3 times, and Node 26's built-in `WebSocket` over `wss:` against this TLS server completed
3 of 3 times.

## Why, as far as I can tell

`send()` → `op_ws_send_binary` → `send_binary` spawns a task that awaits
`ServerWebSocket::write_frame` and then subtracts the message length from the buffered count
(`ext/websocket/lib.rs`, `send_binary`). `ServerWebSocket::write_frame` awaits
`fastwebsockets::WebSocketWrite::write_frame` and returns; that ends with `write_all` on the
underlying stream, and nothing in `ext/websocket` ever calls `flush`.

For a `wss:` connection the underlying stream is `tokio_rustls::client::TlsStream` (the
connection comes from `deno_fetch`, whose connector is `hyper_rustls`). tokio-rustls'
`poll_write` encrypts into rustls' internal buffer, tries to write that ciphertext to the
socket, and when the socket would block it returns `Ready(Ok(n))` for the plaintext it accepted
while the ciphertext stays buffered (`tokio-rustls-0.26.0/src/common/mod.rs`, `poll_write`,
the `(n, true) => Poll::Ready(Ok(n))` arm). Its `poll_read` only reads; it never writes out
pending ciphertext. tokio-rustls' crate documentation says exactly this, under "Why do I need to
call `poll_flush`?" and "Why don't we write during `poll_read`?":
https://docs.rs/tokio-rustls/0.26.0/tokio_rustls/#why-do-i-need-to-call-poll_flush

So once the send task has resolved, up to rustls' 64 KiB of ciphertext can sit in user space
with no future left that polls the write half: `op_ws_next_event` only polls the read half. The
bytes are never lost, just never sent, until some later write drives them out, while
`bufferedAmount` already says they were sent.

Version: Deno 2.9.7 Host: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, GNOME Shell 50.1, Wayland session. Targets built: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (.deb, .AppImage), x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (.msi). ## Bug summary The icon passed via `--icon` / `desktop.app.icons` is packaged correctly but never actually reaches the window or the executable when the `cef` backend is used: 1. **Linux + `--backend cef` on Wayland** the app shows a generic fallback icon in the dock/taskbar and no application name. The same app built with `--backend webview` works. 2. **Windows (`.msi`)** the `.ico` is copied into the install directory as `AppIcon.ico` but is not embedded into the `.exe` as a PE resource, and the MSI `Shortcut` row has no `Icon_`. Explorer, the taskbar and the Start Menu shortcut all show the default icon. These look like two faces of the same gap, so they're filed together; happy to split. ## Reproduction Minimal app (a normal Deno HTTP server, per the `deno desktop` model): `main.ts` ```ts Deno.serve({ port: 0 }, () => new Response("

hello

", { headers: { "content-type": "text/html" }, })); ``` `deno.json` ```json { "version": "0.0.1", "desktop": { "app": { "name": "icon-repro", "identifier": "com.example.icon-repro" }, "backend": "cef" } } ``` Build and install: ```bash deno desktop -A --icon ./icons/app-512.png \ --output ./dist/icon-repro.deb --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu . sudo apt install ./dist/icon-repro.deb ``` Launch it from the GNOME activities overview on a Wayland session. **Expected:** the dock/taskbar entry shows the app icon and the app name. **Actual:** generic fallback icon, no app name. Building the same app with `"backend": "webview"` produces the correct icon and name. I didn't test how it behaves on macOS distributions

Version: Deno 2.9.5

### What steps will reproduce the bug?
```sh
deno eval 'fetch("http://cnylon.localhost")'
```
```log
error: Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: fetch failed
    at mainFetch (ext:deno_fetch/26_fetch.js:2:3449)
    at async fetch (ext:deno_fetch/26_fetch.js:2:7360)
Caused by: Error: error sending request for url (http://cnylon.localhost/): client error (Connect): dns error: failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known
    at mainFetch (ext:deno_fetch/26_fetch.js:2:3477)
    at async fetch (ext:deno_fetch/26_fetch.js:2:7360)
```


### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6761.html#section-6.3
```
6.3 Domain Name Reservation Considerations for "localhost."

   The domain "localhost." and any names falling within ".localhost."
   are special in the following ways:

   1.  Users are free to use localhost names as they would any other
       domain names.  Users may assume that IPv4 and IPv6 address
       queries for localhost names will always resolve to the respective
       IP loopback address.

   2.  Application software MAY recognize localhost names as special, or
       MAY pass them to name resolution APIs as they would for other
       domain names.

   3.  Name resolution APIs and libraries SHOULD recognize localhost
       names as special and SHOULD always return the IP loopback address
       for address queries and negative responses for all other query
       types.  Name resolution APIs SHOULD NOT send queries for
       localhost names to their configured caching DNS server(s).

   4.  Caching DNS servers SHOULD recognize localhost names as special
       and SHOULD NOT attempt to look up NS records for them, or
       otherwise query authoritative DNS servers in an attempt to
       resolve localhost names.  Instead, caching DNS servers SHOULD,
       for all such address queries, generate an immediate positive
       response giving the IP loopback address, and for all other query
       types, generate an immediate negative response.  This is to avoid
       unnecessary load on the root name servers and other name servers.
```

## Description

`deno desktop --hmr .` cannot resolve a transitive npm dependency while loading a Vite config inside the Desktop runtime.

In this SvelteKit project, `kleur` is declared by `@sveltejs/kit@2.69.0` and is present as `kleur@4.1.5` in `deno.lock` and the managed nested `node_modules` tree. The application does not declare `kleur` directly.

## Reproduction

Reproduction repository: https://github.com/TB516/deadlock-build-manager

Environment:

- Deno 2.9.7
- Linux x86_64
- `@deno/svelte-adapter` 0.2.1
- `@sveltejs/kit` 2.69.0
- Vite 8.1.2

`vite.config.ts`:

```ts
import { sveltekit } from "@sveltejs/kit/vite";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [sveltekit()],
});
```

Run:

```sh
deno task dev:desktop
```

## Actual behavior

Desktop HMR starts, then fails while loading `vite.config.ts`:

```
TypeError: Import "kleur" not a dependency
...
code: "ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND"
```

The Vite/SvelteKit dev server does not start.

## Expected behavior

The Vite config loader should resolve `kleur` through the managed npm dependency graph because it is a dependency of `@sveltejs/kit`, even though it is not a direct dependency of the application.

Version: Deno 2.9.5+62d6124

## Summary

On Deno Deploy, `Deno.connectTls()` successfully establishes a verified TLS connection to a MongoDB Atlas endpoint, while `node:tls.connect()` against the exact same hostname and port fails with:

```text
ERR_SSL_TLSV1_ALERT_INTERNAL_ERROR
received fatal alert: InternalError
```

The MongoDB Node.js driver fails through the same Node compatibility TLS/networking path.

This is reproducible on Deno Deploy, while the same Atlas endpoint and `node:tls` connection work locally.

## Environment

Deno Deploy runtime measured directly from the affected Preview:

```text
Deno: 2.9.5+62d6124
V8: 15.0.245.2-rusty
TypeScript: 6.0.3
Node compatibility: 26.3.0
OpenSSL: 3.0.7+quic
N-API: 10
modules: 147
libuv: 1.52.1
```

Target:

```text
MongoDB Atlas
AWS-backed Atlas Dedicated M10 cluster
TLS port: 27017
Hostname: standard Atlas *.mongodb.net hostname
Certificate verification: enabled
SNI: explicitly set to the same Atlas hostname
```

No insecure TLS options are used.

## Minimal reproduction

### 1. Native Deno TLS succeeds

```ts
const hostname = Deno.env.get("ATLAS_HOST")!;

const conn = await Deno.connectTls({
  hostname,
  port: 27017,
});

console.log("NATIVE_TLS_OK");
conn.close();
```

Result on Deno Deploy:

```text
NATIVE_TLS_OK
```

This uses normal certificate verification.

### 2. Node compatibility TLS fails

```ts
import tls from "node:tls";

const hostname = Deno.env.get("ATLAS_HOST")!;

const socket = tls.connect({
  host: hostname,
  port: 27017,
  servername: hostname,
  rejectUnauthorized: true,
});

socket.once("secureConnect", () => {
  console.log("NODE_TLS_OK");
  socket.destroy();
});

socket.once("error", (error) => {
  console.error(error);
});
```

Result on Deno Deploy:

```text
ERR_SSL_TLSV1_ALERT_INTERNAL_ERROR
received fatal alert: InternalError
```

Both tests use:

- the exact same Atlas hostname;
- the exact same port `27017`;
- the same SNI hostname;
- certificate verification enabled.

No MongoDB authentication or MongoDB wire-protocol traffic is required to reproduce the difference.

## MongoDB Node.js driver reproduction

The issue also occurs through the official MongoDB Node.js driver.

Tested versions:

```text
mongodb@6.1.0
mongodb@6.21.0
```

With `mongodb@6.21.0`, the Deno Deploy connection fails with:

```text
MongoServerSelectionError: received fatal alert: InternalError
```

A representative underlying error is:

```text
MongoNetworkError: received fatal alert: InternalError

[cause]: Error: received fatal alert: InternalError
    at TCPWrap.t.onread (ext:deno_node/internal_binding/tls_wrap.ts:...)
{
  code: "ERR_SSL_TLSV1_ALERT_INTERNAL_ERROR"
}
```

All three Atlas replica-set members consequently become `Unknown`.

The resulting topology is:

```text
ReplicaSetNoPrimary
```

However, `ReplicaSetNoPrimary` appears to be a consequence rather than the original failure: TLS negotiation fails against every replica-set member before the driver can discover a primary.

A representative production stack trace includes:

```text
MongoServerSelectionError: received fatal alert: InternalError
    at Timeout._onTimeout (.../mongodb/6.1.0/lib/sdam/topology.js:278:38)
    ...

reason: TopologyDescription {
  type: "ReplicaSetNoPrimary",
  ...
}

[cause]: MongoNetworkError: received fatal alert: InternalError
    at connectionFailureError (.../mongodb/lib/cmap/connect.js:...)
    at TLSSocket.<anonymous> (.../mongodb/lib/cmap/connect.js:...)
    ...

[cause]: Error: received fatal alert: InternalError
    at TCPWrap.t.onread (ext:deno_node/internal_binding/tls_wrap.ts:...)
{
  code: "ERR_SSL_TLSV1_ALERT_INTERNAL_ERROR"
}
```

## Control tests

The Atlas endpoint itself is reachable and functional.

From a local machine with VPN disabled:

```text
Atlas SRV lookup: PASS
Atlas TXT lookup: PASS
TCP connectivity to all three Atlas nodes on port 27017: PASS
OpenSSL TLS 1.2 handshake with explicit SNI: PASS
Certificate verification: OK
mongosh authentication: PASS
mongodb@6.21.0 connect/ping: PASS
Deno.connectTls(): PASS
node:tls.connect(): PASS
```

Example OpenSSL result:

```text
CONNECTION ESTABLISHED
Protocol version: TLSv1.2
Ciphersuite: ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
Peer certificate: CN=*.mongodb.net
Verification: OK
```

The `node:tls` failure is reproducible specifically in the Deno Deploy environment.

## Deno Deploy comparison

Against the same Atlas hostname:

| Path | Result |
| --- | --- |
| HTTP-only `Deno.serve()` | PASS |
| `Deno.connectTls()` | PASS |
| `node:tls.connect()` | FAIL |
| `mongodb@6.21.0` | FAIL |

The important difference within the same Deno Deploy environment is:

```text
Deno.connectTls()
→ successful verified TLS connection

node:tls.connect()
→ ERR_SSL_TLSV1_ALERT_INTERNAL_ERROR
→ received fatal alert: InternalError
```

## Application impact

MongoDB-backed applications running on Deno Deploy intermittently fail with HTTP 500 because the MongoDB Node.js driver cannot reliably establish TLS connections to the Atlas replica-set members.

The application can start its HTTP server successfully when MongoDB initialization is removed from the cold-start critical path.

For example:

```text
Fresh ready
```

is reached successfully.

A subsequent MongoDB-backed request then attempts the database connection and fails with:

```text
MongoServerSelectionError: received fatal alert: InternalError
```

All three Atlas replica-set members show the same underlying TLS error.

This means non-database routes can remain healthy while MongoDB-backed routes fail.

## Separate Deno Node warning / TTY issue discovered during investigation

A second issue was discovered while isolating this problem.

`mongodb@6.1.0` used the following older transitive dependency chain:

```text
mongodb@6.1.0
└─ mongodb-connection-string-url@2.6.0
   └─ whatwg-url@11.0.0
      └─ tr46@3.0.0
         └─ require("punycode")
```

This causes Node's `DEP0040` deprecation warning for the built-in `punycode` module.

On Deno Deploy, emitting that warning could trigger:

```text
SystemError: TTY initialization failed:
uv_tty_init returned UNKNOWN (unknown error)
```

The stack was:

```text
new NodeSystemError
→ new NodeError
→ new WriteStream
→ makeStdioWriteStream
→ process.get [as stderr]
→ process.onWarning
→ process.emit
→ doEmitWarning
```

Representative output:

```text
SystemError: TTY initialization failed: uv_tty_init returned UNKNOWN (unknown error)
    at new NodeSystemError (ext:deno_node/internal/errors.ts:...)
    at new NodeError (ext:deno_node/internal/errors.ts:...)
    at new WriteStream (ext:deno_node/internal/tty.js:...)
    at makeStdioWriteStream (node:process:...)
    at process.get [as stderr] (node:process:...)
    at process.onWarning (ext:deno_node/internal/process/warning.ts:...)
```

Upgrading the MongoDB driver to `mongodb@6.21.0` changes the dependency graph to:

```text
mongodb@6.21.0
└─ mongodb-connection-string-url@3.0.2
   └─ whatwg-url@14.2.0
      └─ tr46@5.1.1
         └─ punycode@2.3.1
```

The newer `tr46` path uses the userland `punycode` package instead of Node's deprecated built-in module.

After that upgrade:

```text
DEP0040: no longer emitted
```

However:

```text
node:tls → Atlas
```

```
pages
```

#28837 was closed but the async suit thing mentioned in the issue body is still not implemented.

In Node.js and Bun this works fine:

```ts
import assert from 'node:assert'
import { describe, it } from 'node:test'

describe('Async Test Suite', async () => {
  const i = await Promise.resolve(42)
  let assertionCount = 0

  it('should handle async operations', async () => {
    const result = await Promise.resolve(i * 2)
    assertionCount++
    assert.strictEqual(result, 84)
  })

  describe('Nested Async Suite', async () => {
    const j = await Promise.resolve(7)

    it('should handle nested async operations', async () => {
      const result = await Promise.resolve(i + j)
      assertionCount++
      assert.strictEqual(result, 49)
    })

    describe('Even More Nested Async Suite', async () => {
      const k = await Promise.resolve(3)

      it('should handle deeply nested async operations', async () => {
        const result = await Promise.resolve(i * j * k)
        assertionCount++
        assert.strictEqual(result, 882)
      })
    })
  })

  it('should have the correct number of assertions after async tests', () => {
    assert.strictEqual(assertionCount, 3)
  })
})
```

Feature request: Support OpenBSD in deno compile

Deno runs on OpenBSD, but deno compile currently does not support OpenBSD targets.

It would be useful to support at least:

x86_64-unknown-openbsd
aarch64-unknown-openbsd

For example:

deno compile --target x86_64-unknown-openbsd main.ts

Use case

I would like to deploy Deno applications on OpenBSD as standalone executables, without requiring a separate Deno runtime installation.

Since Deno already runs on OpenBSD, this seems primarily to require adding OpenBSD targets to the deno compile / denort build and release pipeline.

Would support for OpenBSD targets be considered?

Thanks.

body_text:
When adding an npm package that doesn't provide its own TypeScript types, `--save-types` could also find and install the matching `@types/*` package:

```bash
$ deno add express --save-types
# adds express and @types/express

$ deno add zod --save-types
# adds zod only, because it provides its own types
```

The `saveTypes` option (boolean, defaults to `false` at first, `true` in future versions) could configure this in `deno.json`.

With `package.json`, the `@types/*` package would be added to `devDependencies`. With `deno.json`, it would be added to `imports`.

Deno already [falls back to installed `@types/*` packages (PR #28185)](https://github.com/denoland/deno/pull/28185). PR [#28216](https://github.com/denoland/deno/pull/28216) also implemented an LSP quick fix to install missing `@types/*` packages (closed as stale).

### Prior Art

1. pnpm 12.6 added this with the [`--save-types` flag](https://pnpm.io/blog/releases/12.6#--save-types) (and `saveTypes: true` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`), implementing [pnpm/pnpm#3868](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/3868)
2. Yarn 4+ [automatically installs matching `@types/*` packages by default](https://yarnpkg.com/blog/release/4.0#typescript-integration-interactive-tools-:~:text=Yarn%20will%20now%20auto%2Dadd%20and%20remove%20%40types%20packages%20as%20needed%20whenever%20you%20update%20your%20dependencies%20with%20yarn%20add%20and%20yarn%20remove) ([`tsEnableAutoTypes`](https://yarnpkg.com/configuration/yarnrc#tsEnableAutoTypes) in `.yarnrc.yml`) when a `tsconfig.json` exists at the project root or in the current workspace

Version: Deno 2.9.7
MacOS 27.0 Golden Gate MBP M1

Noticed this initially using 2.9.6 after I had upgraded to macOS 27.0 and 2.9.7 makes no difference.
Only occurs with webview (CEF works OK both dev/prod) and in DEV mode - Prod generally works OK.

When encountering this initially I thought the win.executeJs feature was not working but of course if the page is not ready that will indeed be the case. As far as I can see the delay is c. 1400ms or so whereas the delay on CEF is only c. 7ms. It does not happen if the standard Hello World app is used with the html constant as the page data.

It worked OK on 12.7.6 but I jumped up to 27.0 so not sure if it would happen on any of the interim releases.

Attached a wee project to demonstrate -

[whitewinbug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32608950/whitewinbug.zip)

I'm looking for an alternative with faster build times and deno desktop seems to be a good candidate.

In the current app, the cli is bundled as an executable sidecar: https://v2.tauri.app/develop/sidecar/

Having a way to configure an executable sidecar would be great but AFAICS bundling additional files with a way to reference them so is possible to execute with Deno.Command would be enough: https://v2.tauri.app/develop/resources/

body_text:
Version: Deno 2.9.7

Example (at time of writing, depends on when package was published):

```sh
deno bundle jsr:@li/inner-text@0.0.8
```

Output:

```sh
⚠️  deno bundle is experimental and subject to changes
error: Do not know how to load path: deno:jsr:@li/inner-text@0.0.8
error: bundling failed
```

Actual error is due to https://github.com/denoland/deno/issues/36358, and the fix is to add `--min-dep-age=0` flag, but there's no way to know that from the error message.

Ideally the error messages from `import`-ing and `deno bundle`-ing would both specify that supplying the `--min-dep-age` flag is the fix.

Version: Deno 2.9.7

According to the [documentation](https://docs.deno.com/runtime/reference/cli/pack/#deno-api-shimming)
`deno pack --no-deno-shim` should work.

but looking at the output of `--help`

```deno pack --help          
Create a tarball of the package

Usage: deno pack [OPTIONS] [FILES]...

Options:
  -o, --output <VALUE>    Output file path (defaults to <name>-<version>.tgz)
      --dry-run           Show what would be packed without creating the tarball
      --allow-slow-types  Skip fast-check type extraction; .d.ts files are omitted from the output
      --allow-dirty       Allow packing if the repository has uncommitted changes
      --set-version <VALUE>  Override the version in the tarball
      --no-source-maps    Don't include source maps in the output
      --ignore[=VALUE...]  Ignore files matching these patterns
  -c, --config <VALUE>    Configure different aspects of deno including TypeScript, linting, and code formatting.
                            Typically the configuration file will be called `deno.json` or `deno.jsonc` and
                            automatically detected; in that case this flag is not necessary.
                            Docs: https://docs.deno.com/go/config
      --no-config         Disable automatic loading of the configuration file
      --env-file[=<VALUE>]  Load environment variables from local file
                            Only the first environment variable with a given key is used.
                            Existing process environment variables are not overwritten, so if variables with the same names already exist in the environment, their values will be preserved.
                            Where multiple declarations for the same environment variable exist in your .env file, the first one encountered is applied. This is determined by the order of the files you pass as arguments.
```

The option is not there. Passing the option results in an error.

Deno appears to ignore both "latest" tag on npm and any "deprecations" when selecting version to install.

Repro steps:
```
deno add npm:socket
```

Expected: socket 1.4.0 installed ([latest tag, highest non-deprecated version](https://www.npmjs.com/package/socket/v/1.4.0?activeTab=versions))
Actual: socket 2.1.0 installed ([version marked as deprecated on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/socket/v/2.1.0?activeTab=versions))

I didn't see anything in the docs.deno.com that covered this version selection behavior so it may catch some users off guard

body_text:
`numericSeparator` has no effect in Deno, whether it is passed as an option or set on `util.inspect.defaultOptions`:

```js
import util from "node:util";

console.log(util.inspect(1234567.891, { numericSeparator: true }));
console.log(util.inspect(-1234n, { numericSeparator: true }));
console.log(util.formatWithOptions({ numericSeparator: true }, "%d", 1234567));
```

Node 24 prints:

```
1_234_567.891
-1_234n
1_234_567
```

Deno 2.9.7 prints:

```
1234567.891
-1234n
1234567
```

It is also the first failing assertion in `test-util-format.js` from the Node test suite.

body_text:
Version: Deno 2.9.7

I'm trying to use `deno compile --bundle --minify --exclude-unused-npm` to build an application from a specific entrypoint. Elsewhere in the same codebase, in code unreachable from that entrypoint (as confirmed by `deno info` on that entrpoint), I have an import of `npm:@duckdb/node-api`. When I run the compile command, I see that it includes >100MB extra of native modules from that package despite them being unreachable. I would expect that if the package is completely unreachable from the entrypoint, its native code is not bundled either.

This even happens in a minimal test case if you don't import the package in question at all, and it's just listed in the dependencies in deno.jsonc.

Here's a minimal reproduction project:

`deno.jsonc`:
```
{
  "imports": {
    "duckdb": "npm:@duckdb/node-api"
  }
}
```

`main.ts`:
```
if (import.meta.main) {
  console.log("Hello, world!");
}
```

Steps to confirm:
- `deno install`
- `deno compile --bundle --exclude-unused-npm --minify -o ./main main.ts`
- `ls -al main`
- see this reports `main` is ~186MB on my machine
- remove `"duckdb": "npm:@duckdb/node-api"` from `deno.jsonc`
- `deno install`
- `deno compile --bundle --exclude-unused-npm --minify -o ./main main.ts`
- `ls -al main`
- see this reports `main` is ~68MB on my machine

**Environment:** Deno 2.9.7 (aarch64-apple-darwin), `deno desktop` with the CEF backend (laufey
0.7.0), macOS 26.

### CEF connects to Google on its own

With no request from the page, the packaged app's network service opens HTTPS connections to
Google addresses (2001:4860::/32), which looks like Chromium's background services (component
updates, safe browsing and the like). Apps that promise users a short list of connections can't
keep that promise.

**Ask:** pass `--disable-background-networking` and turn off component updates by default in
`deno desktop`, or give apps a documented switch for both.

### No API to answer permission requests

The window API has no hook for CEF's permission requests (camera, microphone, location,
notifications and so on), so an app can't deny them itself. We work around it with a
`Permissions-Policy` header on every response, which stops the page from asking.

**Ask:** a permission-request callback on the window, or a build-time allow-list, with deny as
the default.

---

Thanks for `deno desktop`. Everything else we checked was what we hoped for: one listener on
127.0.0.1, no debug port by default, and the page's CSP and Permissions-Policy honoured.

body_text:
It is common to have several `deno` processes running against the same `DENO_DIR` and the same project at once: the language server, a dev server, a test run, CI fanning out `deno test` / `deno compile` in parallel. Today the only cross-process coordination is the `node_modules` lock (`LaxSingleProcessFsFlag`). Some of the problems this leads to:

- #35804 and #36423: concurrent `run` / `test` corrupting `node_modules`, and os error 32 rewriting `.bin` shims on Windows.
- Two `deno test --coverage=cov` runs: the second clears `cov/` while the first is still writing, and the first then reports from a half-deleted directory.
- Two `deno compile --output out`: each deletes `out.tmp-*` files "left over from interrupted compilations" at startup, which includes the other run's in-progress temp file. Similar for `deno bundle --outdir` and `deno doc --html --output` (which removes the output directory first).
- `deno.lock`: each writer writes what it read at startup plus its own additions, so with two concurrent writers the last one silently drops the other's entries.
- `deno clean` can delete cache entries another process is reading, and a safe automatic cache GC (#36396, #32932) needs a mode that excludes readers before it can delete anything.

## Proposal

Adopt Cargo's model ([`cargo::util::cache_lock`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/nightly-rustc/cargo/util/cache_lock/index.html)):

- **Package cache locks with three modes** over two lock files in `DENO_DIR/locks/`:
  - `Shared`: held by commands that finish on their own (check, test, compile, cache, install, ...) for their run. Long-running commands (run, serve, LSP, `--watch`) hold no command-wide lock, so `deno clean` doesn't wait for an editor to close.
  - `DownloadExclusive`: held around each HTTP fetch into the cache, in every command. It doesn't block `Shared`, since cache writes are already temp-file-and-rename.
  - `MutateExclusive`: excludes everything; used by `deno clean` and would be what a cache GC takes.
  - Fixed lock order (mutate before download), recursive within a process, out-of-order or upgrade requests refused rather than risking deadlock.
- **Exclusive locks on build outputs** for the whole command: the `--coverage` directory, `compile --output`, `bundle --outdir/--output`, `doc --html --output`. Lock files live under `DENO_DIR/locks/artifacts/` keyed by the normalized path, so nothing is left in published or read-back directories.
- **`deno.lock` writes** become read-merge-write under a lock on the lockfile, reusing `deno_lockfile`'s existing merge-conflict logic, so concurrent writers don't drop each other's entries.
- **Real OS locks** (`flock` / `LockFileEx` via `sys_traits::FsFileLock`): try without blocking, and if contended print Cargo's `Blocking waiting for file lock on <what>` and block. The OS releases them on any exit, so no staleness heuristics are needed. Best effort when the file system doesn't support locking or `DENO_DIR` is read-only.

The existing `node_modules` lock would be left as is; #36423's agreed fix (skip unchanged shim writes) is orthogonal.

## Implementation

I have a working implementation on a fork branch, based on current `main`: https://github.com/Brainwires/deno/tree/feat/cargo-style-locks-main. It has unit tests for the lock modes and the lockfile merge, plus spec tests that drive real concurrent `deno` processes (clean waits for readers, readers wait for a mutation, downloads exclude downloads, two coverage runs, compile output, lockfile merge). They pass on Linux, macOS and Windows in the fork's CI.

Open questions I'd welcome input on: whether long-running commands should hold `Shared` during startup (graph build / type check) and release it before running user code, and whether lock files under `DENO_DIR` (rather than next to outputs) is the right trade-off.

If this direction is acceptable, I'm happy to open a PR.

Disclosure: the implementation and this write-up were prepared with the help of an AI coding assistant (Claude) and reviewed by me.

body_text:
## Summary

The [auto-update docs](https://docs.deno.com/runtime/desktop/auto_update/) say:

> When the app restarts, the launcher swaps the staged update into place before anything else runs.

On Linux this isn't what happens. `apply_pending_update` runs inside the app dylib, not in the launcher: the launcher `dlopen`s the **old** dylib, then that code moves `<dylib>.update` into place. The process doing the swap keeps running the old code it has already mapped. The new version only runs on the launch **after** that.

That has two consequences:

1. **The update appears to need two restarts.** The launch that does the swap still reports the old Deno.desktopVersion`, so `Deno.autoUpdate()` finds the same patch in `latest.json`, downloads it again, and fires `onUpdateReady` a second time for a version that is already on disk.
2. **Rollback never protects the new version.** `op_desktop_confirm_update` writes `<dylib>.update-ok` whenever `<dylib>.backup` exists (per #36574). The first boot where that's true is the swapping launch, which is still the old code, so it confirms the update before the new dylib has ever run. On the next launch the runtime sees `.backup` + `.update-ok`, cleans up the backup, and only then runs the new code. If the new version crashes on startup, there is no backup left to roll back to, and `onRollback` can never fire.

## Environment

- Deno 2.9.7, laufey 0.7.0 (`.downloaded` = `v0.7.0`), CEF backend
- Linux x86_64 (CachyOS); reproduced with a plain-directory build and with a `--compress=xz` AppImage (which unpacks to `~/.local/share/...`, so the dylib is writable)

## Evidence that the swap lives in the dylib

In a built app directory, the launcher contains none of the update strings; the dylib does:

```
$ grep -c -a 'update-ok' MyApp MyApp.so
MyApp:0
MyApp.so:1
$ grep -c -a 'Failed to write update' MyApp MyApp.so
MyApp:0
MyApp.so:1
```

## Reproduction

Staging an update manually without an update server.

`main.ts`:

```ts
// v1 and v2 differ only in this marker
Deno.writeTextFileSync(Deno.env.get("OUT")!, JSON.stringify({ marker: "v1" }));
Deno.exit(0);
```

```sh
# v1 and v2, same app name, both self-extracting so the dylib is writable
deno desktop -A --compress=xz --output ./v1/App.AppImage main.ts
sed -i 's/"v1"/"v2"/' main.ts
deno desktop -A --compress=xz --output ./v2/App.AppImage main.ts

# run each once so they unpack, then find their unpacked dirs
OUT=/tmp/o.json ./v1/App.AppImage; OUT=/tmp/o.json ./v2/App.AppImage
D1=~/.local/share/com.deno.desktop.app/<v1 hash>/App
D2=~/.local/share/com.deno.desktop.app/<v2 hash>/App

# stage v2's dylib as an update for v1
cp "$D2/App.so" "$D1/App.so.update"

for i in 1 2 3; do
  OUT=/tmp/o.json ./v1/App.AppImage; cat /tmp/o.json
  ls "$D1" | grep -E '\.so\.(update|backup|update-ok)$'
done
```

Observed:

| Launch | Code that ran | Files beside the dylib afterwards |
| ------ | ------------- | --------------------------------- |
| 1      | **v1**        | `App.so.backup`, `App.so.update-ok` |
| 2      | v2            | (none)                            |

Expected (per the docs): launch 1 runs v2, and `.update-ok` is only written once v2 has booted.

The [auto-update docs](https://docs.deno.com/runtime/desktop/auto_update/) say:

> When the app restarts, the launcher swaps the staged update into place before anything else runs.

On Linux this isn't what happens. `apply_pending_update` runs inside the app dylib, not in the launcher: the launcher `dlopen`s the **old** dylib, then that code moves `<dylib>.update` into place. That has two consequences:

1. **The update appears to need two restarts.** The launch that does the swap still reports the old Deno.desktopVersion`, so `Deno.autoUpdate()` finds the same patch in `latest.json`, downloads it again, and fires `onUpdateReady` a second time for a version that is already on disk.
2. **Rollback never protects the new version.** `op_desktop_confirm_update` writes `<dylib>.update-ok` whenever `<dylib>.backup` exists (per #36574). Hi @crowlKats @littledivy (cc @bartlomieju),

We've been shipping real apps on Deno Desktop (2.9.7) and ran into enough gaps that we built a
patched runtime: [Brainwires/deno](https://github.com/Brainwires/deno) (branch `denext/v2.9.7`, every change listed in
[DENEXT.md](https://github.com/Brainwires/deno/blob/denext/v2.9.7/DENEXT.md)) and
[Brainwires/laufey](https://github.com/Brainwires/laufey). We'd like it all to land upstream so we can
drop the fork. We'd rather ask how you want it before opening a pile of PRs.

Everything is tested on macOS (arm64 and x64), Linux (x64 and arm64) and Windows x64 with both the
webview and CEF backends, on Deno's own CI bar (lint, fmt, `cargo test --lib`, unit and spec) and
an end-to-end suite that packages and launches an app per area.

**1. Small fixes against current main (laufey 0.7.0, no new API).** Each would be one PR with a test that fails on main:
- `Dock.setBadge(null)` shows the text "null" instead of clearing the badge
- `op_desktop_alert_async` is deleted at bootstrap, so the uncaught-error dialog never shows
- `Notification.close()` can deadlock (the map lock is held while the backend fires `close`)
- the window `close` event can't be cancelled (#36913)
- Node-API addons crash on Windows (#36596, the Windows half; #36718 fixed Linux)
- a full event channel drops discrete events (a lost `contextmenuclose` wedges `showContextMenu`)
- `BrowserWindow`/`Tray`/`Dock`/`Notification` panic in workers
- the HTTPS error report can hang exit; a hidden bootstrap window gets revealed anyway in tray-only apps; a few `desktop.*` keys missing from the config schema

**2. Foundations**
- the in-process memory transport (#35675) plus two follow-ups (an absolute-form `http+memory:`
  target over TCP is refused; `node:http` serves on it)
- a stable custom-scheme app origin (`desktop.app.origin`, e.g. `myapp://app`): a scheme handler
  bridging into `Deno.serve` over the memory transport, plus a loopback relay for WebSockets that only
  accepts the app's exact `Origin`. This fixes #35444 and #35576. Storage persists across launches, and
  OAuth providers that check `Origin` accept it.
- handing the app identifier to every backend (per-app storage; #36768), building on #35662
- letting the runtime provide its own environment variables without `setenv` once the UI thread runs

**3. Features** (each needs its laufey half released first; we have PRs open there, littledivy/laufey#84, littledivy/laufey#85, littledivy/laufey#86, littledivy/laufey#87, littledivy/laufey#88, littledivy/laufey#89, littledivy/laufey#90, littledivy/laufey#91, littledivy/laufey#92 and littledivy/laufey#93):
deep links, opened files and single instance (completing #35465); OS scheme registration and the
`.msi` keys; maximize/minimize/fullscreen, size limits, bounds and screens, title-bar styles and
backdrops, `quit()` (on top of #36761 and #36789); menu accelerators on every backend; notification
actions and scheduling; native file dialogs; drag and drop with paths; HTML and image formats on
`navigator.clipboard`; global shortcuts; launch at login; DevTools control; `runOnMainThread`
(#36738); `ASWebAuthenticationSession` on macOS; native passkeys; and signed full-app updates (a
whole-bundle swap with rollback, which also addresses #36948. We'd like to discuss that design
with you before writing a PR).

Questions:
1. Would you like one PR per item, as listed, with a linked issue each, or the small fixes batched?
2. Should new APIs go under `Deno.desktop` (i.e. after #35939)? Is #35939 close to landing?
3. #35675: shall we rebase it and add our follow-ups, open a fresh PR crediting it, or leave it to you?
4. laufey: is it OK for Deno PRs to wait on laufey releases, and would you prefer we bump the laufey pin or you do?
5. For signed full-app updates: should they replace `Deno.autoUpdate` or sit beside it?
6. Would an end-to-end harness for packaged desktop apps (one small app per area, run on all three OSes) be useful upstream?

Several changes build on open work by others, and we'll keep their authorship and credit: #35662
(@crowlKats), #35675, #36761 (@petamoriken), #36789 (@sasivarnan), #36421 (@johnstonmatt), and on the
laufey side littledivy/laufey#77 (@diegoholiveira), littledivy/laufey#79 / littledivy/laufey#80 (@petamoriken) and littledivy/laufey#81 (@sasivarnan).

AI usage: this work was done with Claude Code (Anthropic) under human direction and review. Every
PR will say so.

webview and CEF backends, on Deno's own CI bar (lint, fmt, `cargo test --lib`, unit and spec) and
an end-to-end suite that packages and launches an app per area.

**1. Small fixes against current main (laufey 0.7.0, no new API).** Each would be one PR with a test that fails on main:
- `Dock.setBadge(null)` shows the text "null" instead of clearing the badge
- `op_desktop_alert_async` is deleted at bootstrap, so the uncaught-error dialog never shows
- `Notification.close()` can deadlock (the map lock is held while the backend fires `close`)
- the window `close` event can't be cancelled (#36913)
- Node-API addons crash on Windows (#36596, the Windows half; #36718 fixed Linux)
- a full event channel drops discrete events (a lost `contextmenuclose` wedges `showContextMenu`)
- `BrowserWindow`/`Tray`/`Dock`/`Notification` panic in workers
- the HTTPS error report can hang exit; a hidden bootstrap window gets revealed anyway in tray-only apps; a few `desktop.*` keys missing from the config schema

**2. Foundations**
- the in-process memory transport (#35675) plus two follow-ups (an absolute-form `http+memory:`
  target over TCP is refused; `node:http` serves on it)
- a stable custom-scheme app origin (`desktop.app.origin`, e.g. `myapp://app`): a scheme handler
  bridging into `Deno.serve` over the memory transport, plus a loopback relay for WebSockets that only
  accepts the app's exact `Origin`. This fixes #35444 and #35576. Storage persists across launches, and
  OAuth providers that check `Origin` accept it.
- handing the app identifier to every backend (per-app storage; #36768), building on #35662
- letting the runtime provide its own environment variables without `setenv` once the UI thread runs

**3. Features** (each needs its laufey half released first; we have PRs open there, littledivy/laufey#84, littledivy/laufey#85, littledivy/laufey#86, littledivy/laufey#87, littledivy/laufey#88, littledivy/laufey#89, littledivy/laufey#90, littledivy/laufey#91, littledivy/laufey#92 and littledivy/laufey#93):
deep links, opened files and single instance (completing #35465); OS scheme registration and the
`.msi` keys; maximize/minimize/fullscreen, size limits, bounds and screens, title-bar styles and
backdrops, `quit()` (on top of #36761 and #36789); menu accelerators on every backend; notification
actions and scheduling; native file dialogs; drag and drop with paths; HTML and image formats on
`navigator.clipboard`; global shortcuts; launch at login; DevTools control; `runOnMainThread`
(#36738); `ASWebAuthenticationSession` on macOS; native passkeys; and signed full-app updates (a
whole-bundle swap with rollback, which also addresses #36948. We'd like to discuss that design
with you before writing a PR).

Questions:
1. Would you like one PR per item, as listed, with a linked issue each, or the small fixes batched?
2. Should new APIs go under `Deno.desktop` (i.e. after #35939)? Is #35939 close to landing?
3. #35675: shall we rebase it and add our follow-ups, open a fresh PR crediting it, or leave it to you?
4. laufey: is it OK for Deno PRs to wait on laufey releases, and would you prefer we bump the laufey pin or you do?
5. For signed full-app updates: should they replace `Deno.autoUpdate` or sit beside it?
6. Would an end-to-end harness for packaged desktop apps (one small app per area, run on all three OSes) be useful upstream?

Several changes build on open work by others, and we'll keep their authorship and credit: #35662
(@crowlKats), #35675, #36761 (@petamoriken), #36789 (@sasivarnan), #36421 (@johnstonmatt), and on the
laufey side littledivy/laufey#77 (@diegoholiveira), littledivy/laufey#79 / littledivy/laufey#80 (@petamoriken) and littledivy/laufey#81 (@sasivarnan).

Version: Deno 2.9.7

`deno publish --dry-run` does not check for `actorNotScopeMember`, and therefore does not check the validity of the current authentication.

It's important to validate the current authentication for use cases like automated releases (https://github.com/sebbo2002/semantic-release-jsr/issues/181), as failing early avoids creating a git tag or GitHub Release before attempting the JSR publish and only then failing, leading to a git tag or GitHub Release without its associated JSR one.

Hopefully that functionality in Deno will be automatically replicated to `npx jsr` as well.

Version: Deno 2.9.7, aarch64-apple-darwin

When `deno lint --fix` applies a fix, the rewritten file loses its permissions. E.g. an executable script (755) becomes 644. `deno fmt` does not do this; it preserves permissions.

Repro:

```
echo 'window.foo = 1;' > a.ts
chmod 755 a.ts
deno lint --fix a.ts
stat -f %Sp a.ts   # -rw-r--r--  (expected -rwxr-xr-x)
```

**Title:** node:https: after piping a ranged `fs.createReadStream()` that is read in one chunk, the next request on the same keep-alive connection is never answered

**Version:** deno 2.9.7 (stable) and the current canary, 2.9.7+7a96f1b; Linux x86_64 (Debian 13)

### Description

A `node:https` server pipes `fs.createReadStream(file, { start, end })` into the response. When that range is read in a single chunk, the client gets the full response. The connection then stays open, but the next request sent on it is never answered.

These variants all work:

- `node:http` with the same handler;
- the same stream without `start`/`end`;
- a range large enough to need several reads;
- Node 24.21 with the same script.

The pattern is common in practice. Express's `express.static` uses `send`, which always passes `start` and `end` to `createReadStream`. Any Express app that serves HTTPS directly from Deno therefore leaves a connection stuck after every small static file, such as the favicon or a small JS chunk. A browser reusing its six connections to the host stalls within seconds: requests sit in "waiting", and Chrome reports `net::ERR_TOO_MANY_RETRIES`.

### Reproduction

```js
// repro.mjs — needs cert.pem / key.pem, e.g.:
// openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem -days 1 -subj /CN=localhost
import { createReadStream, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { createServer as https } from "node:https"
import { createServer as http } from "node:http"

writeFileSync("one-byte.txt", "x")
const handler = (req, res) => {
  if (req.url === "/") return res.end("ok")
  res.setHeader("Content-Length", "1")
  createReadStream("one-byte.txt", { start: 0, end: 0 }).pipe(res)
}
const [proto, port] = process.argv.slice(2)
const server = proto === "https" ? https({ cert: readFileSync("cert.pem"), key: readFileSync("key.pem") }, handler) : http(handler)
server.listen(Number(port), "127.0.0.1")
```

```sh
deno run -A repro.mjs https 8443 &
# two requests on one keep-alive connection: the file, then a plain response
curl -sk -m 4 -w "%{http_code} " -o /dev/null https://127.0.0.1:8443/file -o /dev/null https://127.0.0.1:8443/
```

| runtime | protocol | output |
|---|---|---|
| deno 2.9.7 | https | `200 000` — the second request times out |
| deno 2.9.7+7a96f1b (canary) | https | `200 000` |
| deno 2.9.7 | http | `200 200` |
| node 24.21.0 | https | `200 200` |

On the same `node:https` server, under deno 2.9.7, these handlers all return `200 200`:

- `createReadStream("one-byte.txt")` without `start`/`end`;
- `res.end(readFileSync(...))`;
- a 200 KB file with a range.

Destroying the read stream when the response finishes, as `send` does through `on-finished`, makes no difference either way.

### Expected

The second request on the connection is answered, as it is under `node:http` and under Node.

### Notes

- Possibly related, already fixed: #36496 (truncate streaming responses to content length), #36690 (preserve keep-alive after reading request body), #27223 (a stream chunk that hangs the connection). This case still reproduces on 2.9.7, which includes all three.
- Workaround: send `Connection: close` on every response, so each request gets a new connection.

## Version ``` deno 2.9.7 (stable, release, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) v8 15.0.245.2-rusty typescript 6.0.3 ``` OS: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (Linux 7.0.0-34-generic x86_64), Wayland session ## Description The [Closing the app](https://docs.deno.com/runtime/desktop/windows/#closing-the-app) docs say that calling `event.preventDefault()` in a `BrowserWindow` `close` listener stops the window from closing, for example to show a "Save?" dialog: ```ts win.addEventListener("close", async (e) => { if (hasUnsavedChanges) { e.preventDefault(); const ok = await win.executeJs("confirm('Discard changes?')"); if (ok) win.close(); } }); ``` That doesn't work. The listener runs, but the event isn't cancelable, `preventDefault()` does nothing, and the window closes anyway. A desktop app has no way to confirm or block a user-initiated close (the native close button or Alt+F4). From reading the source: - `cli/rt/desktop.rs`, in the `closeRequested` case: the event is dispatched as `new Event("close")`. That event isn't cancelable, and the result of `dispatchEvent` is ignored. - `cli/rt_desktop/lib.rs`, in `on_close_requested`: since #36718, after forwarding `CloseRequested` to JS the runtime calls `laufey::Window::from_id(ev.window_id).close()` straight away. The comment there says the JS "close" event "is a plain notification (not cancelable)". As far as I can tell from the source, the event has never been cancelable in any 2.9.x release. On 2.9.4/2.9.5 (laufey 0.5.0) the window closes natively without waiting for JS. On 2.9.6 (laufey 0.7.0) it never closes at all (#36715). So the docs example has never worked. ## Reproduction `main.ts`: ```ts Deno.serve(() => new Response( "

Click the window's close button (X)

" + "

Expected: the window stays open.

", { headers: { "content-type": "text/html" } }, ) ); // The first construction adopts the startup window. const win = new Deno.BrowserWindow({ title: "close preventDefault repro" }); win.addEventListener("close", (e) => { e.preventDefault(); console.log( `close event: cancelable=${e.cancelable} defaultPrevented=${e.defaultPrevented}`, ); }); ``` Run, then click the window's close button (X) or press Alt+F4: ```sh deno desktop --hmr main.ts ``` ## Actual output The window closes, and the terminal shows: ``` close event: cancelable=false defaultPrevented=false ``` ## Expected vs actual - expected: `cancelable=true defaultPrevented=true`, and the window stays open until `win.close()` is called - actual: `cancelable=false defaultPrevented=false`, and the window closes ## Possible fix laufey 0.7.0 already defers the close until `Window::close()` is called, so the runtime could let JS decide: - `cli/rt_desktop/lib.rs`: don't call `Window::close()` in `on_close_requested`, and leave `closed_windows`/`open_windows` alone until the close actually goes ahead. - `cli/rt/desktop.rs`: dispatch `new Event("close", { cancelable: true })`, and call `target.close()` if `dispatchEvent` returns `true` (not prevented). If cancelling isn't meant to be supported, the docs example should be removed instead. ## Impact Desktop apps can't ask "Do you want to close?" or "Save changes?" before quitting, even though the docs show exactly that pattern. Apps that follow the docs lose unsaved state when the user closes the window, and nothing logs an error, so it's easy to assume the listener isn't attached rather than that the event can't be cancelled.

body_text:
I just finished [JS13K](https://www.js13kgames.com) and had to basically design my whole own pipeline and/or ship everything as tuples since the [mangleProps option](https://esbuild.github.io/api/#mangle-props) wasn't exposed in the deno bundler.

The API would look like:

```ts
Deno.bundle({ mangleProps: /_$/ });
```

If y'all're worried about this being abused, just supporting `--mangle-quoted` could be a decent compromise. Not as compact, but every "mangle" is opt-in.

```ts
Deno.bundle({ mangleQuoted: true });
```

If interested, I'm open to making this contribution.

**Version:** deno 2.9.7 (stable, release, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)
 
In Deno's `node:fs`, file times only keep milliseconds, in both directions:
 
- **writing:** `fs.utimesSync(f, 1700000000.123456789, ...)` sets the file's mtime to
  `.123000000` (Node sets `.123456000`);
- **reading:** `fs.statSync(f).mtimeMs` is a whole number of milliseconds, and even
  `fs.statSync(f, { bigint: true }).mtimeNs` is a whole number of milliseconds times
  10^6, also for a file whose times have nanoseconds on disk (set by `touch`).
Repro:
 
```js
import fs from "node:fs";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
 
const f = path.join(fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "subms-")), "f");
fs.writeFileSync(f, "x");
fs.utimesSync(f, 1700000000.123456789, 1700000000.123456789);
console.log(fs.statSync(f).mtimeMs);
console.log(fs.statSync(f, { bigint: true }).mtimeNs);
```
 
| | Deno 2.9.7 | Node 22.22.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `mtimeMs` | `1700000000123` | `1700000000123.456` |
| `mtimeNs` (bigint) | `1700000000123000000n` | `1700000000123456000n` |
| on disk after `utimesSync` (`stat -c %y`) | `...20.123000000` | `...20.123456000` |
 
Reading a file set with `touch -d @1700000000.123456789 f` (on disk
`...20.123456789`): Deno's `fs.statSync(f, { bigint: true }).mtimeNs` is
`1700000000123000000n`, Node's is `1700000000123456789n`. `Deno.statSync` /
`Deno.utimeSync` behave the same way (milliseconds).
 
**Expected:** the same precision as Node: `utimes` passes the fractional seconds on
(Node: microseconds), and `stat` reports what the file system has (`mtimeMs` with a
fraction, `mtimeNs` / `atimeNs` / `ctimeNs` / `birthtimeNs` with the nanoseconds).
 
**Why it matters:** Emscripten's test `test_fs_subms_times` (sub-millisecond file
times through NODEFS / NODERAWFS, i.e. host files through `node:fs`) cannot pass
under Deno, so it was disabled there: emscripten-core/emscripten#27898.

The Vulkan extension `VK_KHR_swapchain_mutable_format` allows configuring a view of a swapchain surface in a different format. This is useful to translate between sRGB and linear RGB. The extension is widely supported on desktop but support is [spottier on Android](https://vulkan.gpuinfo.org/displayextensiondetail.php?age=recent&apiversion=all&extension=VK_KHR_swapchain_mutable_format).

The WebGPU API offers configuration of `viewFormats` in `GPUCanvasConfiguration`, and `wgpu` has a corresponding field in `SurfaceConfiguration`. However, on devices that lack `VK_KHR_swapchain_mutable_format`, attempts to configure a non-identity view format mapping will fail due to lacking the `SURFACE_VIEW_FORMATS` downlevel flag.

Firefox and Servo do not use a swapchain to present WebGPU canvases, so are willing to treat adapters as WebGPU compliant even if they lack `SURFACE_VIEW_FORMATS` (https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/pull/10425). I am not sure the current compliant-adapter filtering behavior in Deno, but if Deno wants to support surface view formats on devices that do not have `VK_KHR_swapchain_mutable_format`, a manual blit will be needed (see closed PR https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/pull/10357 for an example). Alternatively, Deno could leave the gap in place (in which case a validation error not described by the WebGPU spec would be raised on these devices), or could decline to expose a GPU through WebGPU if it lacks `SURFACE_VIEW_FORMATS` (which would require a special case on top of `wgpu`'s compliant adapter determination).

Related:
- #23563 <!-- Tracking issue for using WebGPU to render on the window of the desktop environment -->
- https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/issues/10340
- https://github.com/servo/servo/issues/48024
- https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2077117 (issue claims a polyfill is needed, but that is incorrect because Firefox doesn't present with a Vulkan swapchain).

### Summary

For `npm:` specifiers, `deno check` fails to find type declarations for **subpath** exports in two cases that TypeScript (`moduleResolution: nodenext`) and Node resolve correctly, while `deno run` executes all of them fine:

- the export entry has no `types` condition and the declaration lives next to the **resolved** file (e.g. `dist/foo.d.ts` for `"./foo": "./dist/foo.js"`)
- the export key is a **pattern** (`"./*"`), even when that entry *does* have a `types` condition

Resolving types next to the resolved target is what TypeScript does, so packages that ship `dist/*.js` with sibling `dist/*.d.ts` end up untyped on Deno.

Version: `deno 2.9.7+a18ce33` (canary, release, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc), Windows.

### Real-world reproduction (no setup needed)

```sh
echo 'import { Effect } from "npm:effect/Effect"; console.log(typeof Effect);' > main.ts
deno check main.ts
```

```
TS2307 [ERROR]: Cannot find module 'npm:effect/Effect' or its corresponding type declarations.
```

`effect@4.0.0-rc.112` has `"./*": "./dist/*.js"` and ships `dist/Effect.d.ts` right next to `dist/Effect.js`. The package root works, so this is specific to subpaths:

| specifier | result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm:effect` (`".": "./dist/index.js"`) | resolves types |
| `npm:effect/Effect` (`"./*": "./dist/*.js"`, `dist/Effect.d.ts` present) | `TS2307` |
| `npm:effect/unstable/http` (`"./unstable/http": "./dist/unstable/http/index.js"`, `dist/unstable/http/index.d.ts` present) | `TS2307` |
| `npm:zod/v4` (entry has a `types` condition) | resolves types |

`deno run` on all of these prints the expected value, so only type resolution is affected.

### Minimal repro

Each package below is packed with `bun pm pack` (or `npm pack`) and served from a local registry (`NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY`), then checked with a one-line `main.ts` that imports `npm:<pkg>/foo`:

| package `exports` | declaration location | `deno check` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"./foo": { "types": "./dist/foo.d.ts", "default": "./dist/foo.js" }` | `dist/foo.d.ts` | ok |
| `"./foo": { "default": "./dist/foo.js" }` | `dist/foo.d.ts` | `TS2307` |
| `"./foo": { "default": "./foo.js" }` | `foo.d.ts` (package root) | ok |
| `"./*": { "types": "./dist/*.d.ts", "default": "./dist/*.js" }` | `dist/foo.d.ts` | `TS2307` |
| `"./*": { "default": "./dist/*.js" }` | `dist/foo.d.ts` | `TS2307` |
| `".": { "default": "./dist/index.js" }` | `dist/index.d.ts` | ok |
| `"main": "./dist/index.js"` | `dist/index.d.ts` | ok |

The last two rows show the package root behaving differently from subpaths: for the root entry Deno does look next to the resolved target.

The `"./*"` package above resolves fine when it is loaded from `node_modules` (`"nodeModulesDir": "manual"`, bare specifier instead of `npm:`), so this is specific to the `npm:` resolver.

`tsc --noEmit` with `"module": "nodenext"` / `"moduleResolution": "nodenext"` resolves every row above (including the `"./*"` ones) to the right declaration file.

### Expected

`deno check` should resolve declarations the same way TypeScript does: apply the `types` condition for pattern keys too, and when an entry has no `types` condition, fall back to the declaration file next to the resolved target rather than `<package root>/<subpath>.d.ts`.

body_text:
### Summary

When a program running with `--no-config` imports a module from an `https:` URL whose own imports pull in an npm graph, peer dependencies in that graph are resolved to the **newest published version even when it is outside the declared peer range**. The same graph resolved statically (`deno info`) — or resolved by a run that has a config file present — picks the highest version that satisfies the range instead. Programs then crash at `require()` time because the out-of-range peer is not API-compatible.

### Versions

* `deno 2.9.7 (stable, release, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)`
* `deno 2.9.7+a18ce33 (canary, release, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)` (commit `a18ce33`, 2026-10-06)
* Windows 11; both binaries reproduce the same behaviour.

### Minimal repro

`repro.mjs` (no config file next to it):

```js
await import('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steve02081504/my-eslint-config/master/deno.mjs')
```

That remote module imports `npm:eslint-plugin-jsdoc`, which depends on `@typescript-eslint/utils@8.71.1` → `@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree@8.71.1`, whose peer is `typescript@>=4.8.4 <6.1.0`. `typescript@7.0.2` is `latest` and does **not** satisfy that range; `typescript@6.0.3` does.

1. Static resolution — correct (highest satisfying version):

```
$ deno info --no-config https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steve02081504/my-eslint-config/master/deno.mjs
...
npm:/@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree@8.71.1_typescript@6.0.3 (382.58KB)
npm:/typescript@6.0.3 (23.22MB)
```

2. Runtime with `--no-config` — wrong (newest, out of range):

```
$ deno run --allow-all --no-config repro.mjs
Warning The following peer dependency issues were found:
└─┬ eslint-plugin-jsdoc@65.2.0 (imported by https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steve02081504/my-eslint-config/master/deno.mjs)
  └─┬ @typescript-eslint/utils@8.71.1
    ├─┬ @typescript-eslint/typescript-estree@8.71.1
    │ ├─┬ @typescript-eslint/project-service@8.71.1
    │ │ ├─┬ @typescript-eslint/tsconfig-utils@8.71.1
    │ │ │ └── peer typescript@>=4.8.4 <6.1.0: resolved to 7.0.2
    │ │ └── peer typescript@>=4.8.4 <6.1.0: resolved to 7.0.2
    │ └── peer typescript@>=4.8.4 <6.1.0: resolved to 7.0.2
    └── peer typescript@>=4.8.4 <6.1.0: resolved to 7.0.2
```

3. Same run with a `deno.json` present (e.g. `{ "nodeModulesDir": "none" }`) — no peer warning, resolves `typescript@6.0.3`.

Also reproduced with the jsDelivr copy of the same module (`https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/steve02081504/my-eslint-config/deno.mjs`), so it is not host-specific.

### Real-world impact

`fount` documents linting through a `deno install`-generated shim (`~/.deno/bin/eslint`), whose command is:

```
deno run --allow-all --minimum-dependency-age 0 --no-config npm:eslint
```

and whose flat config (`eslint.config.mjs`) imports the remote config above. eslint loads that config at runtime, the peer resolves to `typescript@7.0.2`, and `@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree` crashes while being required, because TypeScript 7's package root no longer exposes the compiler API (`"exports"."."` is `./lib/version.cjs`; the API moved to `typescript/unstable/*`), so `ts.Extension` is `undefined`:

```
ESLint: 10.12.0

TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'Cjs')
    at Object.<anonymous> (.../npm/registry.npmjs.org/@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree/8.71.1/dist/create-program/shared.js:64:18)
    at Object.<anonymous> (.../typescript-estree/8.71.1/dist/create-program/getWatchProgramsForProjects.js:45:18)
```

Exit code 2, no file is ever linted — even though `typescript@6.0.3`, which satisfies the peer range, is available and is what the static resolver selects.

### Expected

`deno run` (runtime) and `deno info` (static) should agree on peer resolution, and a peer dependency should not be auto-installed at a version outside its declared range. Failing that, resolution should fail loudly rather than warn and install an incompatible version.

### Workarounds

* Adding `import 'npm:typescript@6.0.3';` to the program (or to the config that is imported at runtime) makes the peer resolve to 6.0.3 and the crash disappears. This is what I use locally for now.
* Running without `--no-config` avoids it, but the shim that `deno install` generates passes `--no-config`, so that is not something a user of that shim can change.

### Possibly related

* #36607 ("match peer fallbacks when checking peer resolution cache") — this graph resolves `typescript` through the auto-installed peer fallbacks in both cases, so the fallback/cache keying may be where the two paths diverge.

body_text:
## Problem

`child_process.spawnSync`, `execFileSync` and `execSync` give the child the parent's whole environment plus the `env` they are passed. Node gives the child only the `env` it is passed. So a variable that the caller removed from `env` still reaches the child.

Async `spawn` was fixed for this in #27343 (PR #27340), and it now clears the environment. The sync path was not fixed. On `main` (a18ce33715e30cd2b0d99c7e322ef11a65490e4d), `ext/node/polyfills/internal/child_process.ts` has two call sites:

- `ChildProcess` constructor (async `spawn`): `nodeSpawnChild(cmd, { args: cmdArgs, clearEnv: true, cwd, env, ... })`
- `spawnSync`: `nodeSpawnSyncChild({ args: [...], cwd, env: mapValues(env, ...), ..., clearEnv: false, ... })`

`normalizeSpawnArguments` already sets `env` to `options.env || Deno.env.toObject()`. So `clearEnv: true` would not change the default case, where no `env` is passed.

This hit us on GitHub Actions. A test removed `CI` from a copy of `process.env` and ran a script with `execFileSync`. The script still saw `CI=true` on every Deno runner, and it took its CI branch: [disk-space-saviour#31](https://github.com/link-foundation/disk-space-saviour/issues/31), run [38003106785](https://github.com/link-foundation/disk-space-saviour/actions/runs/38003106785).

## Reproduce

```js
// probe.mjs
import { spawn, spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

const env = { ...process.env };
delete env.PROBE;
const script = 'echo "${PROBE-<unset>}"';

console.log('spawnSync:', spawnSync('sh', ['-c', script], { env, encoding: 'utf8' }).stdout.trim());
spawn('sh', ['-c', script], { env, stdio: 'inherit' }).on('close', () => {});
```

```sh
PROBE=leaked node probe.mjs          # spawnSync: <unset>   then  <unset>
PROBE=leaked deno run -A probe.mjs   # spawnSync: leaked    then  <unset>
```

(Deno 2.9.6.) The exact repro from #27343 shows the same thing with the sync API: `spawnSync('env', { env: { test: 'test' } })` prints the parent's variables as well as `test=test`.

## Workaround

Pass a blank value instead of deleting the key, as in `{ ...process.env, CI: '' }`. A blank value overrides the parent's value on every runtime. This only helps when the child treats an empty variable as unset.

## Suggested fix

In `spawnSync` in `ext/node/polyfills/internal/child_process.ts`, pass `clearEnv: true` as the async path does:

```diff
       uid,
       gid,
-      clearEnv: false,
+      clearEnv: true,
       extraStdio: extraStdioNormalized,
```

Port Node's `test-child-process-spawnsync-env.js` and an `execFileSync` variant of the #27343 test, to keep the sync path from drifting again.

body_text:
Version: Deno 2.9.7

### What happened

A desktop app packaged with `deno desktop --engine=quickjs` works on Deno
2.9.6 and fails on 2.9.7. The server starts and binds its port, but the first
request crashes module resolution, so the window stays blank.

The app is open source (GPL-3.0): https://gitlab.com/kenble/dirdap/dirdap-app
— the failing build is release 0.2.3. No LDAP server is needed to reproduce:
the crash happens at startup, before any connection.

### Error

Runtime loaded successfully from: .../libruntime.dylib
Runtime started
Listening on http://127.0.0.1:58522/
TypeError: Cannot resolve module "ext:core/mod.js" from "node:net"
    at async file:///.../_fresh/server/server-entry.mjs:6034:32
    ...
    code: "ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND"

### Repro

1. Fresh 2 app using an npm package that imports `node:net`
   (reproduced with `npm:ldapts@9.2.0`, which opens the LDAP socket
   through `net`).
2. `deno desktop --engine=quickjs --allow-net --allow-read --allow-write
   --allow-env --target aarch64-apple-darwin --output app.dmg .`
3. Install and launch the app: the window opens but never renders.

### Environment

- Deno 2.9.7 (stable, release, aarch64-apple-darwin) — broken
- Deno 2.9.6 (same machine, same build) — works

### Notes

- The built bundle carries `node:net` as a bare specifier (it comes from
  `npm:ldapts`; the app does not import `node:net` directly).
- Under the desktop runtime, Deno's `node:net` shim resolves to
  `ext:core/mod.js`, which is not mapped in the QuickJS desktop runtime —
  the CLI runtime resolves it fine.
- No app code changed between the two builds; only the Deno version differs.

#36141 (`test-http2-ping-settings-heapdump.js` flaky on macos-aarch64) was closed by #36230 on 2026-08-02, but the test has been failing again on `main` since late September. It now fails on both macOS architectures, and `test-http2-compat-serverresponse-close.js` sometimes fails alongside it. The failures are in the `test node_compat (1/3) release macos-*` job, while Linux and Windows pass on the same commits.

**Recent failing `main` runs**

```
Command: NODE_TEST_KNOWN_GLOBALS=0 NODE_SKIP_FLAG_CHECK=1 NODE_OPTIONS='' deno run -A --quiet --unsafe-proto test/parallel/test-http2-ping-settings-heapdump.js
...
failed tests:

1 failed of 3670
```

- #36230 ("fix(ext/node): don't fire http2 settings callback after session destroy") fixed the original aarch64 flake. The new failures look like the same family of http2 session-teardown races, now showing up on x86_64 macOS too.
- `test-http2-multistream-destroy-on-read-tls.js` also failed once (run 37485420724), so other http2 tests may be affected.
- Until there's a real fix, one option is to skip these on macOS only (`"darwin": false` with a `reason` in `tests/node_compat/config.jsonc`). Linux and Windows coverage would stay.

Three top-level keys are also listed twice: `test-dns-lookup-promises.js`, `test-tls-client-resume.js` and `test-tls-client-resume-12.js`, all with identical `{}` values.

body_text:
Version: Deno 2.9.7

## Background

#35138 caches 404 responses for 15 minutes and deliberately skips authenticated requests, since private hosts respond with 404 to unauthorized requests. However, the [cache read path](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/a18ce33715e30cd2b0d99c7e322ef11a65490e4d/libs/cache_dir/file_fetcher/mod.rs#L729-L744) serves a cached 404 without checking whether the current request carries credentials. A single run without `DENO_AUTH_TOKENS` therefore blocks a private module (e.g. on `raw.githubusercontent.com`) for 15 minutes, even after the token is set.

## Steps to reproduce

```ts
// server.ts
Deno.serve({ port: 4545 }, (req) =>
  req.headers.get("authorization") === "Bearer secret"
    ? new Response("export default 1;", { headers: { "content-type": "application/javascript" } })
    : new Response("not found", { status: 404 }));
```

```sh
deno run --allow-net server.ts &
export DENO_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
deno cache http://localhost:4545/mod.js
DENO_AUTH_TOKENS=secret@localhost:4545 deno cache http://localhost:4545/mod.js
```

## Expected behavior

The second `deno cache` sends the token and succeeds, as it does with `--reload`.

## Actual behavior

The second `deno cache` fails with `error: Module not found "http://localhost:4545/mod.js".` without sending a request, until the entry expires or `--reload` is used.

## Background

#35138 caches 404 responses for 15 minutes and deliberately skips authenticated requests, since private hosts respond with 404 to unauthorized requests. However, the [cache read path](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/a18ce33715e30cd2b0d99c7e322ef11a65490e4d/libs/cache_dir/file_fetcher/mod.rs#L729-L744) serves a cached 404 without checking whether the current request carries credentials. A single run without `DENO_AUTH_TOKENS` therefore blocks a private module (e.g. on `raw.githubusercontent.com`) for 15 minutes, even after the token is set.

## Steps to reproduce

```ts
// server.ts
Deno.serve({ port: 4545 }, (req) =>
  req.headers.get("authorization") === "Bearer secret"
    ? new Response("export default 1;", { headers: { "content-type": "application/javascript" } })
    : new Response("not found", { status: 404 }));
```

```sh
deno run --allow-net server.ts &
export DENO_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
deno cache http://localhost:4545/mod.js
DENO_AUTH_TOKENS=secret@localhost:4545 deno cache http://localhost:4545/mod.js
```

## Expected behavior

The second `deno cache` sends the token and succeeds, as it does with `--reload`.

## Actual behavior

The second `deno cache` fails with `error: Module not found "http://localhost:4545/mod.js".` without sending a request, until the entry expires or `--reload` is used.

body_text:
### What

In `deno desktop` apps, a page that saves a file (`<a download>`, a blob
export, a `Content-Disposition: attachment` response) has no consistent save
flow:

- Linux (webview/WebKitGTK): the file is written silently into the XDG
  downloads directory, with no UI.
- Windows (webview/WebView2): WebView2's own in-app download UI.
- macOS (webview/WKWebView): the download can't proceed (no destination
  without host support).
- CEF backend: page downloads are cancelled.

### Request

Ask where to save using the OS save dialog, consistently on every backend:
`NSSavePanel` on macOS, `IFileSaveDialog` on Windows, `GtkFileChooserDialog`
on Linux, CEF's Save As on the CEF backend. The engine already streams the
bytes; the destination decision is the only missing piece.

### Proposal

The laufey side is implemented in littledivy/laufey#126. Once that PR is
merged and a laufey release is cut, the Deno-side change is a pin bump:

- `cli/rt_desktop/Cargo.toml` (`laufey = "0.7.0"` -> new release)
- regenerate `cli/laufey_sums.lock`
- update the `runtime/desktop/dialogs` docs (its "native file-picker API is
  on the roadmap" note covers pickers, not downloads)

### Design note

The dialog is shown for every page-triggered download; on Linux this replaces
WebKitGTK's silent save-to-Downloads default. If the preferred default is
silent-with-a-setting, that is worth deciding here — the laufey change can be
made configurable.

### Blocked on

littledivy/laufey#126 and its release. The Deno-side PR follows once the
release exists.
