Version: Deno 2.9.6, 2.9.7 and `main` (a18ce3371), Linux x86_64 `deno lint` with a lint plugin occasionally segfaults on exit, roughly 1–2% of runs when several run in parallel. The crash is a use-after-free in deno_core's isolate teardown: the op contexts that hold each op's fast-call `CFunction` overload are freed before the isolate is disposed, while a concurrent TurboFan job may still read them. ### Mechanism - With V8 150.x, `FunctionTemplateInfo` stores raw pointers to the `CFunction` overloads passed to `FunctionTemplate::build_fast`. deno_core passes a slice that lives inside each `OpCtx` (`OpCtx::fast_fn_overloads`, `libs/core/ops.rs`). The comment there assumes that "`OpCtx` lives until isolate disposal". - It doesn't. `::drop` calls `cleanup()`, which calls `JsRealmInner::destroy()`. That drops the realm's `ContextState`, and with it `op_ctxs`, before `ManuallyDrop::drop(&mut self.v8_isolate)`. V8 only cancels and joins its concurrent optimization jobs inside `Isolate::Dispose`. - A TurboFan job still running at that point that inlines a fast API call reads the freed slice: ``` OptimizingCompileTaskExecutor::CompileTask::Run PipelineCompilationJob::ExecuteJobImpl InliningPhase JSCallReducer::ReduceCallApiFunction fast_api_call::GetFastApiCallTarget FunctionTemplateInfoRef::c_functions_with_signatures v8/src/compiler/heap-refs.cc:2071 <-- SIGSEGV ``` When it crashes, the lint `PluginHost` thread is in `::drop`, and the main thread is dropping the `CliFactory` at the end of `lint()` (`cli/tools/lint/mod.rs`). - There is also a secondary cause: `PluginHost::create` (`cli/tools/lint/plugins.rs`) detaches the plugin host thread (`let _join_handle = std::thread::spawn(...)`), so the process can reach `exit()` while that thread is still tearing down its isolate. This probably dates from the V8 150 upgrade (#36098), which made the overload slice need to outlive the templates. `OpCtx` was later reshaped in #36693 / #36696. ### Reproduction You need a lint plugin, a few medium-sized files, and parallel runs (so TurboFan is still busy when a run finishes). The scripts below need nothing besides `deno`.
setup.sh: creates the project ```sh #!/usr/bin/env bash # Creates a lint project: a small plugin and a few generated ~500-line files. set -euo pipefail dir=${1:-lint-repro} mkdir -p "$dir/src" cd "$dir" cat > deno.json <<'JSON' { "lint": { "plugins": ["./plugin.ts"] } } JSON cat > plugin.ts <<'TS' export default { name: "repro", rules: { "visit-all": { create(ctx) { let n = 0; return { Identifier(node) { n += node.name.length; }, CallExpression(node) { n += node.arguments.length; }, MemberExpression(node) { if (node.computed) n++; }, "FunctionDeclaration > Identifier"(node) { n += node.range[0]; }, StringLiteral(node) { n += node.value.length; }, "Program:exit"() { if (n < 0) ctx.report({ node: ctx.sourceCode.ast, message: String(n) }); }, }; }, }, }, } satisfies Deno.lint.Plugin; TS for f in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do { echo "// generated file $f" for i in $(seq 1 60); do cat < s.length > ${i}).map((s) => s.trim()); } TS done } > "src/file$f.ts" done wc -l src/*.ts | tail -1 ```
run.sh: runs deno lint N times, P in parallel, and counts exit codes ```sh #!/usr/bin/env bash # Usage: run.sh [parallelism] # Runs `deno lint` times, at a time, and counts crashes. deno=$1; dir=$2; runs=$3; par=${4:-4} cd "$dir" seq 1 "$runs" | xargs -P "$par" -I{} sh -c '"$0" lint -q >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $?' "$deno" \ | sort | uniq -c ```
```sh bash setup.sh proj bash run.sh "$(which deno)" proj 1000 4 # 981 0 # 19 139 <- SIGSEGV ``` ### Measurements (Linux x86_64, 8 cores, 4 parallel runs) | Binary / setup | SIGSEGV (exit 139) | |---|---| | 2.9.7 release | 19 / 1000 | | 2.9.7 release, `DENO_V8_FLAGS=--no-concurrent-recompilation` | 0 / 1000 | | `main` (a18ce3371, `--profile release-lite`) | 13 / 1000, 28 / 2000 | On a larger real-world project I saw the same pattern: 2.9.6 crashed 16/1000, 2.9.7 crashed 9/1000, 17/1000 and 23/1500, there were no crashes without the lint plugin (0/1000), and none when running sequentially (0/400). Backtrace of the faulting thread from the `main` build under gdb: ``` Thread 2 "V8 DefaultWorke" received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault. #0 c_functions_with_signatures () at v8/src/compiler/heap-refs.cc:2071 #1 v8::internal::compiler::fast_api_call::GetFastApiCallTarget(JSHeapBroker*, FunctionTemplateInfoRef, unsigned long) at v8/src/compiler/fast-api-calls.cc:387 #2 v8::internal::compiler::JSCallReducer::ReduceCallApiFunction(Node*, SharedFunctionInfoRef) at v8/src/compiler/js-call-reducer.cc:4597 #3 v8::internal::compiler::JSCallReducer::ReduceJSCall(Node*, SharedFunctionInfoRef) #4 v8::internal::compiler::JSCallReducer::ReduceJSCall(Node*) at v8/src/compiler/js-call-reducer.cc:5177 #5 v8::internal::compiler::GraphReducer::Reduce(Node*) ... #8 v8::internal::compiler::InliningPhase::Run(TFPipelineData*, Zone*) at v8/src/compiler/pipeline.cc:952 #10 v8::internal::compiler::PipelineImpl::CreateGraph(Linkage*) #11 v8::internal::compiler::PipelineCompilationJob::ExecuteJobImpl(RuntimeCallStats*, LocalIsolate*) #12 v8::internal::OptimizedCompilationJob::ExecuteJob(RuntimeCallStats*, LocalIsolate*) #13 v8::internal::OptimizingCompileTaskExecutor::CompileTask::Run(JobDelegate*) at v8/src/compiler-dispatcher/optimizing-compile-dispatcher.cc:60 #14 v8::platform::DefaultJobWorker::Run() ``` At the same moment, the plugin host thread is inside `InnerIsolateState::drop`, past `cleanup()` (in this sample it is dropping `JsRuntimeState`, before the isolate): ``` #21 core::ptr::drop_in_place #22 alloc::rc::Rc::drop_slow #23 ::drop #24 core::ptr::drop_in_place ``` The crash needs concurrent recompilation (it never happens with `--no-concurrent-recompilation`), a lint plugin (which gives the plugin host its own isolate that is torn down at exit), and other load on the machine (sequential runs don't crash). ### Suggested fix Keep the op contexts alive until the isolate has been disposed: `JsRealmInner::destroy()` hands them back, and `InnerIsolateState` drops them only after `v8_isolate`. Separately, keep the lint `PluginHost` thread's `JoinHandle` and wait for it on drop, with a bound. I'll open a PR. _The investigation and this write-up were done with AI assistance (Claude Code)._

## The state of Deno after the Cloudflare announcement

Last week we announced that the Deno company is joining Cloudflare ([Deno blog post](https://deno.com/blog/cloudflare), [Cloudflare blog post](https://blog.cloudflare.com/deno-joins-cloudflare/)).


This issue explains where the Deno runtime stands right now, and we'll keep it pinned and updated as things change.


## What's happening

The Deno Company (now Cloudflare) will continue maintain Deno until October 2027:

- **Monthly releases.** We'll publish a 2.9.x LTS release every month with bug   fixes and security updates.
- **Security reports.** Report vulnerabilities the same way as before (see [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md)). We'll triage reports as they come in.
- **Canary builds.** Canary builds will keep being published automatically from `main`, so new fixes show up there first.

## What's changing

Version: Deno 2.9.4

`crypto.subtle.importKey` accepts P-256, P-384, and P-521 public keys whose point is not on the curve, for the `jwk`, `raw`, and `spki` formats. The Web Crypto spec says import must throw a `DataError` in that case ("If the key value is not a valid point on the Elliptic Curve identified by the namedCurve member of normalizedAlgorithm throw a DataError"). Node.js, Bun, Chromium, and Firefox all reject these keys at import.

```js
const b64 = (bytes) => btoa(String.fromCharCode(...bytes)).replace(/\+/g, "-").replace(/\//g, "_").replace(/=+$/, "");
const jwk = { kty: "EC", crv: "P-256", x: b64(new Uint8Array(32).fill(1)), y: b64(new Uint8Array(32).fill(1)) };

const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey("jwk", jwk, { name: "ECDH", namedCurve: "P-256" }, true, []);
// Expected: DataError. Actual: resolves.
```

The key then fails later, with a different error for each operation:

- `exportKey("jwk" | "spki")`: `OperationError: expected valid public EC key`
- ECDSA `verify`: `TypeError: Invalid key format`
- ECDH `deriveBits`: `TypeError: Unexpected error decoding private key` (the private key is fine; it is the public key that is invalid)

`deriveBits` does reject the point, so ECDH never computes a shared secret from it. This is a conformance problem, not an invalid-curve attack.

The import code only builds or parses the SEC1 encoding and checks for the identity point. `EncodedPoint::from_affine_coordinates` (JWK) and `EncodedPoint::from_bytes` (raw, spki) in `ext/crypto/[import_key.rs](https://github.com/tmp/ext/crypto/import_key.rs)` don't check that the point is on the curve. The check happens later, when `PublicKey::from_encoded_point` is called in `deriveBits`, and that failure is mapped to `CryptoError::DecodePrivateKey`. Validating with `PublicKey::from_encoded_point` (or `from_sec1_bytes`) at import time and returning a `DataError` would fix the import and make the later errors unreachable.

Investigated with help from Claude, the reproduction and results were verified by hand.

Version: deno_core 0.411.0 (and `main`), sourcemap 9.2.0 (this repo's lockfile; >= 9.3.0 adds a second trigger, see comments)

### What happened

When a JS error is thrown, source-mapping its stack trace (in `format_stack_trace`) aborts the process with an overflow panic:

```
thread '...' panicked at deno_core-0.411.0/source_map.rs:143:27:
attempt to add with overflow
   2: core::panicking::panic_const::panic_const_add_overflow
   3: <deno_core::source_map::SourceMapper>::apply_source_map
   4: deno_core::error::apply_source_map
   5: <deno_core::error::JsStackFrame>::from_callsite_object
   6: deno_core::error::format_stack_trace
   7: deno_core::error::prepare_stack_trace_callback
      ... (V8 PrepareStackTrace callback)
  21: <deno_core::error::JsError>::inner_from_v8_exception
  22: <deno_core::error::JsError>::from_v8_exception
  23: deno_core::error::exception_to_err
  24: deno_core::error::exception_to_err_result
  25: <deno_core::runtime::jsruntime::JsRuntime>::resolve_promise_inner
  26: deno_core::runtime::bindings::watch_promise
      ... (V8 function callback)
```

(Published `deno_core 0.411.0`; the panicking line is `source_map.rs:143`, which is `libs/core/source_map.rs:233` on `main`.)

This aborts only on an overflow-checks build; a release build wraps to a wrong line number instead.

### Likely cause

The token's `get_src_line()` is `u32::MAX`, so `apply_source_map`'s `token.get_src_line() + 1` overflows. The `sourcemap` decoder computes `src_line = (i64::from(src_line) + delta) as u32` (`decoder.rs:201`), so a cumulative source line of `-1` wraps to `u32::MAX`.

A negative source line is out of spec, so the source map is malformed. It came from a bundler I was using, not from deno, so producing the bad map is not a deno bug. I am only flagging the deno_core side in case it is worth guarding: it aborts on such input rather than tolerating it. deno hardened a different source-map panic before (#21989), so this seemed worth raising in the same spirit.

### Reproduction

Minimal unit test for `libs/core/source_map.rs`. The mapping `"AADA"` is `[genCol 0, srcIdx 0, srcLine delta -1, srcCol 0]`, so the decoded token `src_line` is `u32::MAX`:

Version: Deno 2.7.14 (aarch64-apple-darwin)

We bundle Deno in Quarto, and our nightly CI on GitHub `macos-latest` (Apple Silicon) sees a `Segmentation fault: 11` about 20ms after the deno process starts. It is rare: 3 crashes in about 40 nightly runs, each run launching deno ~2000 times, each time during a different render, and never on our x86_64 Linux runners. Users reported the same random crash on Apple Silicon since 2024 (quarto-dev/quarto-cli#10426), so it is not only a CI thing.

We collected the macOS crash reports for two of them. Both have the same faulting stack at the same image offsets: `EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV)`, `KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0000000000000000`, pc at 0, on a `tokio-runtime-worker` thread. Symbolicated with panic.deno.com:

- Crashing thread: https://panic.deno.com/v2.7.14/aarch64-apple-darwin/o9ng5Bg4kg5Bgsng5Bol0ntBot5qF4v2qFgu98qB40yqFo46vFg9y7wBgxz8wB4-k1uB
- Another worker thread at the same moment: https://panic.deno.com/v2.7.14/aarch64-apple-darwin/45gm5Bwuhh5Bwxnr5Bwm-j5Bgp0ntBot5qF4v2qFgu98qB40yqFo46vFg9y7wBgxz8wB4-k1uB

From what I can tell, two `CacheDB::spawn_eager_init_thread` tasks open their connections in parallel:

https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/2d674b25625bcc367853d00fe86f6e84390f88cb/cli/cache/cache_db.rs#L213-L220

The crashing thread goes `ensure_safe_sqlite_threading_mode` -> `sqlite3_mutex_alloc` -> `sqlite3_initialize` -> `sqlite3MutexInit` and calls `sqlite3GlobalConfig.mutex.xMutexInit`, which is NULL. The other thread is already in `openDatabase`, so it went through `sqlite3_initialize` just before.

This is `sqlite3MutexInit` ([source](https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite/blob/21bdb75ac804bf693227f3bbb44941ece550a10e/src/mutex.c#L228-L268), same code in the SQLite 3.50.2 bundled by libsqlite3-sys 0.35.0):

```c
int sqlite3MutexInit(void){
  int rc = SQLITE_OK;
  if( !sqlite3GlobalConfig.mutex.xMutexAlloc ){
    /* ... */
    pTo->xMutexInit = pFrom->xMutexInit;
    /* ... other methods ... */
    sqlite3MemoryBarrier();
    pTo->xMutexAlloc = pFrom->xMutexAlloc;
  }
  assert( sqlite3GlobalConfig.mutex.xMutexInit );
  rc = sqlite3GlobalConfig.mutex.xMutexInit();
  /* ... */
}
```

The thread that does the copy writes `xMutexInit`, then a barrier, then `xMutexAlloc`. The thread that finds `xMutexAlloc` already set skips the block and loads `xMutexInit` with no barrier in between. On arm64 these two loads can be reordered, so it can see `xMutexAlloc` set and still read the old NULL `xMutexInit`. On x86_64 loads are not reordered this way, which would explain why we only see it on Apple Silicon.

The disassembly of the 2.7.14 release binary (`deno-aarch64-apple-darwin.zip`, Mach-O UUID `4c4c4435-5555-3144-a10b-c1c14dc2d9bc`, same as in the crash reports) matches this:

```
0x1c80ef0: stp   x29, x30, [sp, #-0x10]!
0x1c80ef4: mov   x29, sp
0x1c80ef8: adrp  x8, #0x5df5000
0x1c80efc: ldr   x8, [x8, #0x608]     ; xMutexAlloc
0x1c80f00: cbnz  x8, #0x1c80fc8       ; already set: skip the copy
           ...                         ; copy block: stores, dmb ish, store xMutexAlloc
0x1c80fc8: adrp  x8, #0x5df5000
0x1c80fcc: ldr   x8, [x8, #0x5f8]     ; xMutexInit, no barrier since the load above
0x1c80fd0: blr   x8                   ; x8 == 0 -> pc 0
0x1c80fd4: dmb   ish                  ; return address in the crash report (imageOffset 29888468)
```

<summary>Crash report excerpt (deno-2026-10-12-053833.ips)</summary>

```

procLaunch: 2026-10-12 05:38:23.8794   captureTime: 2026-10-12 05:38:23.9047
exception: EXC_BAD_ACCESS SIGSEGV KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0000000000000000
faultingThread: 6 (tokio-runtime-worker)
  ?    +0
  deno +29888468
  deno +29886848
  deno +29888192

```

The second report (2026-10-13) has the exact same faulting frames.

</details>

I could not reproduce it on demand: it needs arm64 and it is about one crash per tens of thousands of launches, so this is based on the crash reports and reading the code. The eager init threads are still there in v2.9.7 and SQLite master has the same `sqlite3MutexInit`, so I think current versions are affected too, but I have not tested.

If this is right, one way to avoid it on the Deno side (entirely your call) could be to call `sqlite3_initialize()` once on the main thread before the eager init threads are spawned. `sqlite3_initialize()` is [documented as threadsafe](https://www.sqlite.org/c3ref/initialize.html), so the missing barrier on the reader path is maybe also worth reporting to SQLite.

Does that match your understanding ?

### Description

The Deno Node.js API reference documents `Module.enableCompileCache`, but the API is `undefined` at runtime.

This also prevents Changesets CLI 3.0.3 from starting under Deno. Its CLI checks whether `process.getBuiltinModule` exists, then calls `enableCompileCache()` from the returned `node:module` object. In Deno, that property is undefined, so the CLI exits with `TypeError: enableCompileCache is not a function`.

### Reproduction

Run:

```sh
deno eval 'import { Module } from "node:module"; console.log(typeof Module.enableCompileCache); console.log(typeof process.getBuiltinModule("node:module").enableCompileCache);'
```

### Expected behavior

Both values should be `"function"`, consistent with the documented `Module.enableCompileCache` API:

https://docs.deno.com/api/node/module/

### Actual behavior

Both values are `"undefined"`.

Changesets 3.0.3 consequently fails at startup with:

```text
TypeError: enableCompileCache is not a function
```

Changesets CLI entry point:

https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/packages/cli/bin.js

### Environment

- Deno 2.9.0 (stable, aarch64-apple-darwin)
- Deno 2.9.7 (stable, aarch64-apple-darwin)

The behavior reproduces in both versions.

Version: Deno 2.9.8

After updating vite to 8.3.5 I've noticed the following error:

```
$ deno run --allow-env --allow-read --allow-write --allow-sys --allow-ffi vite build

error: Uncaught (in promise) NotCapable: Requires all access to "/proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/WSLInterop", run again with the --allow-all flag
        if (fs.existsSync("/proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/WSLInterop") || fs.existsSync("/run/WSL")) return !isInsideContainer();
               ^
    at Object.existsSync (ext:deno_node/_fs/_fs_exists.ts:1:1053)
    at isWsl (file:///workspace/node_modules/.deno/vite@8.3.5/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:14848:9)
    at file:///workspace/node_modules/.deno/vite@8.3.5/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:14851:62
```

#### Reproduction

`repro.mjs`:

```js
import fs from "node:fs";
for (const p of ["/proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/WSLInterop", "/run/WSL", "/proc/self/cgroup", "/does/not/exist"]) {
  try { console.log(p, "->", fs.existsSync(p)); }
  catch (e) { console.log(p, "-> THREW", e.name + ":", e.message); }
}
```

```sh
deno run --allow-read repro.mjs
```

**Actual (Deno 2.9.8, `--allow-read`):**

```
/proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/WSLInterop -> THREW NotCapable: Requires all access to "/proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/WSLInterop", run again with the --allow-all flag
/run/WSL -> false
/proc/self/cgroup -> THREW NotCapable: Requires all access to "/proc/self/cgroup", run again with the --allow-all flag
/does/not/exist -> false
```

**Expected (matches `node repro.mjs`, and `deno run -A repro.mjs`):**

```
/proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/WSLInterop -> false
/run/WSL -> false
/proc/self/cgroup -> true
/does/not/exist -> false
```

Returning `false` for a special path the program isn't allowed to touch would be enough. It matches Node's contract and leaks nothing, since the program can't access the path either way.

body_text: **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** Yes. k9s keeps a single navigation stack and a single active namespace. When I'm working through a problem in one namespace, filtered down to a few rows and drilled a couple of levels deep, and I need to check something in another namespace, I have to leave that view and rebuild all of it when I come back. Over a debugging session where I'm going back and forth between two or three namespaces or resource types, that turns into a lot of re-navigating. **Describe the solution you'd like** Browser-style tabs. `Ctrl-t` opens a new tab, `Ctrl-n` / `Ctrl-o` cycle through them, and `Alt-1` through `Alt-9` jump straight to one. Each tab has its own navigation stack, filter, namespace, selection and scroll position, so moving between them is instant and nothing is lost. Only one view is on screen at a time. These are tabs, not split panes, so shell, logs and everything else work exactly as they do now. The tab strip only appears once a second tab exists with one tab the UI is unchanged. **Describe alternatives you've considered** - [ / ] history keys. Good for retracing steps, but they re-run the command and rebuild the view, so the filter and scroll position I had are gone. - Running several k9s instances side by side in tmux. **Additional context** I've already built this and have been running it. Short demo: It's fairly self-contained: the core (model.Stack, command.go, watch.Factory) is untouched, roughly 140 lines added plus new files with tests. Would you take a PR for this?

body_text:
## What happens

Installing one of these `plugins/*.yaml` files shows `Plugins load failed!` in the status bar on every refresh, and the offending binding is silently missing:

```
WRN Plugins load failed error="duplicate plugin key found for \"Shift-J\" in \"argocd-disable-auto-sync\""
```

`pluginActions` refuses a plugin whose `shortCut` is already bound unless it sets `override`, and the refusal is effectively per-file — one bad shortcut and every plugin in that file reports failure.

## Affected files on master

`Table.bindKeys` binds `Shift-N/A/S/O` (`internal/view/table.go`) and the owner extender binds `Shift-J` (`internal/view/owner_extender.go`) on every resource view:

| plugin | key | already bound to |
|---|---|---|
| `argocd.yaml` → `argocd-disable-auto-sync` | `Shift-J` | Jump Owner |
| `cert-manager.yaml` → `cert-status` | `Shift-S` | Sort Status |
| `cloudnative-pg.yaml` → `cnpg-status-verbose` | `Shift-S` | Sort Status |
| `flux.yaml` → `get-suspended-helmreleases` | `Shift-S` | Sort Status |
| `flux.yaml` → `get-suspended-kustomizations` | `Shift-S` | Sort Status |
| `k3d-root-shell.yaml` → `k3d-root-shell` | `Shift-S` | Sort Status |
| `karpenter.yaml` → `karpenter-nodepool-nodes` | `Shift-N` | Sort Name |
| `openssl.yaml` → `secret-openssl-tls` | `Shift-O` | Sort Selected Column |

7 files. `argocd.yaml` is fixed in #4233; the rest are untouched.

## Why nothing catches it

The YAML is valid and the JSON schema accepts it, so the file looks fine everywhere except a running k9s. I confirmed the `argocd.yaml` case by driving the TUI: 7 of 8 descriptions offered, warning on every refresh; after the fix, 8 of 8 and a clean log.

body_text:
**Describe the bug**

In the CronJob view I can mark several rows with `Space`. `Trigger` (`t`) and delete act on all marked rows, but `Suspend/Resume` (`s`) only acts on the row under the cursor and silently ignores the marks.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create a few CronJobs: `kubectl create cronjob cj-a --image=busybox --schedule="*/5 * * * *" -- date`, and the same for `cj-b`.
2. In k9s, go to `:cronjobs`.
3. Mark `cj-a` and `cj-b` with `Space`.
4. Press `t`. The dialog says "Trigger 2 CronJobs?".
5. Cancel, then press `s`. The dialog only lists the cursor row (`default/cj-b`).
6. Confirm. Only `cj-b` is suspended (`kubectl get cronjob` shows `cj-a` still `False`).

**Expected behavior**

`s` acts on all marked rows, like `t`. It would show "Suspend 2 CronJobs" or "Resume 2 CronJobs".

**Additional context**

The code path is `toggleSuspendCmd` in `internal/view/cronjob.go`. It uses `GetSelectedItem()` while `triggerCmd` uses `GetSelectedItems()`, even though both are registered in the same `aa.Bulk(...)` block.

I have a working fix. For a mixed selection (some suspended, some not) I chose "resume only if all are suspended, otherwise suspend all". Happy to change that if you'd prefer different semantics, and I can open a PR if you're fine with the direction.

**Versions**

- OS: Ubuntu 26.04 (WSL2)
- K9s: built from master (9ef1901)
- K8s: v1.36.4+k3s1 (k3s)

**Describe the bug**
With `TERM=tmux-256color` (the `default-terminal` tmux itself recommends) and `COLORTERM=truecolor`, K9s renders every skin hex color through the xterm-256 palette, e.g. `bgColor: '#1e1e2e'` is emitted as `ESC[48;5;234m` instead of `ESC[48;2;30;30;46m`. In the same terminal, `TERM=xterm-256color` or `TERM=xterm-ghostty` gives true color. Same symptom as #3722, which was auto-closed as stale without triage.

**To Reproduce**
1. tmux 3.6b with `set -g default-terminal "tmux-256color"`; `COLORTERM=truecolor` in the pane environment (tmux sets it).
2. Any skin with hex colors, e.g. `k9s.body.bgColor: '#1e1e2e'`.
3. Run `k9s` in that pane, then from another pane: `tmux capture-pane -e -p -t <pane> | grep -oE '48;[25];[0-9;]+' | sort | uniq -c | head`
4. Output shows `48;5;234`. Restart with `TERM=xterm-256color k9s` → `48;2;30;30;46`.

**Expected behavior**
24-bit colors, as with `xterm-256color`/`xterm-ghostty`, and as current upstream tcell does for `tmux-256color`.

**Versions (please complete the following information):**
- OS: macOS, terminal Ghostty 1.3.1, tmux 3.6b
- K9s: v0.51.0 (Homebrew); `master` @ 7e97f9a pins the same tcell/tview
- K8s: n/a (rendering issue)

**Additional context**
Root cause: K9s pins `github.com/derailed/tcell/v2 v2.3.1-rc.4`, a fork of gdamore/tcell v2.2.1 (Apr 2021).

1. The fork has no builtin `tmux-256color` entry ([models.txt](https://github.com/derailed/tcell/blob/v2.3.1-rc.4/terminfo/models.txt#L19)); its `-256color` fallback only tries `tmux-88color`/`tmux-color` ([terminfo.go#L779-L794](https://github.com/derailed/tcell/blob/v2.3.1-rc.4/terminfo/terminfo.go#L779-L794)).
2. `NewTerminfoScreenFromTty` therefore falls back to `loadDynamicTerminfo` ([tscreen.go#L54-L61](https://github.com/derailed/tcell/blob/v2.3.1-rc.4/tscreen.go#L54-L61)), which runs `infocmp -1` without `-x` ([dynamic.go#L120](https://github.com/derailed/tcell/blob/v2.3.1-rc.4/terminfo/dynamic/dynamic.go#L120)), so `Tc`/`RGB`/`setrgbf` are never seen.
3. The `COLORTERM`/`TCELL_TRUECOLOR` handling that creates the `38;2`/`48;2` sequences only exists in `terminfo.LookupTerminfo` ([L748-L751, L808-L818](https://github.com/derailed/tcell/blob/v2.3.1-rc.4/terminfo/terminfo.go#L808-L818)) and is never applied to dynamically loaded entries, while `tscreen` only enables truecolor when those sequences exist ([tscreen.go#L164-L166](https://github.com/derailed/tcell/blob/v2.3.1-rc.4/tscreen.go#L164-L166)). Result: `truecolor=false`, everything is fitted to 256 colors. A custom `~/.terminfo/tmux-256color` with `Tc`/`RGB` does not help, and neither does `TCELL_TRUECOLOR`.

Upstream already fixed this: gdamore/tcell has a builtin `tmux-256color` since v2.5.0 (gdamore/tcell#521, d699c7e; refreshed in v2.8.0, fc16bf7), and tcell v3 dropped terminfo and decides truecolor from `COLORTERM` regardless of `TERM` ([v3.5.0 tscreen.go#L409-L417](https://github.com/gdamore/tcell/blob/v3.5.0/tscreen.go#L409-L417)).

Suggested fix (either):
- Preferred: land #4272 (tcell v3.5.0) together with derailed/tview#12. That fixes the whole class (tmux-256color and any other `TERM` the 2021 fork has no builtin for; cf. #3049, #3052, #3133, #3773).
- Minimal: add the upstream `tmux-256color` builtin to derailed/tcell (cherry-pick d699c7e + fc16bf7; derailed/tcell#2 tried and was withdrawn) and bump it here.

(Filing here because derailed/tcell has issues disabled.)

Workaround: run k9s with `TERM=xterm-256color` (or `screen-256color`). The README preflight suggests `TERM=xterm-256color`, but inside tmux `TERM` should be a tmux/screen variant (see `man tmux`, `default-terminal`), and k9s is the only tcell app in this setup that needs the override.

body_text:
**Describe the bug**
`Forwarders.IsContainerForwarded` can report a container as forwarded when only another container whose name starts with the same string has a forwarding entry.

Keys are stored as `pod_fqn|container|local_port:container_port`, but the lookup prefix currently ends immediately after the container name. For example, `ns1/p1|app-sidecar|8080:80` matches a lookup for `ns1/p1`, `app`.

**To Reproduce**
This is reproducible with an in-memory unit test; no Kubernetes cluster or actual port-forward connection is needed:

```go
ff := watch.Forwarders{
    "ns1/p1|app-sidecar|8080:80": nil,
}
// Returns true; expected false.
ff.IsContainerForwarded("ns1/p1", "app")
```

The values are not accessed by this method. A regression test using the existing `newNoOpForwarder` helper fails on the current master with `expected: false`, `actual: true`.

**Expected behavior**
Only the exact container name within the specified pod should match. Looking up `app-sidecar` should return true, while `app` should return false unless it has its own entry. Multiple port mappings for the same container should continue to match.

**Versions**
- K9s source: master at af23e0cc1b8f1dc59decde492cb8f85f4515c1bd
- Unit-test environment: macOS arm64, Go 1.26.10, CGO_ENABLED=0
- Kubernetes: not required for this unit-level reproduction

**Additional context**
The method is used for container forwarding status and the container port-forward view command. This report concerns incorrect status detection; it does not demonstrate traffic being forwarded to the wrong container.

Appending the existing `|` separator after the container name fixes the lookup boundary. I have a minimal fix and regression tests ready to submit.

{"key": "derailed/k9s#4314", "repository": "derailed/k9s", "issue_number": 4314, "github_issue_id": "5937223936", "url": "https://github.com/derailed/k9s/issues/4314", "title": "Container forwarding status matches containers with the same name prefix", "source_files": ["D:\OSS-Mentor\data\teacher_clickhouse\inventory_20261022T172108Z\issues_discovered.json"], "historical_labels": [], "beginner_difficulty_confirmed": false, "frozen": false, "decision": "availability_passed", "reason": "current_unassigned_no_observed_claim_or_open_pr", "open_pr_references": [], "claim_signals": [], "current_labels": [], "current_signal_group": "historical_signal_only", "body": "**Describe the bug**
`Forwarders.IsContainerForwarded` can report a container as forwarded when only another container whose name starts with the same string has a forwarding entry.

Keys are stored as `pod_fqn|container|local_port:container_port`, but the lookup prefix currently ends immediately after the container name. For example, `ns1/p1|app-sidecar|8080:80` matches a lookup for `ns1/p1`, `app`.

**To Reproduce**
This is reproducible with an in-memory unit test; no Kubernetes cluster or actual port-forward connection is needed:

```go
ff := watch.Forwarders{
    "ns1/p1|app-sidecar|8080:80": nil,
}
// Returns true; expected false.
ff.IsContainerForwarded("ns1/p1", "app")
```

The values are not accessed by this method. A regression test using the existing `newNoOpForwarder` helper fails on the current master with `expected: false`, `actual: true`.

**Expected behavior**
Only the exact container name within the specified pod should match. Looking up `app-sidecar` should return true, while `app` should return false unless it has its own entry. Multiple port mappings for the same container should continue to match.

**Versions**
- K9s source: master at af23e0cc1b8f1dc59decde492cb8f85f4515c1bd
- Unit-test environment: macOS arm64, Go 1.26.10, CGO_ENABLED=0
- Kubernetes: not required for this unit-level reproduction

**Additional context**
The method is used for container forwarding status and the container port-forward view command. This report concerns incorrect status detection; it does not demonstrate traffic being forwarded to the wrong container.

Appending the existing `|` separator after the container name fixes the lookup boundary. I have a minimal fix and regression tests ready to submit.

**Describe the bug**
An entry with no value, such as `pe:` or `pe: # po`, parses to a nil `*GVR`, and `Aliases.LoadFile` calls `String()` on it ([L163-L169](https://github.com/derailed/k9s/blob/e51ac53cb4c3a9a96666297581d309792f8faf8c/internal/config/alias.go#L163-L169)). The schema check above it only logs ([L157-L159](https://github.com/derailed/k9s/blob/e51ac53cb4c3a9a96666297581d309792f8faf8c/internal/config/alias.go#L157-L159)).

If every entry under `aliases:` is commented out, the map becomes nil: the loaded aliases are gone and the next `Define` panics with `assignment to entry in nil map`.

**To Reproduce**
1. Put `pe:` under `aliases:` in `aliases.yaml`.
2. Start k9s. A test that loads it panics:
   ```
   panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
   github.com/derailed/k9s/internal/client.(*GVR).String(...)
   ```

**Expected behavior**
k9s skips the entry and keeps its aliases.

**Versions**
- K9s: v0.51.0 and master at e51ac53

**Additional context**
Startup, context switches and the 15-second reload all run this load. I did not run k9s in a terminal session; tests confirm the nil dereference, the nil map and the `Define` panic.

body_text:
**Describe the bug**
A key under `thresholds:` with no value, such as `cpu:` or `cpu: # off`, parses to a nil `*Severity`. `Threshold.Validate` dereferences it ([L64-L72](https://github.com/derailed/k9s/blob/e51ac53cb4c3a9a96666297581d309792f8faf8c/internal/config/threshold.go#L64-L72)), and so does `LevelFor` ([L78-L83](https://github.com/derailed/k9s/blob/e51ac53cb4c3a9a96666297581d309792f8faf8c/internal/config/threshold.go#L78-L83)). The schema check reports `Invalid type. Expected: object, given: null`, but `Config.Load` still merges the entry ([L282-L292](https://github.com/derailed/k9s/blob/e51ac53cb4c3a9a96666297581d309792f8faf8c/internal/config/config.go#L282-L292)).

**To Reproduce**
1. Put this in `config.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   k9s:
     thresholds:
       cpu:
   ```
2. Start k9s with a context selected. It prints:
   ```
   Boom!! runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference.
   ```

**Expected behavior**
k9s treats the entry like a missing one and starts.

**Versions**
- K9s: v0.51.0 and master at e51ac53

**Additional context**
The startup line is from running the built binary without a terminal. A reload on a file change merges the entry without `Validate`, and with a metrics server the next cluster info update calls `LevelFor`; I read that in the code and did not run it. Tests confirm the `Validate` and `LevelFor` panics.

stable

main

sqlite

Not relevant

### Operating System Version

Linux

### What happened?

Our CI setup already runs all test with the [address sanitizer](https://doc.rust-lang.org/beta/unstable-book/compiler-flags/sanitizer.html#addresssanitizer) enabled. We use this to detect potential issues in our FFI layer.



### What did you expect to happen?

We would like to also enable the [memory sanitizer](https://doc.rust-lang.org/beta/unstable-book/compiler-flags/sanitizer.html#memorysanitizer) (and potentially other useful sanitizers as well) for the same test runs. This should be done as part of the `sqlite_bundled`, `postgres_bundled` and `mysql_bundled` CI test jobs. 

https://github.com/diesel-rs/diesel/blob/bcf28baa8a2be82aa46b79aa111062363e23e6d5/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L460-L602

This might uncover additional issues in our FFI layer, that need to be triaged and fixed in a separate step.

We also might need to perform changes to the upstream `*-sys` bindings crates to allow linking additional sanitizers.

### Rust Version

1.90.0

### Diesel Version

Current `main` (`85c79215`, version `2.3.13`)

### Diesel Features

Not feature-specific. Additional affected types exist behind features such as `r2d2`.

### Database Version

Not database-specific

### Operating System Version

Not OS-specific

### What happened?

Several error types across the Diesel workspace wrap underlying errors but do not represent those errors consistently through `std::error::Error::source()`.

There are two related patterns:

1. Some wrappers render the underlying error through `Display`, but expose it only through the deprecated `Error::cause()` or do not expose it at all. Modern chain-aware reporters therefore cannot traverse the complete error chain.

2. Some wrappers render the underlying error through `Display` and also return it from `source()`. Chain-aware reporters can then print the same underlying message twice.

A preliminary audit found the following affected types:

- `diesel::result::Error`
  - `InvalidCString`
  - `QueryBuilderError`
  - `DeserializationError`
  - `SerializationError`
  - `IntegerConversion`
- `diesel::result::ConnectionError`
  - `InvalidCString`
  - `CouldntSetupConfiguration`
- `diesel::result::DeserializeFieldError`
- `diesel::r2d2::Error`
  - `ConnectionError`
  - `QueryError`
- `diesel_migrations::MigrationError::IoError`
- `diesel_migrations::RunMigrationsError`
  - `MigrationError`
  - `QueryError`
- `diesel_infer_query::Error`
  - `ParserError` exposes and renders its source
  - `ResolverFailure` renders but does not expose its inner error
- The internal `diesel_cli::errors::Error` enum has several variants with the same inconsistency. Variants using `#[from]` or `#[source]` render and expose their source, while other wrapper variants render an inner error without exposing it.

`diesel::result::Error` and `ConnectionError` currently implement the deprecated `cause()` method rather than `source()`. Because the default `source()` implementation returns `None`, modern error reporters do not see those causes. The default impl for `cause()` uses `source()` though.

The deserialization path demonstrates both sides of the problem. `Error::DeserializationError` delegates its display output to the wrapped error but returns `None` from `source()`. The wrapped `DeserializeFieldError`, however, includes its decoding error in `Display` and also returns that error from `source()`.



### What did you expect to happen?

Diesel error wrappers should follow the conventions from the std lib docs:

- `Display` describes the context added by the current error layer.
- `source()` returns the underlying error, where one exists.
- A chain-aware reporter renders each message exactly once.

For example, a deserialization report could produce:

```text
Failed to deserialize query result
caused by: Error deserializing field 'name'
caused by: invalid value
```

### Additional details

The standard library documentation recommends that an error wrapper either include the underlying error in its `Display` output or expose it through `source()`, but not both:

https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/error/trait.Error.html#error-source

Would you be open to making error-source handling consistent across the workspace? I would be happy to prepare the changes with a bit of guidance.


### Steps to reproduce


The deserialization path provides a small example:

```rust
use std::error::Error as _;
use std::io;

use diesel::result::Error;

fn main() {
    let error =
        Error::DeserializationError(Box::new(io::Error::other("invalid value")));

    println!("{error}");
    println!("{:?}", error.source().map(ToString::to_string));
}
```

This prints:

```text
invalid value
None
```

The wrapped error supplies the outer error’s entire display text, but modern source-chain traversal cannot reach it.

`DeserializeFieldError` demonstrates the inverse behavior: its display output includes the underlying decoding error even though its `source()` method returns that same error.

### What happened?

The following query does not compile:
```rs
let entity_ids = vec![1, 2, 3, 4];

incidents::table.select(incidents::id).filter(not(exists(
    entities::table
        .select(entities::id)
        .filter(entities::id.eq_any(entity_ids))
        .except_all(
            alerts::table
                .inner_join(alerts_entities::table)
                .filter(alerts::incident_id.eq(incidents::id)) // compiles if I remove this line
                .select(alerts_entities::entity_id),
        ),
)));
```
It is a conversion attempt from the following query in PostgreSQL:
```sql
WITH incoming(entity_id) AS (
    VALUES (1), (2), (3), (4)
)
SELECT i.id
FROM incidents i
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    (
        SELECT entity_id
        FROM incoming

        EXCEPT

        SELECT ae.entity_id
        FROM alerts a
        JOIN alerts_entities ae ON ae.alert_id = a.id
        WHERE a.incident_id = i.id
    )

    -- The remaining of the query is not necessary to reproduce the error

    -- UNION ALL

    -- (
    --     SELECT ae.entity_id
    --     FROM alerts a
    --     JOIN alerts_entities ae ON ae.alert_id = a.id
    --     WHERE a.incident_id = i.id

    --     EXCEPT

    --     SELECT entity_id
    --     FROM incoming
    -- )
)
```

### What did you expect to happen?

The query should compile.

### Additional details

_No response_

)

body_text: Following https://github.com/diesel-rs/diesel/pull/5266#issuecomment-5977676991, I collected a year of workflow history to distinguish runner waiting time, execution cost and workload growth, and this is a brief visualization of it so we may best understand how to proceed from here. The sharp increase in CI completion times and summed runner usage aligns with the [MariaDB integration](https://github.com/diesel-rs/diesel/pull/5139) on August 14, 2026. That integration adds seven checks, including two macOS lanes, taking the usual active-job count from 31 to 38. Of 44 matrix-matched high-delay flags, 42 finish on macOS, and final-job queueing accounts for a median 71.2% of elapsed time across all flags. My suggestions would be to: - [ ] Keep only macOS Arm, but it has nevertheless substantial queues. Potentially consider running only for the approved merge queue itself instead of per-PR, and even consider setting up a local server if you have anything like a mac mini around. - [ ] Keep only macOS runs on things where macOS can be reasonably expected to behave differently from other systems. I am not sure yet which ones these may be. - [x] Use PostgreSQL 17 on Windows instead of 14 as it comes pre-installed. Same considerations as mac above: maybe run only on approved merge queues, consider local hosted server to avoid entirely the queue issue. - [ ] Drop PostgreSQL 14, as it's EOL is November 12, 2026 - [ ] Cache CI Black magic. I have seen a few tutorials, understand nearly nothing about it, honestly last time I tried it was a month ago with Fable and the damn thing did a x10 speedup in a CI of a project with caches. I propose we try this with any tool available in a fork, and if it indeed manages to speedup things drastically we then proceed to dissect it and understand what it is doing exactly. It cannot be done in a simple PR because it will need to store caches on main, like CusterFuzzLite does. - [ ] Measure whether reduced debug symbols shorten diesel_tests compilation and linking, and verify coverage and diagnostic quality before adopting the setting. For instance macOS ARM MySQL job spends 41m24s building tests and about 154s executing 924 tests. Maybe a stripped version would be much faster. - [ ] Run lint and tests to run concurrently *Figure 1.* Successful completion times by event, with preceding-window mean and median baselines and high-delay flags. ## Outcome

Running `diesel print-schema --schema diesel_name_probe` for the PostgreSQL table `diesel_name_probe."work items"` produces a schema that compiles, but its native Diesel query targets `"diesel_name_probe"."diesel_name_probe.work items"`. PostgreSQL rejects that relation. Generated queries should target `"diesel_name_probe"."work items"`.

## Versions

- Rust stable: `rustc 1.98.1 (48a229cea 2026-09-01)`.
- Diesel and installed Diesel CLI: 2.3.13; diesel_derives 2.3.10.
- Diesel features: default features plus `postgres`.
- PostgreSQL: 17.11.
- OS: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, x86_64 Linux.

## Steps to reproduce

Create this ordinary fixture in a disposable PostgreSQL database:

```sql
CREATE SCHEMA diesel_name_probe;
CREATE TABLE diesel_name_probe."work items" (
    id bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    label text NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO diesel_name_probe."work items" VALUES (1, 'native fixture');
```

With an otherwise empty `[print_schema]` configuration, run:

```sh
diesel print-schema --schema diesel_name_probe
```

The installed CLI actually emits:

```rust
pub mod diesel_name_probe {
    diesel::table! {
        #[sql_name = "diesel_name_probe.work items"]
        diesel_name_probe.work_items (id) {
            id -> Int8,
            label -> Text,
        }
    }
}
```

Use that exact generated file as `src/schema.rs`, with `diesel = { version = "=2.3.13", features = ["postgres"] }` and this executable:

```rust
use diesel::{Connection, QueryDsl, RunQueryDsl};
mod schema { include!("schema.rs"); }
fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let query = schema::diesel_name_probe::work_items::table
        .select(schema::diesel_name_probe::work_items::label);
    println!("{}", diesel::debug_query::<diesel::pg::Pg, _>(&query));
    let mut connection = diesel::PgConnection::establish(&std::env::var("DATABASE_URL")?)?;
    println!("{:?}", query.load::<String>(&mut connection));
    Ok(())
}
```

## Observed result

`cargo +stable run --locked` successfully compiled and actually printed:

```text
SELECT "diesel_name_probe"."diesel_name_probe.work items"."label" FROM "diesel_name_probe"."diesel_name_probe.work items" -- binds: []
Err(DatabaseError(Unknown, "relation \"diesel_name_probe.diesel_name_probe.work items\" does not exist"))
```

Expected: a successful query returning `native fixture` from the existing table. There was no Rust compiler error in this corrected reproduction.

## Cause and required change

`TableName::full_sql_name` joins the physical schema and table. `TableDefinitions` emits that joined name as the table's `sql_name` when its Rust name differs from its physical name, while also emitting the explicit schema separately. The native table macro treats `sql_name` as one quoted identifier. The table attribute should retain only the physical table identifier when the explicit schema is already present.

Pinned source: [CLI emission](https://github.com/diesel-rs/diesel/blob/9628f5ca470dea2adaa8194365541e304e3d56dc/diesel_cli/src/print_schema.rs#L806), [physical-name construction](https://github.com/diesel-rs/diesel/blob/9628f5ca470dea2adaa8194365541e304e3d56dc/diesel_cli/src/infer_schema_internals/table_data.rs#L52), [native rendering](https://github.com/diesel-rs/diesel/blob/3eb6cf4217d0db90fcab7b6929f37599c44aad42/diesel_derives/src/table.rs#L105). The same full-name emission was also present in current main when inspected on 2026-10-07 UTC; the executed reproduction is specifically the pinned versions above.

## Done when

- A real nonpublic-schema renamed-table CLI fixture generates the physical table name without duplicating its schema.
- The unmodified generated schema compiles and selects the fixture row on PostgreSQL.
- Existing public-schema renamed-table and ordinary explicit-schema cases remain valid.

## Evidence limits and disclosure

This report and reproduction were prepared by a Codex agent on behalf of the account owner. Only the listed ordinary fixture, CLI generation, stable compilation and real query were executed. Issue tracker and discussions searches found no matching report; related closed issues 2168 and 3692 concern different failures. No upstream fix is proposed as already tested, and no third-party crate beyond Diesel is needed by the Rust reproduction.

I have released the version `0.6` of dejadoc, and it now comes with more reductions to canonical form and execution graph isomorphisms, plus scoping which can now include workspaces, organizations, and dependencies to an arbitrary degree. For instance, now it can find code duplication between diesel and diesel-async.

[As is tradition](https://youtu.be/2POYSKiVwM4?si=bTNW-EUSdK7AI9u3&t=95), this is the run on diesel. It did not find anything in the immediate dependencies, but found several other interesting things in the workspace and organization. I have only opened a few at random for now because they are a lot, but the ones I have read look good indeed.

I set the minimum filter at 30 syn tokens, we can change it as needed.

| Check | Diesel workspace | Organization, partial |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contextual duplicate groups | 53 | 72 |
| Whole-function duplicate groups | 0 | 17 |
| Doctest duplicate groups | 0 | 0 |

I hope it is an interesting exploration.
Once we determine which configuration is reasonable and looks good, I can bump the CI.

Ciao,
Luca

Dioxus: 0.8.0-alpha.1
Wry: 0.55.1
Platform: Android API 37
Device: Pixel 10 Pro XL emulator

**Command:**
dx serve --package mobile --android --device emulator-5554

**Observed behavior:**
The application starts with a white screen.

**Logcat:**
panicked at wry-0.55.1/src/android/mod.rs:189:54:
no available activity

**Cause:**
WryActivity registers ProcessLifecycleOwner observer before the Android
Activity is registered in Rust. The observer may synchronously initialize
Wry, causing Tao to fail with NoAvailableActivity.

**Upstream fix:**
https://github.com/tauri-apps/wry/pull/1720

The CI currently lacks a [`cargo-llvm-cov`](https://github.com/taiki-e/cargo-llvm-cov#github-actions-and-codecov) task. A coverage report would help contributors identify untested paths and assess whether regression tests exercise the code changed by a pull request.

In [sqlparser](https://github.com/apache/datafusion-sqlparser-rs/pull/2565) and [diesel](https://github.com/diesel-rs/diesel/pull/5244) and most other projects I went for the `cargo-llvm-cov` + [codecov](https://about.codecov.io/) combo. Of course, each project has its own tweaks needed to combine the different coverage reports for the various backends, and most likely nightly is needed to really get the highest coverage percentage possible (including wasm tests and doctests).

If a PR adding this is appreciated, lmk and I will add it.

body_text:
## Feature Request

Allow to exclude non rust files or specific glob patterns from triggering dx hot patching.

Use case:
In bevy and other tools assets can be often embedded into an executable and the corresponding tool already provides inbuilt logic for asset hotpatching. In these kinds of tools dx hotpatching does hotpaching when it is not needed, doesn't really do anything.

So it would be useful to be able to exclude files from triggering unnecessary hotpatch. 

## Implement Suggestion

Support `--hot-patch-skip-assets` or similar flag or add support to define glob patterns in Dioxus.toml configuration file, which should be read by dx serve --hot-patch.

body_text:
**Problem**

Android apps produced by `dx` are not 16 KB page-aligned. On Android 15+ devices and 16 KB page-size emulators, launching the app shows a system warning that the native libraries are not 16 KB aligned.

`dx` 0.7.10 links the app `cdylib` with the NDK selected by `NDK_HOME` / `ANDROID_NDK_HOME`. NDK r27 and older default to 4 KB ELF `LOAD` alignment. `packages/cli/src/build/android.rs` sets `CARGO_TARGET_<TRIPLE>_RUSTFLAGS` to only the `clang_rt.builtins` link line and never passes:

```
-Wl,-z,max-page-size=16384
-Wl,-z,common-page-size=16384
```

Because that environment variable replaces `.cargo/config.toml` `rustflags`, an app cannot reliably add the flags itself while building through `dx`. ```

NDK r28+ already does this by default, but `dx` should not depend on which NDK the environment happens to select.

body_text:
### Is your enhancement related to a problem? Please describe

Developers can run AI coding tasks in Che, but there is no single place to manage multiple agents working on related tasks. It is difficult to see what is running, return to previous tasks, and review the resulting changes.


### Describe the solution you'd like

Provide an Agentic Workspace MVP where a developer can:

- Create or select an Agentic Workspace to organize one or more agent tasks.
- Start one or more agent sessions, assign tasks, and see their status.
- Use the terminal interface provided by each agent. The Agentic Workspace should not recreate a separate chat UI for Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, or other supported agents.
- Use the **Changes** right panel to review files and diffs produced by the selected agent.
- Use the **Terminal** right panel to access the Agentic Workspace development environment, inspect files, and run commands.
- Use **Open in VS Code** to open the Agentic Workspace in the Dev Spaces development environment through VS Code.

The Agentic Workspace should build on the agent runtime support described in [Eclipse Che issue #23921](https://github.com/eclipse-che/che/issues/23921) and [che-operator PR #2184](https://github.com/eclipse-che/che-operator/pull/2184) as its backend and execution foundation.

An Agentic Workspace groups the agent sessions and development environment used for a piece of software. It uses the Dev Spaces development environment when the developer needs to inspect, test, or continue the work.

The MVP should support this flow:

1. Create or select an Agentic Workspace.
2. Start a task through the agent's (Claude/Codex/OpenCode) existing TUI.
3. Leave and return to see whether the task is running, blocked, or complete.
4. Review the changes and use the Terminal panel when needed.
5. Open the Agentic Workspace in VS Code to continue development.

This MVP does not include a new agent chat UI or replace the terminal interfaces provided by individual agents. Implementation and technology choices are intentionally open.

[View the running Agentic Workspace MVP](https://firewall.github.io/Dev-Spaces-Start-workspace/pr-preview/pr-2/#/agent-space-mvp)


### Describe alternatives you've considered

### Is your enhancement related to a problem? Please describe

The UDI ships podman but no Docker Compose provider, so `podman compose` cannot run:

```console
$ /usr/bin/podman.orig compose version --short
Error: looking up compose provider failed
7 errors occurred:
        * exec: "/home/user/.docker/cli-plugins/docker-compose": stat ...: no such file or directory
        * exec: "/usr/local/lib/docker/cli-plugins/docker-compose": stat ...: no such file or directory
        * exec: "/usr/local/libexec/docker/cli-plugins/docker-compose": stat ...: no such file or directory
        * exec: "/usr/lib/docker/cli-plugins/docker-compose": stat ...: no such file or directory
        * exec: "/usr/libexec/docker/cli-plugins/docker-compose": stat ...: no such file or directory
        * exec: "docker-compose": executable file not found in $PATH
        * exec: "podman-compose": executable file not found in $PATH
```

This blocks two things:

1. **`devcontainer.json` files that use `dockerComposeFile`.** Work on native devcontainer support
   in Che (#23458, eclipse-che/che-server#1050) drives [`@devcontainers/cli`](https://github.com/devcontainers/cli) with podman as the engine. The CLI resolves its compose provider by running `<engine> compose version`, so with no provider present every compose-based repository is unusable. 
2. **Users who simply want `podman compose up`** for a multi-service stack inside their workspace, independent of devcontainers.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Bundle a compose provider in the UDI, so that `podman compose` works out of the box.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

**Installing it per-workspace.** This works today and is what the verification below used:

```bash
python3 -m pip install --user podman-compose
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
ln -sf /usr/bin/podman.orig "$HOME/.local/bin/podman"   # ahead of the kubedock wrapper
```

It is not a solution: it costs every user a manual step, it fails in air-gapped environments where
PyPI is unreachable, and with `persistUserHome` disabled it evaporates on every workspace restart.
The same argument was made for bundling the devcontainer CLI in
devfile/developer-images#267.

**Leaving compose unsupported.** Viable, but it permanently excludes a common class of repository
from devcontainer support in Che, and users hitting it get a confusing seven-path error rather than
a statement that compose is not available.

### Describe the bug

When creating a workspace via a factory URL that includes a subpath (e.g. https://github.com/org/repo/tree/main/subdir), the project-clone init container ignores the devfile's checkoutFrom.revision and instead attempts to check out main/subdir as the revision. Since that's not a valid branch, it falls back to the default branch.

### Che version

7.122@latest

### Steps to reproduce

Reproducer repository: https://github.com/agiertli/sparse-attribute

- main branch contains PYTHON/2CPU/devfile.yaml and PYTHON/4CPU/devfile.yaml
- Each devfile specifies projects[].git.checkoutFrom.revision: cloned
- cloned branch is empty (single empty commit)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Apply the getting-started-samples ConfigMap from the repo: kubectl apply -f getting-started-samples.yaml
2. Open the Eclipse Che dashboard and click the "Python (2 CPU)" sample tile
3. Check the project-clone init container logs

Actual: project-clone logs show Could not find revision main/PYTHON/2CPU in repository, using default branch — the URL subpath is injected as the revision, overriding the devfile's checkoutFrom.revision: cloned



### Expected behavior

Expected: Workspace checks devfile's checkoutFrom.revision (i.e. 'cloned') 


### Runtime

OpenShift

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Installation method

OperatorHub

### Environment

macOS

### Eclipse Che Logs

```shell
project-clone container log:
Processing project python-2cpu
Cloning project python-2cpu to /projects/project-clone-990217814/python-2cpu
Cloned project python-2cpu to /projects/project-clone-990217814/python-2cpu
Setting up remotes for project python-2cpu
Fetched remote origin at https://github.com/agiertli/sparse-attribute.git
Could not find revision main/PYTHON/2CPU in repository, using default branch
```

### Is your enhancement related to a problem? Please describe

Since the beginning of my use Eclipse Che I've found the boot time of a workspace to be quite heavy.
The first answer was on the reconciliation not reconciling https://github.com/eclipse-che/che/issues/23067 (thanks a lot for your help back then)
The second was the image puller.
The third focus on the IDE:
- Jet brains have a heavy first boot but I don't think we can do anything about that. BUT the second start takes less than 30s. In most cases, thank's to https://github.com/che-incubator/jetbrains-ide-dev-server/blob/main/build/scripts/entrypoint-init-container.sh#L73
- VsCode copy at each boot the whole ide https://github.com/che-incubator/che-code/blob/main/build/scripts/entrypoint-init-container.sh#L15 . If the copy takes 1m30, it will ALWAYS take this time 

### Describe the solution you'd like

I would like for the init container to only copy the needed files.

### Describe the bug

`ApiUrlResolver.resolveWorkspaceName()` can resolve a missing workspace name to a different DevWorkspace whose Kubernetes resource name merely starts with the requested name plus a hyphen. The fallback accepts any nonempty alphanumeric suffix. `TestWorkspaceUtil.stopWorkspaceByName()` and `deleteWorkspaceByName()` use the resulting URL, so cleanup can stop or delete the wrong workspace.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Ensure there is no DevWorkspace with `metadata.name: workspace`.
2. Have a separate DevWorkspace with `metadata.name: workspace-2` and display-name label `kubernetes.io/metadata.name: workspace-2`.
3. Call `getWorkspaceApiUrl('workspace')` (or `stopWorkspaceByName('workspace')`).

**Actual:** the resolver returns the API URL for `workspace-2`.

**Expected:** the resolver reports that `workspace` was not found. A restored resource such as `workspace-4fnq` should remain resolvable when its display-name label is `workspace`.

### Code references

- [Prefix fallback in `ApiUrlResolver.ts`](https://github.com/eclipse-che/che/blob/main/tests/e2e/utils/workspace/ApiUrlResolver.ts#L79-L95)
- [Stop/delete callers in `TestWorkspaceUtil.ts`](https://github.com/eclipse-che/che/blob/main/tests/e2e/utils/workspace/TestWorkspaceUtil.ts)

### Why it matters

A name collision during E2E cleanup can act on a workspace other than the one the test requested. Checking the DevWorkspace display-name label before accepting a generated-name fallback would preserve backup-restore support while avoiding this case.

Related: #23911 introduced the suffix fallback for backup restore; #23965 added an exact-name check against the list.

### Is your enhancement related to a problem?

The AI provider schema supports `tags?: string[]` and the gallery forwards tags to provider cards, but the badge renderer filters to the exact string `Tech-Preview`. A community-maintained AI-tool integration cannot display a Community maintenance/support badge using valid registry metadata `tags: ["Community"]`.

The product identity/publisher must stay unchanged: the badge describes the Che integration maintenance, not a renamed product or a claim of vendor support.

### Describe the solution

Support an explicit `Community` provider badge alongside the existing `Tech-Preview` badge. Preserve existing Tech-Preview rendering, selection, versions and API-key indicators. Prefer an explicit supported-tag allowlist rather than rendering arbitrary registry tags as trusted support claims. Cover Community-only, Tech-Preview-only, both, unknown tags and absent tags in component tests.

### Evidence and affected version

- Schema: https://github.com/eclipse-che/che-dashboard/blob/a56c2745cbb9c668bdd7662511c3515198d38bfc/packages/common/src/dto/api/index.ts#L152-L162
- Renderer: https://github.com/eclipse-che/che-dashboard/blob/a56c2745cbb9c668bdd7662511c3515198d38bfc/packages/dashboard-frontend/src/components/AiSelector/Gallery/Entry/index.tsx#L173-L185
- Also observed in OpenShift Dev Spaces 3.30.2, dashboard image `registry.redhat.io/devspaces/dashboard-rhel9@sha256:e5ce2b3dbfbf9f41883fc3291f6f11f937f8238238c9aa1b20b64d5bbb000600`. Its deployed client bundle contains `.filter(e=>"Tech-Preview"===e)` in the card tag renderer. Community metadata alone therefore cannot produce a visible badge there.

Logos can be delivered independently through provider.icon; no image rebuild or provider identity change is necessary. The dashboard repository has issues disabled, so this enhancement is tracked here.

Please describe When the user clicks on the 'Agent Space' button a dedicated namespace for Agents should be provisioned on the k8s level: ### Describe the solution you'd like Currently, each user is provisioned with a dedicated namespace once they enter user dashboard e.g. `-che`. For the `Agent Space` the dedicated namespace should be provisioned once the user either enters the space or more ideally, crafts a first Agent e.g. - `-che-agents` This agent namespace will have a different RBAC in comparison to the `-che` namespace. Agents should not have the same privileges that developers have. Implementation Details: - For default dynamic provisioning, the agent namespace should be provisioned once a user either enters the Agent Space or crafts the first Agent - If automatic namespace provisioning is disabled, agent namespaces must be pre-created by an admin (technically, the admin can control which users can / can not access Agent Spaces based on namespace pre-provisioning): - if namespace is not pre-created, the error message is displayed on the UI - smth. like `You do not have access to the Agent Space - please contact admin.` - Provisioning will probably stay in **che-server**, mirroring the existing flow for -che. The operator keeps doing what it already does well: reconciling cluster-scoped RBAC and syncing content into the namespace once it exists. - Labels & annotations (must not collide with the `-che` namespace) ### Describe alternatives you've considered Create Agents in the existing -che namespace, but this approach will be much less secure and convoluted ### Additional context Once this part is implemented, we should look into exposing dedicated `Agent Preferences` for Agents on UI for Agent Spaces that would be different from "User Preferences" for CDEs:

## Description

`EclipseFileManager.list()` throws when asked to list a package that does not exist in a system module.

`JrtFileSystem.list()` initializes its intermediate `files` variable to `null`. When `Files.list(resolve)` throws `NoSuchFileException`, the default error path logs the exception and continues. The subsequent iteration over `files` then throws a secondary `NullPointerException`.

Source: https://github.com/eclipse-jdt/eclipse.jdt.core/blob/80fa9fa3e994d5f7b8d97ff1fcc88179efbe59f9/org.eclipse.jdt.core.compiler.batch/src/org/eclipse/jdt/internal/compiler/tool/JrtFileSystem.java#L73-L100

## Reproducer

```java
JavaCompiler compiler = new EclipseCompiler();

try (StandardJavaFileManager fileManager =
        compiler.getStandardFileManager(null, null, null)) {

    JavaFileManager.Location javaBase =
            fileManager.getLocationForModule(
                    StandardLocation.SYSTEM_MODULES,
                    "java.base");

    boolean found = fileManager.list(
            javaBase,
            "org.eclipse.jdt.__missing_package__",
            Set.of(JavaFileObject.Kind.CLASS),
            false)
        .iterator()
        .hasNext();

    System.out.println(found);
}
```

## Expected behavior

The lookup returns an empty iterable and prints `false`.

A nonexistent package is an ordinary negative lookup. The directory-backed implementation returns when its package directory does not exist, and the archive-backed implementation returns when the archive contains no types for the requested package.

## Actual behavior

With the default value of `org.eclipse.jdt.propagate_io_errors` (`false`), ECJ logs `NoSuchFileException` and then throws `NullPointerException` while iterating over the null `files` variable.

With `-Dorg.eclipse.jdt.propagate_io_errors=true`, the missing package instead produces `IllegalStateException`.

## Suggested fix

- Catch `NoSuchFileException` and `NotDirectoryException` before the general `IOException` handler.
- Treat those two exceptions as negative lookups and return an empty list without writing to `System.err`.
- Preserve the existing propagation policy for other checked `IOException`s.
- When propagation is disabled, return an empty list after logging the original checked I/O failure instead of producing a secondary NPE.
- Avoid a nullable intermediate list so every normal return path produces a valid result.

This intentionally changes the behavior for missing packages when `org.eclipse.jdt.propagate_io_errors=true`: these lookups would return an empty list instead of throwing `IllegalStateException`.

## Scope

Kind filtering remains in `EclipseFileManager.collectAllMatchingFiles()`. `JrtFileSystem.list()` does not currently use its `kinds` parameter, and this issue does not propose changing that behavior.

Recursive enumeration is also separate. The current implementation does not use the `recurse` parameter, but a missing package should produce an empty result for either value. Correct recursive traversal has different enumeration and performance implications and can be addressed independently.

An `UncheckedIOException` raised during lazy stream traversal currently propagates past the checked `IOException` handler and is outside the scope of this issue.

## Version

Reproduced from current master at `80fa9fa3e994d5f7b8d97ff1fcc88179efbe59f9`.

body_text:
Environment: Eclipse 2026-09 (4.41), Windows Server 2025, JDK 27, workspace
with ~20 interdependent Maven projects (dependencies resolved as workspace
SOURCE, not jars, while projects are open).

Three separate freezes within 3 days, three triggers, three internal paths —
one root cause: name resolution for symbols living in workspace projects runs
on the UI thread and requires parsing sources / building structures there.

--- Sample A (35s, 2026-09-22, Ctrl+hover) — cascading import resolution:
  JavaElementHyperlinkDetector.detectHyperlinks
   -> codeSelect -> SelectionEngine
    -> CompilationUnitScope.faultInImports -> findSingleImport -> askForType
     -> ... -> source-level type resolution (per-import cascade)

--- Sample B (46s, 2026-09-25, hovering the annotation ruler) — eager package
    cache initialization:
  AbstractAnnotationHover -> createJavadocProposal -> codeSelect
   -> new SearchableEnvironment
    -> JavaProjectElementInfo.initializePackageNames
     -> JarPackageFragmentRoot.computeChildren
      -> WindowsPath.normalize                              <- per jar entry

--- Sample C (36.9s, BLOCKED, 2026-09-25, Ctrl+hover) — structure building +
    lock contention with background indexer:
  JavaElementHyperlinkDetector.detectHyperlinks -> codeSelect -> SelectionEngine
   -> faultInImports -> askForType -> SearchableEnvironment.findType
    -> CompilationUnit.buildStructure -> SourceElementParser.parseCompilationUnit
     -> CompilationUnitStructureRequestor.createField
      -> DeduplicationUtil.toString                         <- BLOCKED on lock
        (held by a background structure-building thread)
Workaround (verified): closing dependent projects forces jar-based resolution
(freeze disappears); first-query-per-cache warmup remains expensive.

Expected:
1. Resolution of workspace sources must not block the UI thread for tens of
   seconds — move to a job with progress, or prefer binary index results
   before falling back to source parsing.
2. initializePackageNames should be lazy/incremental (see Sample B).
3. DeduplicationUtil lock scope should exclude long structure parses (Sample C).

Related: Issue 1 (jdt.ui, 142s parameter-name source parsing — same
"unbounded source work on UI thread" family).

{"repository": "eclipse-jdt/eclipse.jdt.core", "task_candidate_id": 3769, "repository_id": 73, "issue_number": 5438, "github_issue_id": 5578028171, "html_url": "https://github.com/eclipse-jdt/eclipse.jdt.core/issues/5438", "created_at": "2026-09-25T04:13:30+00:00", "author_association": "NONE", "title": "UI freezes 15-46s on hover in large workspaces: SelectionEngine resolves workspace sources on the UI thread (structure parsing + dedup lock contention)", "body_text": "

Environment: Eclipse 2026-09 (4.41), Windows Server 2025, JDK 27, workspace
with ~20 interdependent Maven projects (dependencies resolved as workspace
SOURCE, not jars, while projects are open).

Three separate freezes within 3 days, three triggers, three internal paths —
one root cause: name resolution for symbols living in workspace projects runs
on the UI thread and requires parsing sources / building structures there.

--- Sample A (35s, 2026-09-22, Ctrl+hover) — cascading import resolution:
  JavaElementHyperlinkDetector.detectHyperlinks
   -> codeSelect -> SelectionEngine
    -> CompilationUnitScope.faultInImports -> findSingleImport -> askForType
     -> ... -> source-level type resolution (per-import cascade)

--- Sample B (46s, 2026-09-25, hovering the annotation ruler) — eager package
    cache initialization:
  AbstractAnnotationHover -> createJavadocProposal -> codeSelect
   -> new SearchableEnvironment
    -> JavaProjectElementInfo.initializePackageNames
     -> JarPackageFragmentRoot.computeChildren
      -> WindowsPath.normalize                              <- per jar entry

--- Sample C (36.9s, BLOCKED, 2026-09-25, Ctrl+hover) — structure building +
    lock contention with background indexer:
  JavaElementHyperlinkDetector.detectHyperlinks -> codeSelect -> SelectionEngine
   -> faultInImports -> askForType -> SearchableEnvironment.findType
    -> CompilationUnit.buildStructure -> SourceElementParser.parseCompilationUnit
     -> CompilationUnitStructureRequestor.createField
      -> DeduplicationUtil.toString                         <- BLOCKED on lock
        (held by a background structure-building thread)
Workaround (verified): closing dependent projects forces jar-based resolution
(freeze disappears); first-query-per-cache warmup remains expensive.

Expected:
1. Resolution of workspace sources must not block the UI thread for tens of
   seconds — move to a job with progress, or prefer binary index results
   before falling back to source parsing.
2. initializePackageNames should be lazy/incremental (see Sample B).
3. DeduplicationUtil lock scope should exclude long structure parses (Sample C).

Related: Issue 1 (jdt.ui, 142s parameter-name source parsing — same
"unbounded source work on UI thread" family).

Summary
Introduce an API for lazy constants, which are objects that hold unmodifiable data. Lazy constants are treated as true constants by the JVM, enabling the same performance optimizations that are enabled by declaring a field final. Compared to final fields, however, lazy constants offer greater flexibility as to the timing of their initialization. This is a [preview API](https://openjdk.org/jeps/12).

body_text:
Found while compiling Eclipse Collections (`RichIterableTestCase`, an interface with about 450 serializable lambdas) with ECJ: javac compiles it, ECJ fails.

### Reproducer

Generate a class with N serializable lambdas:

```bash
N=430
{
echo 'import java.io.Serializable;'
echo 'public class T { interface SF extends Serializable { int f(String s); }'
for i in $(seq 1 $N); do echo " static SF m$i() { return s -> s.length() + $i; }"; done
echo ' }'
} > T.java
```

### Expected

`javac T.java` compiles (the generated `$deserializeLambda$` is smaller than 64 KB; with javac 25 the largest N that compiles is 449).

### Actual

`java -jar ecj.jar -release 21 T.java` (ECJ 3.46.100 and a current master build):

```
ERROR in T.java
	public class T { ...
The code of method $deserializeLambda$(SerializedLambda) is exceeding the 65535 bytes limit
```

The largest N that compiles with ECJ is 423, so ECJ's `$deserializeLambda$` is about 6% bigger than javac's (a similar difference on the real `RichIterableTestCase`: 448 serializable lambdas, 61,852 bytes with javac).

### Analysis

ECJ already uses the same strategy as javac (switch on the hash code of the implementation method name, then a switch on an index; `CodeStream.generateSyntheticBodyForDeserializeLambda`). The body of each case is byte-for-byte the same as javac's. The difference is in the code around the cases:

- the second switch (dense index 0..N-1) is a `lookupswitch` (8 bytes per entry), javac uses a `tableswitch` (4 bytes per entry); there is a TODO about it in `CodeStream.java` ("need to use a tableswitch"), about 1.8 KB for 448 cases;
- ECJ adds a `goto` at the end of each case of the first switch.

I did not check that these two points explain the whole difference. Using a `tableswitch` and dropping the useless jumps would give ECJ a bit more room, which is enough for projects like Eclipse Collections that are just under the limit with javac.

I could not find an existing issue (`deserializeLambda` ones: #155, #294, #295, #1031, #4055 are about other problems).

This report was prepared with the help of Claude (Anthropic); the reproducer was checked with javac and ECJ.

{"key": "eclipse-jdt/eclipse.jdt.core#5595", "repository": "eclipse-jdt/eclipse.jdt.core", "issue_number": 5595, "github_issue_id": "5975060862", "url": "https://github.com/eclipse-jdt/eclipse.jdt.core/issues/5595", "title": "$deserializeLambda$ exceeds the 64 KB limit with fewer serializable lambdas than javac (Eclipse Collections)", "source_files": ["D:\OSS-Mentor\data\teacher_clickhouse\inventory_20261022T172108Z\issues_discovered.json"], "historical_labels": [], "beginner_difficulty_confirmed": false, "frozen": false, "decision": "availability_passed", "reason": "current_unassigned_no_observed_claim_or_open_pr", "open_pr_references": [], "claim_signals": [], "current_labels": [], "current_signal_group": "historical_signal_only", "body": "Found while compiling Eclipse Collections (`RichIterableTestCase`, an interface with about 450 serializable lambdas) with ECJ: javac compiles it, ECJ fails.

### Reproducer

Generate a class with N serializable lambdas:

```bash
N=430
{
echo 'import java.io.Serializable;'
echo 'public class T { interface SF extends Serializable { int f(String s); }'
for i in $(seq 1 $N); do echo " static SF m$i() { return s -> s.length() + $i; }"; done
echo ' }'
} > T.java
```

### Expected

`javac T.java` compiles (the generated `$deserializeLambda$` is smaller than 64 KB; with javac 25 the largest N that compiles is 449).

### Actual

`java -jar ecj.jar -release 21 T.java` (ECJ 3.46.100 and a current master build):

```
ERROR in T.java
	public class T { ...
The code of method $deserializeLambda$(SerializedLambda) is exceeding the 65535 bytes limit
```

The largest N that compiles with ECJ is 423, so ECJ's `$deserializeLambda$` is about 6% bigger than javac's (a similar difference on the real `RichIterableTestCase`: 448 serializable lambdas, 61,852 bytes with javac).

### Analysis

ECJ already uses the same strategy as javac (switch on the hash code of the implementation method name, then a switch on an index; `CodeStream.generateSyntheticBodyForDeserializeLambda`). The body of each case is byte-for-byte the same as javac's. The difference is in the code around the cases:

- the second switch (dense index 0..N-1) is a `lookupswitch` (8 bytes per entry), javac uses a `tableswitch` (4 bytes per entry); there is a TODO about it in `CodeStream.java` ("need to use a tableswitch"), about 1.8 KB for 448 cases;
- ECJ adds a `goto` at the end of each case of the first switch.

I did not check that these two points explain the whole difference. Using a `tableswitch` and dropping the useless jumps would give ECJ a bit more room, which is enough for projects like Eclipse Collections that are just under the limit with javac.

I could not find an existing issue (`deserializeLambda` ones: #155, #294, #295, #1031, #4055 are about other problems).

This report was prepared with the help of Claude (Anthropic); the reproducer was checked with javac and ECJ.
