## Summary An improvement of the work that started in https://bugs.eclipse.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=366048#c21 but without the problems described in https://bugs.eclipse.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=366048#c31 / https://bugs.eclipse.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=366048#c34 **Expands on:** - https://github.com/eclipse-jdt/eclipse.jdt.ui/issues/1977 I am fairly sure that one is this exact same problem but I didn't declare it as a _duplicate_ yet since the other issue doesn't mention which other threads were involved. But by looking at the mentioned stack-trace, I see that the involved Thread has the same pattern we all know, namely: the call to the recursion X times and the call to `fWaitLock.wait(30000)` at the top. --- `CoreASTProvider.getAST(element, WAIT_YES | WAIT_ACTIVE_ONLY, monitor)` can hang indefinitely — observed in production for 76 minutes — when three unrelated call sites all request the AST of the same active editor's element while a reconcile for it is in progress, and that reconcile never completes. ## The specific scenario Three independent call sites, all targeting the **same active element**, two different wait flags: | Call site | Thread | Flag | |---|---|---| | `OrganizeImportsAction.run()` | **main UI thread** (synchronous) | `WAIT_ACTIVE_ONLY` | | `OverrideIndicatorLabelDecorator` ("Decoration Calculation" job) | background worker | `WAIT_YES` | | `SelectionListenerWithASTManager` ("Requesting Java AST from selection" job) | background worker | `WAIT_YES` | At the time all three called `getAST`, the element was marked as being reconciled (`isReconciling() == true`), but the background reconciler responsible for it had already gone idle — it was not going to call `reconciled()` for this element again. A thread dump of the incident shows all three callers still blocked in `Object.wait()` inside `CoreASTProvider.getAST`, at increasing recursion depth, while every reconciler thread in the process sits idle. The freeze was recorded as still ongoing 4,581 seconds (~76 minutes) after it started — roughly 152 stacked 30-second retries. ```mermaid gantt title CoreASTProvider deadlock — a real 76-minute UI freeze dateFormat HH:mm axisFormat %H:%M section Main UI thread (SWT event loop) OrganizeImportsAction -> getAST(WAIT_ACTIVE_ONLY), blocked :crit, main, 11:49, 76m section Worker: Decoration Calculation OverrideIndicatorLabelDecorator -> getAST(WAIT_YES), blocked :crit, dec, 11:49, 76m section Worker: Requesting Java AST from selection SelectionListenerWithASTManager -> getAST(WAIT_YES), blocked :crit, sel, 11:49, 76m section Java reconciler thread Idle in AbstractReconciler.delay() — not reconciling this element anymore :done, idle, 11:49, 76m ``` Note: `WAIT_ACTIVE_ONLY` is not the conservative "never wait" flag its name suggests — for an element that *is* the active one but has no AST cached yet, `CoreASTProvider.getAST`'s `canReturnNull` computation makes it behave identically to `WAIT_YES`. That's why `OrganizeImportsAction`, running on the main UI thread, ends up blocked too. ## Root cause `getAST(WAIT_YES)` retries by recursing when the requested (active) element is still marked as reconciling. Each retry gets a **fresh** 30-second `fWaitLock.wait(...)`, with no overall deadline across retries. body_text:
## Problem

In hierarchical package presentation, chains of Java packages can be folded into a single node. Equivalent resource-folder chains remain fully expanded.

For example:

```text
src/main/resources/
└── org/
    └── example/
        └── app/
            └── assets/
```

requires opening four separate folder nodes, even when every intermediate folder contains only the next folder.

## Proposed behavior

Add a separate **Java > Appearance** preference to fold resource-folder chains in hierarchical Package and Project Explorer layouts.

A chain should be folded while every intermediate folder has:

- exactly one visible child folder;
- no other visible children.

Active viewer filters should be respected, so filtered resources such as `.DS_Store` do not prevent folding, while visible files do.

The folded node should display the complete slash-separated path, for example:

```text
org/example/app/assets
```

Adding or removing a visible resource in an intermediate folder should immediately unfold or refold the affected chain.

Body:
Environment: Eclipse 2026-09 (4.41), Windows 11, JDK 27, workspace with
hundreds of Maven jars (m2e auto-attaches -sources.jar; dependencies compiled
without -parameters).

Repro: Invoke content assist at a method/constructor call position where
candidates come from a dependency with attached sources and no parameter debug
info.

The UI thread blocks for 142 seconds. Monitoring sample (full stack captured):

CompletionProposalPopup.computeFilteredProposals
-> AbstractJavaCompletionProposal.validate
-> isValidPrefix -> computeDisplayString
-> CompletionProposalLabelProvider.createMethodProposalLabel
-> appendUnboundedParameterList
-> InternalCompletionProposal.findParameterNames
-> findConstructorParameterNames
-> SourceMapper.mapSource
-> SourceElementParser.parseCompilationUnit        <-- full source parse

Two compounding problems:

1. Parameter names are extracted by parsing the ENTIRE attached source, with no
timeout (unlike the Javadoc-based path which has one).
2. The parse is repeated per candidate proposal, so one assist invocation can
parse the same sources many times over.

Expected: parameter-name extraction from sources should be time-boxed and/or
cached per type, and must never block the UI thread for minutes.

Also observed on the same hot path: a preference lookup per candidate
(JavaCore.getOption inside isSubwordMatching) — see second sample below —
which would be cheap to cache.

Sample 2 (6.3s, same invocation family):
CompletionProposalPopup.computeFilteredProposals
-> validate -> isPrefix
-> AbstractJavaCompletionProposal.getPatternMatchRule
-> CharOperation.subWordMatch -> SubwordMatcher (allocated per candidate)

Body:
Environment: same as above (hundreds of jars on the classpath).

Repro: With a cold per-project cache, hover the annotation ruler (error/warning
squiggle) in a Java editor — AbstractAnnotationHover builds a Javadoc proposal,
which requires codeSelect, which constructs a new SearchableEnvironment.

The first SearchableEnvironment construction eagerly initializes the full
package-name cache of the project: for EVERY jar, computeChildren() enumerates
all entries and normalizes each path individually (WindowsPath.normalize /
initOffsets). Total cost is O(total jar entries) on the UI thread.

Monitoring sample (46s):

AbstractAnnotationHover$AnnotationInformationControl.deferredCreateContent
-> createJavadocProposal -> getJavaElement -> codeSelect
-> JavaProject.newSearchableNameEnvironment
-> new SearchableEnvironment
-> JavaProjectElementInfo.getProjectCache
-> initializePackageNames
-> JarPackageFragmentRoot.computeChildren
-> Util.getEntryName -> WindowsPath.normalize          <-- per entry

Same stack family observed at 15s / 35s / 2.7s in other triggers
(Ctrl+hover, completion) — always the same eager initialization.

Expected: package-name cache built lazily/incrementally (or off the UI thread);
path normalization batched.

Related: Issue 1 (jdt.ui) — same "first SearchableEnvironment" cost center.

The UI froze when the caret was put in a constructor in a Java editor while a long build was running. The thread dump below was taken while it was frozen.

Seen with Eclipse 2026-09 (4.41, `org.eclipse.jdt.ui` 3.39.0) on Windows, Java 25.0.1. The code is the same on master.

### Thread dump

The UI thread waits for the shared AST of the active editor:

```
"main" TIMED_WAITING (on object monitor)
	at java.lang.Object.wait0(Native Method)
	at java.lang.Object.wait(Object.java:389)
	at org.eclipse.jdt.core.manipulation.CoreASTProvider.getAST(CoreASTProvider.java:176)
	at org.eclipse.jdt.core.manipulation.CoreASTProvider.getAST(CoreASTProvider.java:189)
	[... 64 more frames of CoreASTProvider.getAST(CoreASTProvider.java:189) ...]
	at org.eclipse.jdt.core.manipulation.SharedASTProviderCore.getAST(SharedASTProviderCore.java:138)
	at org.eclipse.jdt.internal.corext.refactoring.RefactoringAvailabilityTesterCore.isCanonicalConstructor(RefactoringAvailabilityTesterCore.java:313)
	at org.eclipse.jdt.internal.corext.refactoring.RefactoringAvailabilityTester.isCanonicalConstructor(RefactoringAvailabilityTester.java:169)
	at org.eclipse.jdt.internal.corext.refactoring.RefactoringAvailabilityTester.isIntroduceParameterObjectAvailable(RefactoringAvailabilityTester.java:902)
	at org.eclipse.jdt.internal.ui.actions.IntroduceParameterObjectAction.selectionChanged(IntroduceParameterObjectAction.java:74)
	at org.eclipse.jdt.ui.actions.SelectionDispatchAction.dispatchSelectionChanged(SelectionDispatchAction.java:262)
	at org.eclipse.jdt.ui.actions.SelectionDispatchAction.selectionChanged(SelectionDispatchAction.java:257)
	at org.eclipse.jface.viewers.Viewer$1.run(Viewer.java:151)
	at org.eclipse.core.runtime.SafeRunner.run(SafeRunner.java:47)
	at org.eclipse.ui.internal.JFaceUtil$$Lambda/0x00000000151e9000.run(Unknown Source)
	at org.eclipse.jface.util.SafeRunnable.run(SafeRunnable.java:169)
	at org.eclipse.jface.viewers.Viewer.fireSelectionChanged(Viewer.java:148)
	at org.eclipse.jface.viewers.StructuredViewer.updateSelection(StructuredViewer.java:2133)
	at org.eclipse.jface.viewers.ColumnViewer.updateSelection(ColumnViewer.java:1044)
	at org.eclipse.jface.viewers.StructuredViewer.setSelection(StructuredViewer.java:1668)
	at org.eclipse.jface.viewers.TreeViewer.setSelection(TreeViewer.java:1093)
	at org.eclipse.jdt.internal.ui.javaeditor.JavaOutlinePage.select(JavaOutlinePage.java:1133)
	at org.eclipse.jdt.internal.ui.javaeditor.JavaEditor.synchronizeOutlinePage(JavaEditor.java:2173)
	at org.eclipse.jdt.internal.ui.javaeditor.JavaEditor.synchronizeOutlinePage(JavaEditor.java:2161)
	at org.eclipse.jdt.internal.ui.javaeditor.JavaEditor.selectionChanged(JavaEditor.java:2272)
	at org.eclipse.jdt.internal.ui.javaeditor.JavaEditor$EditorSelectionChangedListener.selectionChanged(JavaEditor.java:314)
	at org.eclipse.jface.text.TextViewer.firePostSelectionChanged(TextViewer.java:2808)
	at org.eclipse.jface.text.TextViewer.firePostSelectionChanged(TextViewer.java:2738)
	at org.eclipse.jface.text.TextViewer.postSelectionChanged(TextViewer.java:2721)
	at org.eclipse.jface.text.TextViewer$$Lambda/0x00000000159abc78.run(Unknown Source)
	at org.eclipse.jface.util.Throttler.lambda$0(Throttler.java:66)
	at org.eclipse.jface.util.Throttler$$Lambda/0x00000000155858e0.run(Unknown Source)
	at org.eclipse.jface.util.Throttler.lambda$1(Throttler.java:79)
	at org.eclipse.jface.util.Throttler$$Lambda/0x0000000015585b10.run(Unknown Source)
	at org.eclipse.swt.widgets.RunnableLock.run(RunnableLock.java:40)
	at org.eclipse.swt.widgets.Synchronizer.runAsyncMessages(Synchronizer.java:131)
	at org.eclipse.swt.widgets.Display.runAsyncMessages(Display.java:4136)
	at org.eclipse.swt.widgets.Display.readAndDispatch(Display.java:3752)
```

In the same dump:

- the wait was woken up 65 times and started again each time (the recursive `getAST` frames);
- the four `JavaReconciler` threads are idle in `AbstractReconciler.delay`: nothing is computing the AST;
- the auto build is running a full build of a project (`BatchImageBuilder`, for 17 minutes);
- two jobs wait at the same place, which does not block the UI: "Requesting Java AST from selection" (`SelectionListenerWithASTManager`) and "Decoration Calculation" (`OverrideIndicatorLabelDecorator`).

### Analysis

`IntroduceParameterObjectAction.selectionChanged(IStructuredSelection)` runs in the UI thread each time the selection of the Outline follows the caret. When the selected element is a constructor, `RefactoringAvailabilityTesterCore.isCanonicalConstructor` calls `SharedASTProviderCore.getAST(cu, WAIT_YES, null)` to ask its binding whether it is a canonical constructor.

For the active editor, `CoreASTProvider.getAST` waits while a reconcile is announced and no AST is cached. It is woken up by each `aboutToBeReconciled` and `reconciled`, and waits again if there is still no AST.

What I think keeps it waiting, which the dump alone does not prove: during a long build the workspace sends resource change notifications from time to time (`NotificationManager`, no more often than every 1.5 s). On a Java model change or a marker change, the `JavaReconciler` of the active editor calls `forceReconciling()`, which cancels the reconcile that is running, announces a new one (`CoreASTProvider.aboutToBeReconciled` drops the AST) and starts its delay again. When a reconcile of the file takes longer than the time between two notifications, the AST is never available until the build ends.

This is the stack of #2323, where it showed as delays of a few seconds. That issue was closed with the change of the priority of the job, and the wait in the UI thread is still there.

### Proposal

Whatever makes the AST late, a selection listener should not wait for it in the UI thread. A canonical constructor can be told from the Java model, without the AST: it is the constructor of a record whose parameter types have the erasures of the types of the record components. I will open a PR for this.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a JUnit launch configuration for a test class of a project with many libraries.
2. Restart Eclipse, or close and reopen the project.
3. Open *Run > Run Configurations...* with this configuration selected.

The UI freezes for a second or more (1.9 s here, on Windows, Java 25), before the dialog shows.

### Thread dump of the UI thread

body_text:
Environment: Eclipse 2026-09 (4.41.0.20260903-0719), Windows Server 2025,
JDK 27; debuggee is Spring Boot 4.1 with virtual threads (enabled by
default), sustained thread churn (scheduled tasks suffice — no external
traffic required).

Symptom: repeated UI freezes (2-30s+, cyclic, CPU only 1-3% during freeze).
Captured deadlock pair in .metadata/.log (2026-09-17/18):

main: TreeModelContentProvider.updateNodes (recursive x3)
 -> TreeViewer.replace/setChildCount -> OS.SendMessage (SWT tree surgery)
'Text Viewer Hover Presenter': Display.syncExec() cancelled waiting for the
UI lock

Still reproducible on 4.41 as of 2026-09-24 (monitoring sample attached).

Triggered by thread start/death events while a debug session is active,
even when the user is not interacting.

Workarounds (verified): uncheck Show Running Threads / Thread Groups /
Virtual Threads / Monitors in the Debug view menu, or close the Debug view,
or run without the debugger.

Related:
- eclipse-jdt/eclipse.jdt.debug#602 (virtual threads 1000x slower under
  the debugger)
- eclipse-jdt/eclipse.jdt.debug#296 (virtual thread presentation in Debug
  view — same component)
- eclipse-jdt/eclipse.jdt.debug#351 (same component, same stack shape:
  TreeModelContentProvider.handleAdd; closed as not planned)

Note: this issue is against the Debug view implementation
(org.eclipse.debug.ui, TreeModelContentProvider); the jdt.debug tickets
above are referenced as the same-family history in the debugger area.

Attached: raw monitoring samples (deadlock pair 2026-09-17, recurrence
2026-09-24).

body_text:
With a large workspace (tens of thousands of markers), any marker change
triggers ExtendedMarkersView.updateTitle -> Markers.getMarkerCounts, which
iterates ALL markers; each Marker.getAttribute() performs a workspace
ElementTree traversal. Durations escalated over 2 days: 2.4s -> 17s (BLOCKED on
marker lock) -> 36s.

Samples:
Markers.getMarkerCounts -> Marker.getAttribute -> MarkerManager.findMarkerInfo
-> Workspace.getResourceInfo -> ElementTree.getElementData

Also: editor caret movement triggers ExtendedMarkersView.setSelection ->
Markers.getMarkerItem (BLOCKED 17s) waiting on the same marker model lock.

Expected: incremental counts or caching; selection lookup should not contend
with bulk counting.

(search "Problems view slow" / "getMarkerCounts" first and add samples if an
open issue exists)

If you're not comfortable with this template for your particular report, feel free to erase it and write your report from scratch -->

Let's make sure issue is not already fixed in latest builds first.

- [ ] I verified I can reproduce this issue against [latest Integration Build of Eclipse SDK](https://download.eclipse.org/eclipse/downloads/)

## Steps to reproduce
This happens intermittently in our RCP app when we are closing and reopening an editor and annotating it. It seems to happen because in `AnnotationModel.getAnnotationIterator(boolean, boolean)` you first get the keySet iterator `Iterator<Object> it= fAttachments.keySet().iterator()` and then you iterate over the keys and get the value `fAttachments.get(it.next()).getAnnotationIterator()`. But if another thread removes an entry in the map in between, it will cause a NPE.

So a fix would be to simply iterate over the values directly, since we are not doing anything with the keys anyway (except getting the value).

I expected: *No Exception*

But got: *Null Pointer Exception*

## Here is some relevant log output
```
Exception in thread "Thread-80" java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "org.eclipse.jface.text.source.IAnnotationModel.getAnnotationIterator()" because the return value of "java.util.Map.get(Object)" is null
	at org.eclipse.jface.text.source.AnnotationModel.getAnnotationIterator(AnnotationModel.java:791)
	at org.eclipse.jface.text.source.AnnotationModel.getAnnotationIterator(AnnotationModel.java:712)
	at org.eclipse.jface.text.source.projection.ProjectionSummary.removeSummaries(ProjectionSummary.java:181)
	at org.eclipse.jface.text.source.projection.ProjectionSummary.internalUpdateSummaries(ProjectionSummary.java:159)
	at org.eclipse.jface.text.source.projection.ProjectionSummary$Summarizer.run(ProjectionSummary.java:75)
```

## Tested under this environment:
* OS & version: MacOS Tahoe 26.6.2
* Eclipse IDE/Platform version (as shown in *Help > About*): 2026-09 (4.41.0)

I will make a PR for this, thanks!

body_text:
Blending two `RGB` values by a ratio is implemented over a dozen times in platform.ui, each with its own parameter type and rounding.
Following the discussion in #4489, SWT now provides the shared helper: `RGB.blend(RGB other, double weight)` and `RGBA.blend(RGBA other, double weight)` (eclipse-platform/eclipse.platform.swt#3732, `@since 3.136`).
The weight is the share of `other`, from 0 (the receiver) to 1 (`other`), and channels are rounded to the nearest integer.

Work to do in platform.ui, once SWT 3.136 is in the target platform:

- Raise the `org.eclipse.swt` lower bound to 3.136 in each touched bundle's `MANIFEST.MF`.
- Replace the private copies with `RGB.blend`:

| Bundle | Copy | Replacement |
|---|---|---|
| jface | `PopupDialog.blend(bg, fg, factor)` | `bg.blend(fg, factor)` |
| jface.databinding | `SWTUtil.mix(rgb1, rgb2, ratio)` | `rgb2.blend(rgb1, ratio)` |
| jface.text | `Colors.blend(bg, fg, factor)`, projection `SourceViewerInformationControl.blend` | `bg.blend(fg, factor)` |
| jface.text | `OverviewRuler.interpolate(fg, bg, scale)`, `DiffPainter.interpolate` | `fg.blend(bg, scale)` |
| ui.editors | `SourceViewerInformationControl.blend(bg, fg, factor)` | `bg.blend(fg, factor)` |
| ui.workbench | `ShowViewDialog.blend(c1, c2, ratio)` | `c2.blend(c1, ratio / 100.0)` |
| ui.workbench | `HeapStatus.blend(fg, bg)` (40% foreground) | `bg.getRGB().blend(fg.getRGB(), 0.4)` |
| e4 renderers | `CTabRendering.blend(c1, c2, ratio)` | `c2.blend(c1, ratio / 100.0)` |

- Keep the public API and let it delegate: `FormColors.blend(c1, c2, ratio)` and `ColorUtil.blend(c1, c2, ratio)` become `c2.blend(c1, ratio / 100.0)`, and `ColorUtil.blend(val1, val2)` becomes `val1.blend(val2, 0.5)`.

The copies truncate while `RGB.blend` rounds, so a migrated color can differ by one per channel.
Tests that compare exact RGB values need adjusting rather than a rounding shim.

Copies in other repositories (Compare in eclipse.platform, JDT UI, PDE, GEF Classic's `FigureUtilities`) can follow the same way.

- Replace the private copies with `RGB.blend`:

|---|---|---|

| e4 renderers | `CTabRendering.blend(c1, c2, ratio)` | `c2.blend(c1, ratio / 100.0)` |

- Keep the public API and let it delegate: `FormColors.blend(c1, c2, ratio)` and `ColorUtil.blend(c1, c2, ratio)` become `c2.blend(c1, ratio / 100.0)`, and `ColorUtil.blend(val1, val2)` becomes `val1.blend(val2, 0.5)`.

<!-- Thanks for suggesting an enhancement! -->
<!-- The following template is highly recommended to trigger an efficient course of actions: it's pretty suitable if you're not familiar with the project as it will guide you in sharing the most important information. If you're not comfortable with this template for your particular report, feel free to erase it and write your report from scratch -->

Let's make sure issue is not already fixed in latest builds first.

- [x] I verified [latest Integration Build of Eclipse SDK](https://download.eclipse.org/eclipse/downloads/) doesn't provide the feature.

## Suggestion

The NotificationPopup (org.eclipse.jface.notifications) has some minor flaws, where some workarounds are necessary.

* The MIN_HEIGHT, MAX_WIDTH and PADDING_EDGE of the popup cannot be configured as desired, as it is hardcoded in the AbstractNotificationPopup.

To shrink the height of the popup, I needed to create a workaround like this:
```java
Point size = popup.getShell().getSize();
Point location = popup.getShell().getLocation();
popup.getShell().pack();
popup.getShell().setLocation(location.x, location.y + (size.y - popup.getShell().getSize().y));
```
It would be nice to have these options in the builder like this:

```java
NotificationPopup.forDisplay(Display.getDefault())
    .text("A problem occurred.")
    .title("Warning", true)
    .minHeight(0)
    .maxWidth(500)
    .paddingEdge(10)
    .open();
```

* The Popup does not follow its parent shell, when it is moved or resized. It would be nice to have an option for this when creating the popup (or maybe as default behavior)

The listener could look like this:
```java
    static void attachPopupFollower(Shell parentShell, Shell popupShell, int padding) {
        Listener moveListener = e -> {
            if (parentShell == null || parentShell.isDisposed()) {
                return;
            }
            if (popupShell == null || popupShell.isDisposed()) {
                return;
            }

            Rectangle clientArea = parentShell.getClientArea();
            Point clientOriginOnDisplay = parentShell.toDisplay(clientArea.x, clientArea.y);
            Point popupSize = popupShell.getSize();

            int x = clientOriginOnDisplay.x + clientArea.width - popupSize.x - padding; //use the configured paddingEdge here
            int y = clientOriginOnDisplay.y + clientArea.height - popupSize.y - padding;

            popupShell.setLocation(x, y);
        };

        parentShell.addListener(SWT.Move, moveListener);
        parentShell.addListener(SWT.Resize, moveListener);

        popupShell.addListener(SWT.Dispose, e -> {
            if (!parentShell.isDisposed()) {
                parentShell.removeListener(SWT.Move, moveListener);
                parentShell.removeListener(SWT.Resize, moveListener);
            }
        });
    }
```

I attached the whole example as a file here.

## Community

- [x] I understand suggesting an enhancement doesn't mandate anyone to implement it. Other contributors may consider this suggestion, or not, at their own convenience. The most efficient way to get it fixed is that I implement it myself and contribute it back as a good quality patch to the project.

The breadcrumb implementation currently used by the JDT Java editor contains
generic viewer infrastructure that is not specific to Java.

Move the reusable breadcrumb viewer implementation to
org.eclipse.jface.viewers and adapt JDT to use the JFace implementation.

The refactoring keeps JDT-specific behavior in JDT through extension hooks,
including:
- ProblemTreeViewer for the drop-down viewer
- Java-specific element openability semantics
- persistent dialog settings

The goal is to make the breadcrumb viewer reusable by other clients while
preserving the existing Java editor behavior.

The change spans eclipse.platform.ui and eclipse.jdt.ui and will be submitted
as coordinated pull requests.
